title: Happywhale sightings with an offset time zone are stored ~14 hours off; 582 show on the wrong day
description: derived.happywhale_occurrences computes observed_at as (start_date + start_time) AT TIME ZONE e.timezone. Happywhale reports some encounters' zone as a bare ISO 8601 offset ('-07:00', '-08:00', 'Z', '+02:00', ...). Postgres reads a bare offset given to AT TIME ZONE as a POSIX zone, whose sign is the reverse of ISO's: '-07:00' becomes seven hours EAST of Greenwich. Example: encounter 533338, reported 2025-02-23 13:01:38 at -07:00 (= 20:01:38Z), stored as 06:01:38Z, which is 22:01 the previous evening Pacific. Measured on production 2026-10-01: 945 Happywhale occurrences have an offset-form zone, and 582 of them appear on the map on a different Pacific day than the photographer reported; the rest are hours off on the right day. observed_until has the same fault. IANA names (America/Vancouver) and 'Z' are read correctly. Found while porting the view to DuckDB (salish-xv35.2), whose twin reproduces the fault on purpose so the agreement gate holds (scripts/read-path/derive/occurrences.sql, happywhale_instant). Fix: in Postgres, a migration that replaces the view so an offset is applied with ISO's sign (e.g. parse it, or rewrite '-07:00' to the POSIX form 'UTC+07:00' before AT TIME ZONE), ending with a refresh of the happywhale source per decision 055; in the same release, the DuckDB twin's happywhale_instant changes to match. Ship both together or the gate fails the read-path build in between (which is the gate working, but noisy).
close_reason: Fixed in #536 (31e571a), deployed 2026-10-01 03:2x UTC: derived.happywhale_instant reads a bare offset as an interval (ISO sign); the view uses it; the migration refreshed the happywhale source (945 rows changed, 582 moved day). The read-path twin changed in the same release; Fly redeployed; the agreement gate passes on 63,739 live occurrences; encounter 533338 now in days/2025-02-23.json at 20:01:38Z. Parity test pins Postgres vs the twin across zone forms and DST edges.

title: Key an occurrence's taxon on a register entity, and load register membership
description: The identity half of salish-53t, and the piece two other issues wait on. (1) scripts/register/load.ts loads membership (or dist/ancestor.tsv) alongside entities, names and mappings, so SQL can walk J pod -> Southern Resident -> Resident -> Orcinus orca. (2) public.occurrences can build its taxon from a register entity rather than only from inaturalist.taxa -- iNat-keyed sources keep reaching a register entity through the skos:exactMatch crosswalk. Needs salish-0gb.2/.3 first or alongside: 8.5% of occurrences (almost all subspecies) have no register taxon to key on until the ecotypes are crosswalked to iNaturalist's two killer-whale subspecies. Not decided yet: Peter leans towards growing a taxonomic_parent relation in the register for HIERARCHY (proposed shape: a script-generated excerpt of NCBI's lineage in NCBI's namespace, not curated and minting no SSA identifiers); that is a separate, register-side question and does not gate this.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-21 to the part-2 measurement above: the six taxa absent from classification.tsv split as FOUR subspecies (Orcinus orca ater 4,707; O. o. rectipinnus 222; Phoca vitulina richardii 20; Eumetopias jubatus monteriensis 2) and TWO taxa with no register entity at all (Eubalaena 3; Delphinapterus leucas 1). An earlier note said 'the first four are subspecies', which in that listing order wrongly included Eubalaena — a genus, not a subspecies. The subspecies resolve via their species; the two strays need the iNaturalist walk retained.

ALSO: the join from dwc.occurrences to dwc.taxa_classification is INNER, not LEFT. A missing classification row does not blank the columns, it DROPS THE OCCURRENCE from the archive. So the naive cutover would have removed 4,955 of 20,952 records rather than leaving them unclassified, and produced a smaller archive that passed every check we have.

AND a finding that corrects the 'byte-identical' claim: of 513 rows, 511 are identical and 2 differ. Kogia breviceps and Kogia sima — NCBI says family Physeteridae, iNaturalist and the SMM list say Kogiidae. 0 exported rows and no Kogia anywhere in the corpus, so the effect is latent, not live. Accepted per decision 047 rather than corrected in SQL, because correcting NCBI here would mint a third opinion in the export.
close_reason:
Both halves shipped 2026-09-21. Part 1 PR #478 (3c32841): register.membership, register.ancestor, register.deprecations loaded — the first dist/ artefacts this loader reads — plus register.taxon_entity_for() and register.taxon_for(). Total: 773 of 773 entities resolve to a taxon. Part 2 PR #479 (f68afb6): dwc.taxa_classification reads the register's NCBI excerpt for phylum..genus, keeping iNaturalist's Animalia for kingdom (decision 047).

salish-8vr.26 is unblocked: register.taxon_for('SSA:0000020') returns ('Orcinus orca','Killer whale',41521,'SSA:0000900'), which is the taxon a bout branch needs.

WHAT THE NEXT PERSON SHOULD KNOW. (1) taxon_for stops at the SPECIES and walks past the ecotype, deliberately — an ecotype is kind='group', ADR-0008 refuses it taxonomic standing, and keying species_id on rectipinnus would stop a Bigg's bout ever chaining with a sighting recorded as plain Orcinus orca (src/segments.ts splits tracks on that field). The ecotype reaches the map through the label. Revisiting that is a decision about salish-8vr.26's branch, not a tweak to the function. (2) The join from dwc.occurrences to taxa_classification is INNER: a missing classification row drops the occurrence from the archive rather than leaving it unclassified. The iNaturalist fallback is load-bearing, not defensive. (3) Part 2 changed no output — 511 of 513 rows byte-identical, 0 exported rows affected. It bought provenance, not accuracy; decision 047 says so explicitly so nobody merges a follow-up expecting the archive to improve.

title: [epic] Taxon identity and hierarchy still belong to iNaturalist; only names moved to the register
description:
RAISED BY Peter 2026-09-20: 'It sounds like we need to formally shift off of inaturalist for our authoritative taxonomy. Perhaps this was missed during planning.' It was. salish-ayb moved NAMES to the register (decision 033) and deferred the individual catalogue to salish-ox2; neither epic covers which taxon key a row holds or how a record rolls up to a species. It stayed invisible because every source so far arrives with an iNaturalist taxon or a scientific name. Orcasound bouts (salish-8vr.25) are the first source whose identity is a register entity with no iNaturalist taxon behind it -- 'J pod' has no iNat id.

NOT YET DECIDED. This epic holds the inventory so the decision can be made against facts. The decision record is Peter's to make and is not written.

INVENTORY (codebase sweep 2026-09-20)
NAMES -- moved: vernacular_name on all four public.occurrences branches via register.inaturalist_taxon_name; SHORT_MAP_FORMS keyed on SSA:. Residue: the 8.5% iNat-vernacular fallback (almost all subspecies) and SUBSPECIES_FORMS in src/symbology.ts:171 -- that residue is salish-0gb.
IDENTITY -- entirely iNat: FK columns inaturalist.observations.taxon_id, maplify.sightings.taxon_id, public.observations.taxon_id, public.individuals.taxon_id (DEFAULT 41521), inaturalist.taxa.current_taxon_id. upsert_observation resolves the form's scientific-name string to an iNat integer; no register identifier is stored on a native row. src/individual-page.ts:18 has a raw iNat id in the client. The register is today a name overlay KEYED ON iNat ids.
HIERARCHY -- entirely iNat, and the register has no equivalent: inaturalist.species_id() (rank + parent_id rollup; src/segments.ts:85 chains tracks on it), dwc.taxa_classification (recursive parent_id walk producing every DwC-A rank/kingdom..genus column), public.haulout_occurrences (parent_id walk from Phocidae/Otariidae to define 'pinniped'), ingest scope filter on ancestor_ids.
RETIRED-TAXON RESOLUTION (decision 032, current_taxon_id) is an iNat-identity concern every read path depends on.

WHAT THE REGISTER CAN AND CANNOT OFFER (animals main, edition 2026.09.1)
Can: 40 kind=taxon entities as stable identifiers, 39 with skos:exactMatch to the iNat id our rows hold; social rollup J pod -> Southern Resident -> Resident -> Orcinus orca (membership -- NOT loaded here yet; load.ts reads entities, names, mappings only).
Cannot, by design: taxonomic hierarchy. Zero taxon->taxon edges, no rank on taxa. ADR-0008: subsumption is not membership; the register is 'a forest, one tree per species'; species authority is delegated to NCBI; iNaturalist is 'deliberately not the taxonomic authority', only a crosswalk. ADR-0008 names a separate taxonomic_parent relation as the honest route if a backbone is ever wanted, and warns it means maintaining one.

SO THE QUESTION IS TWO QUESTIONS. Identity can move to the register's taxon entities. Hierarchy cannot move there as the register stands; but with ~40 taxa the hierarchy consumers are few and enumerable (four, above), and each could be answered by a small explicit set rather than a tree.

DEPENDS ON / RELATED: salish-0gb.2 and .3 (closeMatch the two ecotypes to iNat's subspecies -- unblocked now that Q1 is released in 2026.09.1; without it 8.5% of occurrences have no register taxon to key on). salish-8vr.25 needs the identity half. salish-ox2.5 needs register membership loaded, which is the same loader change.
notes:
2026-09-22: the individual-profile slice of the inventory above is now DONE (PR #480), so two lines of that inventory are stale:

- "public.individuals.taxon_id (DEFAULT 41521)" -- the column is DROPPED, with its FK into inaturalist.taxa. Every individual's taxon now comes from register.taxon_for(entity_id).
- "src/individual-page.ts:18 has a raw iNat id in the client" -- TAXON_LABELS is deleted, and the page reads public.animal_names.

What the inventory still gets right: identity is STORED on iNaturalist keys for public.observations (our own submissions, via upsert_observation resolving a name string to an iNat integer) and for the Maplify ingest (which joins inaturalist.taxa by scientific name purely as a dictionary). Those two are salish-53t.3.

The mirror columns -- inaturalist.observations.taxon_id, inaturalist.taxa.current_taxon_id -- are decision 008 working as intended and are not defects. The original inventory listed them beside the others, which conflates "we hold a foreign key in our own data" with "a mirror mirrors".
close_reason: All three children done 2026-09-22 (53t.1 read path, 53t.2 DwC classification from the register, 53t.3 our sightings + Maplify keyed on register entities; decisions 047, 048, 049). Taxon identity now comes from the register everywhere except the iNaturalist mirror itself (decision 008) and the dormant HappyWhale branch (salish-vax, P3).

title: Occurrences gain an end time; Orcasound bouts get tables in our own shape
description:
DIRECTION (Peter, 2026-09-20): orcasite is our project, so ideally it needs no anti-corruption layer. Fix the shape at the source and read it directly, the way decision 033 treats the register -- no orcasound mirror schema, no translation SQL. This departs from decision 013 (mirror verbatim into an orcasound schema, translate at the boundary) and carves orcasite out of decision 008; 013 needs an amendment BEFORE this is built, and it is genuinely a salishsea-io decision. Not yet written -- the storage shape and the time-range question below are open.

ORDER OF WORK
1. orcasite#1013 (salish-8vr.7): kind + nullable unique iri on tags, exposed on the JSON:API tag type. Accepted by the team in conversation.
2. orcasite#1016 (salish-8vr.15), animal slice only: 16 tags. Measured 2026-09-20 against the live API (221 bouts, 155 biophony, 94 tags) using the register fold: 15 tags name exactly one entity (220 applications: KW, SRKW, J, K, L, Bigg's, humpback, CA sea lion, seagull, T419/T420/T421, T38C, T34s, T090s); T37 is ambiguous (matriline T037s or whale T037) and needs a person; 78 name no animal, correctly (call types, vessels, snr notes, false-positive). 92 of 155 biophony bouts carry at least one animal tag.
3. Here: table + ingest + a fifth branch in public.occurrences.

WHAT THE CODEBASE SURVEY FOUND (2026-09-20)
- Ingest is pg_cron + pg_net -> the 'ingest' Edge Function (supabase/functions/ingest/index.ts, z.enum of sources), pure core in scripts/ingest/*.ts. ingest.runs has CHECK (source IN ('maplify','inaturalist')); scripts/ingest/heartbeat.ts has SOURCES. Both need 'orcasound'.
- public.occurrences is a UNION ALL view, 22 columns, latest definition supabase/migrations/20260829020000_resolve_retired_taxa_on_read.sql:76. A new branch means rewriting the whole view. taxon already carries entity_id; identifiers column exists.
- collections already has ('orcasound','Orcasound','acoustic_feed'). providers has NO orcasound row.
- Time is an instant everywhere (observed_at). A bout is a range: median 14 min, max 2.9 h. HappyWhale's mirror has start/end and the view collapses it. OPEN: add an end column to the view, or collapse to start_time.
- API: /api/json/bouts?include=feed,tags, page[limit] max 250, follow links.next. feed.location_point is GeoJSON lon/lat. No open-ended bouts today.
- dwc.occurrences is also per-source; needs an explicit include/exclude call (decision 005 excludes iNat/HappyWhale).
- A new public.* readable relation must be added to supabase/read-grants.test.ts.

STILL OPEN AND NOT ORCASITE'S: salish-8vr.4 (the 63 biophony bouts with no animal tag -- occurrence with zero identifications? -- and certainty vs our identifications.status).
notes:
DECIDED by Peter 2026-09-20 (to be written into the decision 013 amendment, since both are this project's calls): (1) Occurrence END TIME: yes -- add it to the public.occurrences view, null for every existing source. Eventually it may also be offered on the sighting reporting form, so model it as a property of occurrences generally, not as an acoustic special case. (2) DwC-A: WITHHOLD bouts from the export until this integration is working well end to end and we like how it looks. Revisit then; not a permanent exclusion.
2026-09-20: BLOCKING DESIGN DEPENDENCY found while scoping the view branch -- every branch of public.occurrences builds its taxon from inaturalist.taxa; the register only overlays a name. A bout tagged 'J pod' (SSA:0000020) has no iNat taxon, so a bout branch needs (a) register membership loaded here, to walk J pod -> Orcinus orca, and (b) the view able to key a taxon on a register entity. That is the identity half of epic salish-53t. The end-time column and the bout table do not depend on it.
2026-09-20: scope narrowed to what did not wait on taxon identity -- observed_until and the two tables. The ingest and the view branch moved to salish-8vr.26, which depends on salish-53t.1 (identity half of salish-53t). The orcasite dependencies moved with them.
close_reason: salishsea-io#476 merged 2026-09-20 as 6e21aa6 and verified in production: migrations through 20260920210000 applied; public.occurrences has observed_until (1,468 of 5,601 HappyWhale encounters carry one, none ending at or before their start; every other source NULL); acoustic_bouts and acoustic_bout_entities exist, empty, with no anon/authenticated read privilege; 'orcasound' provider row present; both dependent matviews still populated; smoke green. NOTE the PR body's '5,069 have an end time' overstated it -- 3,589 of those have end = start, i.e. an instant; corrected in a PR comment. The ingest and the view branch are salish-8vr.26.

title: iNaturalist reconcile deleted every evening's observations: UTC delete bound vs local-date fetch
description: scripts/ingest/persist.ts bounded the reconcile DELETE by observed_at (UTC instant) in [start, end+1), while iNat's d1/d2 filter on the observer's LOCAL date. An observation at 6 pm Pacific the day before a window's start is dated the previous day by iNat (not fetched) but sits at 01:00 UTC on start (inside the bound) — so reconcile deleted it. Measured in prod 2026-09-11: since the edge-function cutover (2026-06-26) every day's 00–08 UTC slice is empty once it ages out of the rolling window (0 rows/day vs 5–24 inside the window and before June 26); ~10 rows/day lost, ~800 in all, plus 4–9 rows at each of July's manual backfill month boundaries and one 1969-12-31 row in today's history backfill (run 38708). Fix: reconcile only the window's interior [start+1, end) in UTC — no straddle for any zone; edge days are covered by the rolling window's next tick. Recovery: after deploy, re-run windows 2026-06-15..today through scripts/backfill/inat-history.ts (pure upsert restores the deleted rows), then the history backfill (decision 041).
close_reason: Fix deployed in PR #455 (4b4dee1); recovery walk 2026-06-15..2026-09-18 run 2026-09-18 (runs 42740-42743): 2103 rows upserted, 17 interior deletions reconciling upstream removals. Verified: the 00-08 UTC slice is 20-22% of each month Jun-Sep, matching May's 19% baseline; it was empty for aged-out days after the 2026-06-26 cutover.

title: Visitors' reads (the map, the calendar) time out in production when the database is busy
description:
Someone opens salishsea.io, the day's sightings never arrive, and they get "Couldn't load sightings. The list may be incomplete." over an empty map. Postgres killed the query at the statement timeout.

Twice in production so far, both on 2026-08-31/09-01, different people (Bothell, Oceanside), sampled at 100%: SALISHSEA-IO-3D (https://beam-reach.sentry.io/issues/SALISHSEA-IO-3D) and SALISHSEA-IO-3G (https://beam-reach.sentry.io/issues/SALISHSEA-IO-3G). Same error, `PostgrestError: canceling statement due to statement timeout`; two issue groups only because the minified frames differ. These are the only two of the thirteen open Sentry issues on 2026-09-09 that are about our own code failing — everything else was third-party noise or a self-healing ingest tick.

The query is `fetchOccurrences` in src/salish-sea.ts: select from the `occurrences` *view*, `observed_at` inside one PST8PDT day, and when a region is selected four more predicates on `location->lon` / `location->lat`. `location` is a composite (`lon_lat`), and `->` on a composite field is an expression — so unless there is an expression index to match, those four bounds are a filter applied after rows are materialised, on top of whatever the view costs to assemble.

Two things make this worse than the raw count suggests. The failure is *silent by design* short of the toast: an empty sighting list is indistinguishable from a quiet day on the water, which is exactly the case decision 031 introduced `persist` for. And we only hear about it at all because 031 wired `reportError` into this path — so the two events are a floor, not a census, and we have no idea how long this predates 2026-08-31.

First step is an EXPLAIN against prod for a busy day with a region selected, to find out whether the cost is the view or the unindexed bbox predicates. salish-b0v ("Add missing indexes on FK/JOIN columns used by the export and live map views") is adjacent and may cover part of it, but it is scoped to the export; this is the live map's own path and the one a visitor waits on.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text:
Measured against prod, 2026-09-09. The query is not slow — it is fast and occasionally collides with something.

A busy day (2026-08-30) with a region selected, the exact shape fetchOccurrences sends: **50ms execution, 16ms planning, 69 rows**. Against a 3s budget that is 60x headroom. The planner does use an expression index — `sightings_observed_at_gmt` on `(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'GMT')` — so the day range prunes before the expensive per-row work. The bbox bounds are a post-filter as suspected, but by then there are 32 rows to filter, so they cost nothing. My "unindexed bbox predicates" guess in the description was wrong.

Timeout budgets: `anon` is **statement_timeout=3s**, `authenticated` 8s. So a signed-out visitor — most visitors — has 3 seconds, and normally uses 50ms of it.

What actually competes: two materialized views refresh every 5 minutes on the same tick (`1-59/5`), and **both fully scan `public.occurrences`** — `refresh-occurrence-index` (`SELECT id, observed_at, location FROM public.occurrences`) and `refresh-identifier-candidates` (`FROM public.occurrences o CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(o.identifiers)`). Over the last 24h, 288 runs each, averaging 8.0s and 7.0s, max 22.1s and 19.9s. So ~5% of wall-clock is spent scanning the whole dataset twice over, on the instance the map shares, churning the buffer cache each time.

SALISHSEA-IO-3G lands squarely inside one of those windows. The Sentry event is 2026-09-01 00:31:28.5; `refresh-occurrence-index` ran 00:31:00.3 → 00:31:34.0 that tick, and `refresh-identifier-candidates` 00:31:00.3 → 00:31:26.7. Both far above their averages — 33.7s and 26.4s, roughly 4x. The visitor's query started inside the heaviest refresh of the day and never got 3 seconds of the database's attention.

SALISHSEA-IO-3D does **not** fit. It fired 2026-08-31 19:25:06; the surrounding refreshes ran 19:21:00→19:21:10 and 19:26:00→19:26:08, so it fell in a quiet gap, and even allowing 3s of timeout before capture it started around 19:25:02. Refresh contention is therefore not the whole story, and one correlation out of two is not a diagnosis. Something else made that one slow.

Consequence for the fix: this does not want a cheaper query or a fallback query — at 50ms there is nothing to optimise on the read path. It wants the contention removed. The cheapest lever is the refresh schedule, and the migration that introduced `occurrence_index` already says its ~6-minute lag is "immaterial in practice", which is an argument its 5-minute cadence has to answer. Doing the expensive scan twice on the same tick, rather than once shared, is the other obvious waste.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: PR #434 (https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/pull/434) takes the schedule half: refresh-identifier-candidates moves from the :01 tick to :03 so the two caches stop scanning public.occurrences simultaneously. Explains SALISHSEA-IO-3G, not SALISHSEA-IO-3D — this issue stays open for 3D and for the structural half (give occurrence_index an identifiers column; build candidates FROM occurrence_index so the expensive scan runs once per tick, not twice). 🤖

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: PR #434 now also carries a regression guard: supabase/refresh-schedules.test.ts asserts no two matview refreshes fire on the same minute. It compares expanded firing minutes rather than schedule strings — a step of five and a step of ten are different text sharing every tenth minute, so string comparison could pass while the caches collided (CodeRabbit caught that; my first version had the flaw). Verified both ways against the local stack. Full suite 597/48 with SUPABASE_DB_URL. 🤖

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text:
SALISHSEA-IO-3D explained, 2026-09-10. The visitor did not lose a race with a matview refresh. They lost one with the ingest tick, and our own client made it a stampede.

The trace (ba4f989b387c4a9b9e1cf1a5fd42923e) shows the page loaded fine at 19:24:59 — two occurrence queries at ~300ms. Then at 19:25:00 pg_cron kicked the ingest; the maplify run wrote 201 rows to maplify.sightings from 19:25:01.2 to 19:25:04.0 (ingest.runs 32409). At 19:25:02.47 the browser fired two more identical occurrence queries at once, both timed out at ~3.9s; at 19:25:03.95 two more, 2.5s and 2.4s, succeeded. Four unprompted refetches, in two pairs, inside the ingest write.

Why four: the statement-level trigger on maplify.sightings and inaturalist.observations calls realtime.send on every INSERT and DELETE statement, and the ingest issues two of each per tick — realtime.messages shows exactly 4 broadcasts on every :x0/:x5 minute today. salish-sea.ts refetches on every broadcast. So every open tab runs the map query four times per tick, at the exact moment the writer is busiest, on an instance with shared_buffers 224MB, work_mem 2MB and one parallel worker. The maplify upsert has no change guard (scripts/ingest/persist.ts ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, unlike the inaturalist one which checks updated_at), so the trigger fires even when nothing changed: 864k updates on a 27k-row table, and observation_photos has 4.2M on 45k rows.

Ruled out: a plan flip. Under force_generic_plan the map query still uses the observed_at index (cost 378, 63 rows). The query is fine; pg_stat_statements has it at 8,240 calls, mean 19ms, max 663ms — but note cancelled statements never land there, so the max is the max of the survivors.

Not measurable after the fact: how many tabs were open at 19:25 (CloudFront shows ~5 page loads/min that hour and a 46-IP burst at 19:16, but the SPA keeps tabs alive for hours) and CPU/IO on the instance (Supabase's infra reports don't reach back 10 days; postgres_logs retention here is about an hour). Both are why the two Sentry events are a floor.

So both events have the same shape: a background job saturates a small instance, and the map's 3s budget is what breaks. #434 staggered the refreshes; the remaining levers are (1) stop broadcasting no-op writes — guard the maplify upsert and the deletes, or make the trigger conditional on rows affected; (2) stop refetching four times per broadcast — debounce in the client, or send one message per ingest run; (3) precompute: the view runs extract_identifiers, extract_travel_direction, species_id and st_x/st_y per row on every read and both matviews recompute all 49k rows every 5 minutes when ~200 change. A maintained occurrences table updated incrementally by the ingest would make the map read a plain indexed table and retire both refreshes. 🤖

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: PR #446 (https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/pull/446) takes the broadcast half: row-level triggers with a once-per-transaction flag, change guards on the maplify and photo upserts, and a 3–8s jittered coalesce in the client. Explains and addresses SALISHSEA-IO-3D. The structural half (a maintained occurrences table) is filed as salish-4h3. 🤖

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: Verified in production, 2026-09-10 18:00 UTC. Migration 20260910120000 applied; all four triggers row-level with the no-op guard. Broadcasts per ingest tick: 4, 4, 4, 4 before the deploy (17:25–17:40), then 0 at 17:45, 1 at 17:50 (an iNaturalist observation changed: one write transaction, one broadcast), 0 at 17:55 and 18:00. Maplify rows_upserted went from 199 a tick to 0 on quiet ticks. Nothing left on this issue except waiting to see whether the timeout recurs; the structural half is salish-4h3. 🤖

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text:
It recurred, 2026-09-14, and this time it was the calendar, not the map. Three visitors, 17:33:43 / 17:36:06 / 17:36:06 UTC, each a fresh page load whose occurrence_days RPC hit anon's 3s timeout (3.6-4.6s). Sentry files them under SALISHSEA-IO-37 (https://beam-reach.sentry.io/issues/SALISHSEA-IO-37), which is mostly unrelated 'Load failed' network errors and is archived until escalating -- which is why this went unseen for 8 days. Search 'statement timeout' across issues, not the xfo issue groups.

Neither fixed cause explains it. No deploy or migration that day; both ingest runs at 17:30 and 17:35 upserted 0 rows (so no broadcast refetch); traffic was ~45 page loads/hour, no burst. The 17:36 pair overlaps an 11.3s refresh-occurrence-index (17:36:00-17:36:11); the 17:33 one falls in a gap after refresh-identifier-candidates finished at 17:33:05. In the same page loads designations and social_groups -- trivial tables -- took up to 2.3s, so the instance as a whole was slow for those minutes.

The difference from the map query is weight. pg_stat_statements since 2026-08-28: the map's occurrences read, 10,118 calls, mean 20ms; occurrence_days, 1,945 calls, mean 445ms, max 2,742ms, stddev 432 -- and cancelled calls never land there, so the max is of survivors. EXPLAIN ANALYZE in prod for the failing request (2026-08-30..2026-10-10, bbox -126,47,-122,50.5): 135ms warm, shared hit=19,536 buffers, ~150MB, against shared_buffers of 224MB. One calendar render touches two-thirds of the cache, so it is fast only when nothing else is competing, and it is the first thing to cross 3s when anything is.

Levers, none chosen: (a) read occurrence_index, measured at 28ms / 731 buffers in 20260803000000, rejected then because it lags ingest by up to ~6min and decision 021 wants a contributor's own sighting to move their circle immediately -- a union of occurrence_index with the not-yet-indexed tail would keep that; (b) salish-4h3's maintained occurrences table, which makes both reads plain indexed scans and retires the refreshes; (c) a client retry on timeout for the calendar, which is cosmetic but cheap (the calendar already degrades to a bare date picker on error). 🤖

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: PR #481 (https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/pull/481) deployed 2026-09-22, migration 20260922030000 applied. The failing request (2026-08-30..2026-10-10, bbox -126,47,-122,50.5) in prod now: 75-81ms and 6,125 buffers per call, was 135ms warm and 19,536. Of the 6,125, 2,651 are the body (961 index half via the new occurrence_index_observed_at, 1,687 live 48h half) -- measured as a generic prepared plan; the rest is the SQL function re-planning the occurrences view each call, which reads the catalog, not the sighting pages that were being evicted. anon can call it (sum 1,218). Issue stays open to watch for recurrence; search Sentry for 'statement timeout' across all issues, since SALISHSEA-IO-37 hides it among network errors. 🤖

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: Title updated 2026-09-22. The original description's two suspicions are superseded by the comments below and should be read as history: the bbox predicates are NOT the cost (measured 2026-09-09, 50ms), and it is NOT map-only -- the 2026-09-14 recurrence was the calendar's occurrence_days. Established causes: background work saturating a small instance (co-scheduled matview refreshes, fixed #434; per-statement broadcast refetch stampede, fixed #446) and one heavy read, occurrence_days (fixed #481). Structural remedy remains salish-4h3. 🤖

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: The two five-minute matview refreshes this issue kept losing to are gone as of #501 (decision 055, deployed 2026-09-28): occurrences are stored and maintained per write; a full rebuild runs only when reference data changes (~3x/day, ~18s on prod). Worth watching Sentry for statement timeouts a few days before closing.

title: Automated backups of production data — there are none today
description:
Verified 2026-08-30 via the Supabase Management API: the project (grztmjpzamcxlzecmqca) is in the Beam Reach org on the FREE plan — pitr_enabled: false, backups: [], no add-ons. Free tier takes no daily backups; Pro gives 7 days, PITR is an add-on beyond that. No workflow or script in the repo runs pg_dump. The nightly DwC-A on s3://salishsea-io/site/dwca/ is a ~3 MB projection of dwc.occurrences only, overwritten nightly on a bucket with no versioning. docs/design-notes/dwca-attribution-pitfalls.md assumes 'restore from Supabase PITR' as a mitigation; that assumption is false.

What is re-fetchable: maplify.sightings (40,792) and inaturalist.observations (21,951) — the upstream APIs still serve history. What is NOT recoverable from anywhere: 501 native public.observations, 510 individuals + 133 social_groups (the catalogue, now carrying register ids), 36 auth.users, 95 storage.objects (user photos), the provenance/collection reference tables. Whole DB is 166 MB.

Proposed: a nightly pg_dump from GitHub Actions to S3, same shape as dwca-nightly.yml — assemble the IPv4 pooler DSN from the existing DB_PASSWORD + SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID secrets (memory: supabase-dsn-assembled-inline), pg_dump --format=custom of the whole database including auth and storage schemas, upload to a versioned prefix or a bucket with versioning/lifecycle so it is not overwrite-only, and a restore test at least once so the dump is known to load. Decide separately whether storage bucket OBJECTS (the 95 photos) need copying too — pg_dump captures only their metadata. Alternative or complement: upgrade the org to Pro for managed daily backups; a self-owned dump is still worth having since Pro's backups live in the same vendor account.

Record the choice as a decision record (docs/decisions/) and fix the PITR assumption in the design note.
notes: PR #424: https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/pull/424 — nightly dump + incremental media mirror to a new private versioned bucket (salishsea-io-backups), plus a manual restore-verify workflow. NOT yet run end to end: the bucket is created by the CDK deploy this merge triggers, and workflow_dispatch needs the workflow on the default branch. After merge: dispatch Database Backup Nightly, then Database Restore Verify.
close_reason: Merged and verified end to end. Nightly workflow dumps roles/schema/auth-storage/data to s3://salishsea-io-backups/db/YYYY/MM/DD/HHMMSS/ (private, versioned, BLOCK_ALL, RETAIN) and mirrors the 95 media objects incrementally. Restore verification passed on run 33416297278: roles clean, both auth/storage passes clean, trigger assertion passed, 61 tables and 170,522 rows restored, every irreplaceable table at its live count. Decision 038 records the design and the known gaps (vault secrets, platform config, 07:00 UTC granularity).

title: The register has no sub-matrilines; we have 73 of them
description:
We model a matriline at two depths and the register models it at one. Until someone
decides which side changes, 73 of our 132 matriline groups have no identifier to adopt
and 213 of our 375 membership rows have no group to hang from.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND (salish-ox2.1, PR salishsea-io#415, report at
docs/reference/register-reconciliation.md)

We carry the T073 lineage as three groups; the register carries it as one.

  ours (social_groups)                  register
  T073  <- T073A, T073B, T073C, T073D   SSA:0002039 "T073s"
  T073A <- T073A1, T073A2, T073A3       (nothing)
  T073C <- T073C1, T073C2               (nothing)

T073B and T073D are individuals with no lineage of their own, so they are members of T073
and nothing else. Verified against prod social_groups 2026-08-30.

Not one of the register's 134 matriline entities has a letter suffix. They are all
T002s, T007s, T073s, J17s, L32s -- top level only. So our 132 matriline rows split
cleanly: 59 plain T-numbers match a register T###s; 73 letter-suffixed sub-lineages
have no group upstream to be.

Those 73 report as `wrong-kind-only` rather than as misses because T073A is also a
whale -- the matriarch the sub-lineage is named after, SSA:0010248, an individual. The
name resolves; it resolves to an animal. This is not a spelling or fold problem and no
comparison rule fixes it. It is a modelling disagreement about how finely a matriline
subdivides.

It cuts both ways: 73 Bigg's register matrilines (T002s, T012s, T018s, ...) have no
catalogue group at all -- we carry T002C but no T002. The report's register-only figure is
75, which is those 73 plus the two Southern Resident lineages J17s and L32s that a
Bigg's-only catalogue was never going to hold.

WHY THIS BLOCKS salish-ox2.5

If public.social_groups becomes a materialization of the register, the 73 sub-lineages
have nothing to materialize from, and the 213 membership rows that point at them lose
their anchor. Over half our membership data.

The shortcut to avoid: assigning each row the identifier its name resolves to. That
hands 73 groups an individual's SSA:, after which T073A1's maternal group is the whale
T073A. Reporting kind mismatches separately from misses exists to make that visible
before someone writes it.

THE OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN

1. The register grows sub-matrilines as first-class entities.
2. The register derives matrilines from parentage -- ADR-0016 holds the edges, and
   nothing yet derives lineages from them. This would produce the sub-structure for
   free and is the option that needs the least new vocabulary upstream.
3. We collapse T073A into T073 and lose the sub-structure. Cheapest for us, destroys
   data a curator entered deliberately, and ADR-0012 frames our divergences as
   requirements the register must meet, not errors to delete.
4. We keep sub-lineages locally. Contradicts ADR-0012's "stops holding independent
   identity", but may be the honest answer for a while.

NEXT STEP

Carry it upstream as a curator question alongside the two in salish-ox2.3, with the
counts above. It is a bigger question than either of those: finding 1 sized to zero
and finding 4 turned out to be already expressed, while this one is unbounded and was
not among ADR-0012's five findings at all.

Re-run scripts/register/reconcile.ts against the current edition before acting -- the
numbers here are edition 2026.08.1.

Refs: animals ADR-0012, ADR-0016, ADR-0005. This repo: docs/reference/register-reconciliation.md.
notes:
The evidence went upstream by REWRITING animals#13 itself (2026-08-30) — the issue body now
carries the measured facts in the project's voice, addressed to S. Veirs and D. Bain; the
comment thread is empty. Title: 'Q22 — Does a Bigg's lineage have one level of real groups,
or two?' The ask is two questions: are letter-suffixed sub-groups real, and which level
should an observer record. User confirmed this form 2026-08-30.

(Earlier notes here described comment drafts that were posted and deleted; the final form
replaced them all.)

This issue waits on the reviewers' answer. salish-ox2.5's group half and salish-8vr.24 stay
blocked behind it.
2026-09-20: DECIDED upstream, option 1 (a register decision, recorded in animals ADR-0015 / animals#31; on this side only decision 035's Consequences carry an amendment note -- there is no separate salishsea-io record, deliberately). The register mints the 73 sub-lineages ahead of Q22 (animals#31, open, awaiting Peter's review because merging makes 73 identifiers permanent). The designation rule run on the register's own individuals reproduces our 73 exactly. Close this when #31 merges. Q22 (animals#13) is now assigned to Scott Veirs and no longer gates anything: its answer confirms the groups or retires them by merged/replaced_by.
close_reason: animals#31 merged 2026-09-20 as 1a30615: the register now holds the 73 Bigg's sub-lineages (SSA:0002131-0002203), nested inside the top-level lineages, minted ahead of Q22. The modelling disagreement is resolved in the direction of two levels; Q22 (animals#13, assigned to Scott Veirs) now confirms or retires them and gates nothing. Not yet in a released edition -- the changelog PR for 2026.09.1 is animals#33. salish-ox2.5's group half starts once that edition is released and loaded.

title: animals: settle Q1 as (a) — add the Resident ecotype, Southern Resident becomes a community
description:
Q1 (salish-sea/animals#1) asks whether "Southern Resident" is an ecotype or a
community of the Resident ecotype. Decided: option (a), the strict reading.
This is the gate for salish-0gb — nothing downstream can proceed until the
register holds an entity that corresponds to iNaturalist's `ater`.

WHAT (a) REQUIRES, from the rows as they stand on 2026-08-29:

  * ADD an ecotype `Resident`. SSA:0000003 is free and sits in the ecotype
    block beside SSA:0000001/2. Members: SSA:0000900 (Orcinus orca) as parent,
    per the existing pattern.
  * DEPRECATE SSA:0000001 -> SSA:0000010. Q1 says merge the ecotype into the
    community. ADR-0010 forbids reuse, so this is deprecations.tsv's first row;
    the file is header-only today.
  * MOVE the two names off SSA:0000001 onto SSA:0000010: "Southern Resident
    killer whale" (common) and "SRKW" (hidden).
  * RELABEL SSA:0000010 from "Southern Resident community" to "Southern
    Resident". The rank column already says `community`; repeating it in the
    label is the ADR-0011 error of writing display into the name.
  * REPOINT membership: SSA:0000001 -> SSA:0000900 becomes SSA:0000010 ->
    SSA:0000003, and SSA:0000003 -> SSA:0000900 is added. That closes the graph
    break Q1 diagnoses — SSA:0000010 currently has no row pointing up at all.
  * MOVE the mapping: SSA:0000001 skos:broadMatch NCBITaxon:9733 becomes
    SSA:0000003's.

OPTIONAL, and probably wanted given salish-frk: a Northern Resident community
as a sibling under SSA:0000003. The whole reason `ater` cannot be labelled SRKW
is that it includes Northern and Alaskan residents, and the register currently
cannot say so.

THE COST Q1 NAMES, and it is real: "SRKW" becomes a community rather than an
ecotype, which reads oddly to people who say it the other way — including
orcasite#1001, which calls SRKW, Bigg's, offshore and NRKW four parallel
ecotypes. Worth a note in the record so the orcasite conversation is not
surprised by it (salish-8vr).

Owners of the science call are S. Veirs and D. Bain per the issue. This is
their answer to give; the rows above are what it costs once given.
notes:
SHARPENED BY THE REGISTER OWNER (2026-08-29): the only ecotypes are Bigg's and
resident.

This makes (a) crisper. After the fix the ecotype layer is CLOSED AT TWO —
SSA:0000002 Bigg's and SSA:0000003 Resident — and everything below is community
or narrower. It also confirms the optional item above: Northern Resident is a
COMMUNITY under SSA:0000003, a sibling of Southern Resident, not an ecotype.

The register's DATA already agrees. entities.tsv has exactly two rows at rank
`ecotype` today, and the only defect is that one of them is Southern Resident,
which is the thing (a) fixes. Nothing has to be deleted.

The register's PROSE does not agree, in three places, and they should be
corrected as part of this change or they will re-teach the wrong hierarchy:

  * Q1 itself (salish-sea/animals#1) writes "where the ecotypes are resident,
    Bigg's and offshore".
  * docs/scope.md:86 — "Northern Residents and offshores are in scope but
    unpopulated."
  * decisions/0017-no-counts.md:24 and docs/open-questions.md (Q4) repeat it.

Note the SMM 2024 review supports the two-ecotype reading in its own words:
"the two ecotypes are considered provisionally as distinct subspecies of
Orcinus orca". Morin et al. addressed resident and Bigg's only; offshores were
not part of that proposal.

OPEN, and it is a rank question rather than a scope one: Q4 promises offshores
will be populated. If offshore is not an ecotype, what rank does it take when
it arrives? It cannot inherit the ecotype slot the docs currently assume. This
does not block (a) — no offshore entity exists — but the answer should land in
the same record, because (a) is what closes the ecotype vocabulary.

WIDENING GAP WITH ORCASITE, worth carrying to salish-8vr: orcasite#1001 calls
SRKW, Bigg's, offshore and NRKW four parallel ecotypes. After (a) it is two,
with SRKW and NRKW as communities beneath one of them and offshore unranked.
That is a bigger correction than the tag picker (salish-8vr.9) currently
assumes.
OFFSHORE, RESOLVED (2026-08-29, register owner): don't fight it — offshores can
occur, and the register should be able to record one.

THIS REMOVES WORK RATHER THAN ADDING IT. ADR-0004 already makes rank an open
vocabulary, so "the only ecotypes are Bigg's and resident" and "we can record
an offshore" were never in tension: the register never has to assert that the
ecotype set is exactly two. So (a) should do the actual fix — Southern Resident
becomes a community, the Resident ecotype is added — and NOT write down a
closed ecotype list anywhere.

Consequence: the three prose corrections flagged in the note above are NOT
needed. Q1's "the ecotypes are resident, Bigg's and offshore", scope.md:86 and
ADR-0017's "Northern Residents and offshores are in scope but unpopulated", and
Q4 all stand as written. An offshore entity, when it arrives, is a third
`ecotype` sibling of SSA:0000002 and SSA:0000003 under SSA:0000900, following
the same pattern.

What stays wrong is only orcasite#1001's list — not because it includes
offshore, but because it puts SRKW and NRKW beside it as parallel ecotypes when
they are communities. Already flagged on salish-8vr.9.

NO CROSSWALK FOR OFFSHORE, and this is why it does not affect salish-0gb.2.
SMM's 2024 review names O. o. ater, O. o. rectipinnus and O. o. orca as the
nominate subspecies; offshores are not assigned to any of them. So an offshore
ecotype gets a broadMatch to the species like SSA:0000001 has today, and no
skos:closeMatch to an iNaturalist subspecies. The coextensive-crosswalk
argument covers exactly two entities and no more.

TRAP FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS THE PROSE SIDE, measured 2026-08-29: 246 occurrence
bodies contain the word "offshore", 92 of them on Orcinus records — and in that
text it is almost always a LOCATION ("two whales offshore", "offshore of Point
No Point"), not an ecotype. src/identifiers.ts `ecotypeRE` deliberately does not
match it, and src/symbology.test.ts:151 pins that: `labelFor(orca('two whales
offshore'))` is 'Killer whale'. Adding an offshore entity upstream must not
become a reason to start matching the word downstream. If offshore sightings
ever need detecting from prose, it needs a different signal than the bare word.
CORRECTION to the note above (2026-08-29). It said "what stays wrong is only
orcasite#1001's list". Nothing is wrong there. #1001 sketches a data model —
tag `kind`, `iri`, `certainty` — and defers to the register for identifiers; it
makes no claim about which groups are ecotypes. Reading a design proposal as a
taxonomic assertion was the error, and it is mine, not the proposal's.

Minor consequence for Q1 itself, offered rather than asserted: Q1 cites that
same phrasing as evidence of "a real conflict of usage, and it is yours to
settle". A design comment is weak support for a usage claim. The conflict does
not depend on it — Q1's other example, that NOAA's listing unit is the Southern
Resident DPS, is a genuine and independent one — but if (a) is written up, the
#1001 citation is the part worth dropping.
PR OPEN: salish-sea/animals#30 (branch q1-resident-ecotype, 04ee8a7). CI green — validate, pull-request gates, CodeRabbit. Q1 commented with the SMM evidence: https://github.com/salish-sea/animals/issues/1#issuecomment-5466134805

Result: 12 unreachable entities -> 0. Two latent bugs fixed on the way — validate.py reported the deprecated tombstone as unreachable, and dist/structure.md's subtree diagram was keyed on `label` (ADR-0011 violation) so the relabel emptied it silently.

RAISED IN THE PR, NOT ANSWERED: searchable_name does not know about deprecation, so 'Southern Resident' now returns two candidates — the retired SSA:0000001 ecotype and the live SSA:0000010 community — with nothing marking the first retired. Hiding vs surfacing-with-a-flag is a schema call for the owner.

Awaiting the science confirmation from S. Veirs and D. Bain; not merged.
SEARCHABLE_NAME QUESTION ANSWERED (2026-08-29, register owner): surface the retired
row with a flag; do not hide it. `searchable_name` gains `retired` and `replaced_by`.

Rationale, and it is the view's own doctrine: this view describes awkward rows rather
than dropping them — that is why entity_label/kind/rank ride along, and why a `hidden`
name is typed rather than filtered. Hiding would be the only place the register drops
rows: a name surviving only on a tombstone becomes unresolvable, and C9's automatic
substitution needs a join it would otherwise not need. A picker filters `retired`;
an ingest pipeline follows `replaced_by` on the same row. `replaced_by` is null for a
`consider` deprecation, which is exactly right — that is the MUST-NOT-substitute case.

Existing columns and order unchanged: a consumer reading by name keeps working, one
reading by position does not. Recorded in CHANGELOG under Register.

Checked, not asserted: validate.py compares retired/replaced_by against
deprecations.tsv for EVERY deprecation, and "Southern Resident" joins the C2
acceptance trio. Both negative-tested (hardcode retired off; drop the replaced_by
join — each fails the build).

THE SWEEP THAT CAME WITH IT, and it was larger than expected. CodeRabbit found one
stale reference and it was a class, not an instance — prose and derived artefacts
still pointing at SSA:0000001 or at the pre-Q1 shape:
- README.md's outline drew the OLD hierarchy (no species at the top, community under
  an ecotype of the same name). First structural picture a reader sees.
- dist/structure.md's rank counts included the tombstone: THREE ecotypes where two
  are live. Same deprecation-blindness as searchable_name, on the diagram README
  points at. Node counts and edges now both exclude deprecated; the unreachable count
  already did.
- docs/walkthrough.md rolled J pod up through SSA:0000001 to reach a species.
- C5/C6 said "Partly ... pending Q1"; both are answerable in full.
- ADR-0008 illustrated the ecotype crosswalk with the identifier whose mapping moved.
- ADR-0021 offered SSA:0000001 as the Bioregistry submission's example.
- ADR-0013's objection to gating on --strict has lapsed: it rested on the count mixing
  provenance debt with a modelling gap, and the unreachable half is now zero.

LESSON WORTH KEEPING: a deprecation is not done when deprecations.tsv gets its row.
Every derived artefact and every doc that names the identifier or draws the shape has
to be swept, and `grep SSA:0000001` is the cheap way to find them. The register's own
front page was wrong for the length of this branch.

BRANCH: q1-resident-ecotype at d1c33bb, pushed. CI green (validate, pull-request).
PR #30 body rewritten — the "deliberately not answered" section is now the answer, all
blob links repointed to d1c33bb and curl-verified 200.

STILL BLOCKING THE MERGE, and it is not engineering: the science confirmation from
S. Veirs and D. Bain on Q1 (salish-sea/animals#1). Nothing else is outstanding.
close_reason: animals#30 squash-merged 2026-09-20 as 0e7aec3. Q1 settled as (a): SSA:0000003 Resident added, SSA:0000001 merged into SSA:0000010. UNRELEASED -- sits under 'Unreleased' in the animals CHANGELOG; salishsea-io loads by release tag, so nothing here changes until an edition after 2026.08.1 is cut and loaded. salish-0gb.2 is next.

title: Decide the URL scheme: a public route may not key on a designation
description:
/individuals/<designation> keys a public URL on a label, which animals ADR-0011
forbids outright — "nothing may join, match, or key on `label`" — and ADR-0012
names it as a live violation the migration has to address. Our own schema
already agrees it is unstable: designations.superseded_by exists precisely
because a code can be replaced.

Decide the target URL scheme and the transition, and record it as a decision
that amends 015 (and 016, 017 for matrilines and ecotypes).

The tension to resolve: T065A2 is what a person types, searches for and reads
in a Facebook post. SSA:0000123 is what is stable. A scheme that shows only the
opaque identifier is correct and unusable; one that shows only the designation
is usable and wrong.

Candidate shapes, not a recommendation:
  * Keep the designation path, resolve it through the register's fold, and
    301 a superseded code to its current one. The URL stays readable and the
    key stops being a label in everything but appearance.
  * /individuals/SSA:0000123/t065a2 — identifier is the key, slug is cosmetic
    and ignored, as GitHub and Stack Overflow do it.
  * Both: canonical is identifier-keyed, designation paths redirect.

Must account for: the Lambda@Edge rewrite that maps profile paths to
individual.html (decision 015) and the OG card renderer that reads the path;
existing links in the wild; e2e/og-previews.spec.ts, which asserts against
production.
notes:
DECIDED 2026-08-30 as docs/decisions/034-profile-urls-key-on-the-register-identifier.md
(branch profile-url-scheme, commit 5bab209).

Shape: /individuals/<7-digit local part>/<Designation>. Identifier is the key, slug is
composed by us and ignored on read, conventional casing (T065A2 not t065a2), designation
paths 301. Redirect at the viewer-request Lambda, fail-open to the shell with client-side
replaceState so a slow lookup degrades rather than 503s (decision 015's deadline rule).

Two things the issue did not anticipate:
1. The violation is already live. /individuals/T046A returns the generic site card in prod;
   65 non-primary designations are dead as URLs. The fix for ADR-0011 and the fix for those
   65 are the same change.
2. This is NOT blocked by salish-ox2.5. Individuals reconcile 510/510 and the ecotype 1/1,
   so /individuals/ and /ecotypes/ can move as soon as public.individuals carries SSA:.
   Only /matrilines/ waits on Q22 (salish-ox2.6). The epic's graph had all URL work behind
   the migration; it should not be.

Remaining for this issue: implementation, which needs SSA: on public.individuals first --
a narrow slice of ox2.5 that Q22 does not block.
PR salishsea-io#416 opened 2026-08-30 (branch profile-url-scheme, HEAD 6dbba9e).

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-11: PR salishsea-io#452 (branch profile-urls-by-identifier). Edge 301s designation paths, bare identifiers and (for crawlers) stale slugs to /individuals/<7-digit>/<slug> and /ecotypes/<7-digit>/<slug>; page canonicalises client-side; linker and all in-page links emit the new shape; smoke asserts the 301s. Matrilines untouched pending salish-ox2.6. Close on merge.
