title: Reconcile the catalogue against the register, entity by entity
description:
Before any schema moves, produce the reconciliation report: for each row in
public.individuals, social_groups, designations, group_memberships and
nicknames, the register entity it corresponds to, or the reason it has none.

USE THE REGISTER'S OWN FOLD, not an ad-hoc one. ADR-0019 publishes the
comparison rule with executable test cases (dist/fold_test.tsv), and the one
clause that must NOT be applied is folding the trailing `s` — it merges a
matriline with its matriarch. The indicative pass done when this epic was filed
used a crude upcase-and-strip-punctuation fold and matched 572 of 575
designation codes; that number needs redoing properly before anyone relies on
it.

Report per category, because the categories have different answers:

  * A catalogue row with exactly one register entity — the easy majority.
  * A catalogue row with none. Known: AO10 and CA20 (Alaska/California
    designations, animals Q23 / salish-sea/animals#14, open) and T046A.
  * A catalogue row with more than one candidate — the case that must not be
    guessed at.
  * A register entity with no catalogue row. The register holds 518 individual
    and 141 group entities against our 510 and 139, so a handful exists.
  * group_memberships by basis. How many are `association` decides how much of
    our data has nowhere to go under ADR-0005 (animals Q15,
    salish-sea/animals#11, open) — this is the number that sizes finding 1.
  * social_groups by kind, specifically how many are `named_group`, which the
    register's validator cannot express (finding 4).

Output a checked-in artefact, not a one-off query, so it can be re-run against
a later edition and diffed. scripts/register/ already holds the loader.

This is measurement only. It changes no schema and decides nothing.
notes:
DONE. PR salishsea-io#415 (branch register-reconciliation, ff2a3f5). Artefact is
docs/reference/register-reconciliation.md + .tsv, generated by
scripts/register/reconcile.ts; re-run and diff. CodeRabbit run locally until clean.

THE FOLD IS THE REGISTER'S AND IT IS PROVEN BEFORE USE. scripts/register/fold.ts
implements ADR-0019 once; reconcile.ts re-reads dist/fold_test.tsv out of whichever
edition it is reconciling and ABORTS if the fold disagrees. Reads a digest-verified
release, not register.* in the DB, so a proposed edition can be diffed against
production before adoption. Default --tag is whatever the DB says is loaded.

RESULTS, edition 2026.08.1 in production:

• individuals    510/510 resolve to exactly one register individual.
• designations   572/575. The three misses are the KNOWN ones: AO10, CA20 (animals
                 Q23) and T046A. The crude 572 was correct after all — but it was
                 correct by luck, since the ad-hoc fold was not the register's.
• social_groups  66/139 only. See below — this is where the work is.
• nicknames      380/403 carried. 23 names the register does not hold for that
                 animal; they are a migration loss unless asserted upstream.
• memberships    375/375 maternal, ZERO association.

FINDING 1 SIZES TO ZERO. ADR-0012 could not bound how much membership data has
nowhere to go under ADR-0005 while Q15 is open. None of it does. That removes the
largest unbounded risk from salish-ox2 and should be said on salish-ox2.3.

SOCIAL_GROUPS IS A GRANULARITY DIFFERENCE, NOT A NAMING ONE — and it is new.
Both sides hold 132 Bigg's matrilines and only 59 are the same 59. We carry
sub-lineages (T073A, T064B1); the register carries top-level prefixes (T073s) and
has NO letter-suffixed matriline at all. Invisible until now because the indicative
pass only ever tested designation codes, which are individuals, never group
designations. 73 of our matrilines have no register group; 75 register matrilines
have no row of ours (73 Bigg's + J17s + L32s). Same phenomenon counted twice.
This is the real content of salish-ox2.5 and it is bigger than "assign identifiers".

FINDING 4 IS NOT WHAT ADR-0012 THOUGHT, and this is the most useful thing found.
A category nobody asked for — register entities claimed by TWO catalogue rows —
turned up exactly six, and every one is a named_group and the matriline it names
(Secret Agents + T007 -> SSA:0002001; Motley Crew + T023; Ted's Gang + T041; Sea
Monster Family + T073; Gretzky's + T099; Runaway's + T109). The register DOES
express a named group: as a `common` NAME on the ranked matriline. So finding 4 is
not "the validator requires a rank and we have none to give" — it is "it is
expressed as a name, and we model it as a group". Carry THAT upstream on
salish-ox2.3, not the original framing.

METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING: count collisions per catalogue THING, not per row. Per
row it reports all 510 individuals colliding with their own designation codes,
which is true by construction and says nothing.

CORRECTNESS THE DATA CANNOT EXERCISE, added because the animals side changed under
it: a retired identifier keeps its names upstream, so once an edition with a
deprecation ships, a catalogue row would resolve onto a withdrawn identifier and
this migration is what would write it into public.*. Retired entities are read
where published, ignored where not, excluded from matching, reported as
`retired-only` with the replacement, and skipped in the reverse pass. 2026.08.1 has
no deprecations, so that path and the `many` verdict are covered by unit tests
against a constructed edition (scripts/register/match.test.ts) rather than by data.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: nothing is decided. Where a row has more than one
candidate the report lists them and stops.
close_reason: Closed

title: [epic] Adopt the register as the source of individual and group identity
description:
SUPERSEDED IN PART BY salish-ox2.1's MEASUREMENT (2026-08-30) — read the notes
before acting on this. Two of the claims below are measured false: association
membership is zero rows, and named_group is already expressed upstream. Groups are
a much larger reconciliation problem than "nearly total" suggests. The framing
below is kept as what was believed when the epic was filed.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

ADR-0012 in salish-sea/animals decides that this repository "stops holding
independent identity and becomes a materialization of" the register. The
salish-ayb epic took the FIRST half of that — taxon names — and deliberately
deferred the second: "it does not touch the individual catalogue (individuals,
social_groups, designations, group_memberships, nicknames, parties) or the
public profile URLs keyed on primary_designation ... which ADR-0012 also
retires, but which is a much larger migration and should be its own epic once
names have proved the pipeline."

Names have proved the pipeline. Decision 033 records the naming half; edition
2026.08.1 is loaded in production and resolves 91.5% of occurrences (58,669 of
64,097, measured 2026-08-29). This is that second epic.

WHAT IS STILL OURS THAT SHOULD NOT BE

  public.individuals          510 rows   primary_designation, taxon_id, sex,
                                         life_status, mother_id, father_id
  public.social_groups        139 rows   kind, anchor_individual_id, designation,
                                         parent_group_id
  public.designations         575 rows   code, scheme, is_primary, superseded_by
  public.group_memberships    375 rows   basis ∈ maternal/association/curated
  public.nicknames            403 rows
  public.parties                         (naming authorities — likely stays ours)

The register holds 518 individual and 141 group entities — near-identical
counts, which is expected: both were seeded from the same Bigg's material.

MEASURED OVERLAP (2026-08-29, crude fold: upcase, strip non-alphanumerics —
NOT ADR-0019's fold). 572 of 575 catalogue designation codes match a register
label or names.tsv row. Every individual has a designation. The three that do
not match:

  AO10, CA20  — Alaska/California designations, which is exactly animals Q23
                (salish-sea/animals#14), still open.
  T046A       — a Bigg's code the register appears not to carry under any
                spelling; worth checking before assuming a real gap.

So the mapping is nearly total and the migration is not a data-reconciliation
problem. It is a schema, URL and semantics problem.

WHAT ADR-0012 SAYS THIS COSTS US

  * New identifiers. public.* carries SSA: directly — ADR-0012 is explicit that
    decision 008 does not apply to the register (recorded on our side in
    decision 033), so there is no `animals` mirror schema and no translation
    layer.
  * Changed URLs. /individuals/<designation> is keyed on primary_designation,
    which ADR-0011 forbids: "nothing may key on a label". ADR-0012 calls this
    "a live violation ... a present fact and the migration has to address it".
    Decisions 015, 016, 017 define these routes; the Lambda@Edge rewrite in
    infra/ knows the path shape (decision 015).
  * A rank-vocabulary reconciliation. The register has ecotype, community, clan,
    pod, matriline. We add `named_group` — real travelling groups with names and
    no rank ("Motley Crew") — and the register's validator REQUIRES a rank. This
    is one of ADR-0012's five findings and is NOT yet answered upstream.

THE FIVE FINDINGS, AND WHICH ARE STILL OPEN. ADR-0012 frames the catalogue's
divergences as requirements the register must meet before migration, not as
errors to delete:

  1. membership_basis = association — UNRESOLVED upstream (animals Q15,
     salish-sea/animals#11). ADR-0005 declares membership genealogical without
     saying what a curator does when a published roster is associational. We
     hold 375 membership rows; how many are `association` decides how much of
     our data has nowhere to go.
  2. mother_id / father_id — ANSWERED upstream by ADR-0016 (parentage as edges,
     per-claim provenance). The register does not yet DERIVE matrilines from
     parentage, so the two are asserted independently and cross-checked.
  3. normalize_designation() — ANSWERED by ADR-0019 plus dist/fold_test.tsv.
     One clause must not survive: folding the trailing `s`, which merges a
     matriline with its matriarch. Tracked as salish-8vr.18, which belongs to
     this epic as much as to the Orcasound one.
  4. named_group — OPEN, see above.
  5. identification_status separate from evidence — DISCHARGED by relocation
     (ADR-0018): annotation semantics are the consumer's, so our model stands
     and this one does not migrate.

SEQUENCING QUESTION ADR-0012 RAISES AND DOES NOT ANSWER: does the catalogue
migrate before or after the first Orcasound bout is tagged? Tagging against
identifiers that later change defeats the purpose. That makes this epic and
salish-8vr order-dependent, and neither currently says which goes first.

CAVEATS THAT CARRY OVER FROM salish-ayb. The animals README still says
"Nothing here is ratified. No row in data/ has been verified by a curator", and
ADR-0012 is itself Status: Proposed. Names were tolerable to ship uncurated.
Identity in a public URL is a much larger commitment, and 13 curator questions
are open upstream.

EXISTING ISSUES THAT THIS EPIC SHOULD ABSORB OR REFRAME — all predate the
register and assume a local catalogue is authoritative: salish-0f6 (individuals
lacking a maternal membership row), salish-lzi (ingest the SRKW catalogue),
salish-47h, salish-754, salish-ek3. Re-read each against ADR-0012 before
working it.

Refs: animals ADR-0005, ADR-0011, ADR-0012, ADR-0016, ADR-0018, ADR-0019,
Q15/Q23. This repo: decision 033, decision 015, decision 016, decision 017,
decision 027, and the epic salish-ayb it continues.
notes:
salish-ox2.1 IS DONE (PR salishsea-io#415). Three things in this epic's description are
now measured rather than estimated, and two of them are wrong as written:

1. "The mapping is nearly total and the migration is not a data-reconciliation problem.
   It is a schema, URL and semantics problem." TRUE FOR INDIVIDUALS (510/510) AND
   DESIGNATIONS (572/575, the three known misses), FALSE FOR GROUPS. Only 66 of 139
   social_groups resolve. We and the register both hold 132 Bigg's matrilines and only
   59 are the same 59: we subdivide (T073A, T064B1), the register carries top-level
   prefixes (T073s) and has no letter-suffixed matriline at all. The indicative pass
   missed this because it only tested designation codes, which are individuals.

2. Finding 1 (association membership) SIZES TO ZERO. 375/375 maternal. The largest
   unbounded risk in this epic is not a risk.

3. Finding 4 (named_group) is already expressed upstream, as a `common` name on the
   ranked matriline rather than as a rankless group — so the framing "the register's
   validator REQUIRES a rank and we have none to give" is not the problem to solve.
   Detail on salish-ox2.3.

Also new, and the finding most likely to break salish-ox2.5 quietly: six register
entities are each claimed by TWO of our rows (a named_group and the matriline it
names). A migration assigning identifiers row by row would hand both the same SSA:.

The report is regenerable — scripts/register/reconcile.ts, --tag to point it at an
edition that is not loaded yet — so re-run it before ox2.5 rather than trusting these
numbers later.
close_reason: Every child closed. The register is the source of individual and group identity: register identifiers key profile URLs (034), matriline membership and the group hierarchy are the register's (050, 051), designations are compared by its fold (052), and an animal's sex, birth years and life status are copied from it on every load (051). What stays ours is what the register lacks: the matriarch a matriline is named for, parentage, unpublished designations, and nickname facts.

title: [bug] Re-run the deploy for #399: db push failed on a Supabase pooler outage
description:
The Deploy run for #399 (6a4b30c) FAILED at `supabase db push`:

  failed to connect to postgres: host=aws-1-us-west-1.pooler.supabase.com
  user=postgres.grztmjpzamcxlzecmqca — FATAL: Failed to connect to database:
  {:error, :timeout} (SQLSTATE 08006)

Not our code. Supabase's control plane was down at the time: `supabase db query --linked`
was failing the same way ("Failed to create login role: Connection terminated due to
connection timeout") for roughly the preceding hour.

WHAT STATE PROD IS IN (checked 2026-08-28)
  - salishsea.io: 200. PostgREST answers 401 without a key, i.e. responding. The DATA
    PLANE IS HEALTHY and users are unaffected.
  - The ingest Edge Function WAS deployed — that step runs before db push. #399 changed no
    ingest code, so it is functionally identical to what was already running.
  - Migration 20260828120000_subspecies_show_species_name.sql was NOT applied. Production
    still shows "Pacific Harbor Seal" and "Western River Otter" rather than rolling them
    up to the species name.
  - The frontend was not deployed either (the step follows db push). #399 is
    migration-only, so nothing is missing there.

TO RESOLVE
  Re-run the Deploy workflow once Supabase is healthy. `supabase db push` is forward-only
  and idempotent over already-applied migrations, so a re-run is safe. Confirm first:

    npx supabase db query --linked "SELECT 1"

  Then verify the migration landed:

    SELECT pg_get_viewdef('public.occurrences'::regclass) ILIKE '%Delphinus delphis %';

WORTH NOTING: the deploy is documented as "no automatic rollback, deliberately" and the
sequence is Edge Function -> db push -> S3 sync with no atomicity. This failure landed in
exactly that gap. It caused no harm this time because #399 touched only a migration, but a
PR that changed the function AND the schema would have left them out of step.
close_reason:
Resolved by a later deploy, verified in prod 2026-08-29.

Migration 20260828120000_subspecies_show_species_name is present in prod supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (alongside 20260828000000/100000/110000 and 20260829000000), so a subsequent successful Deploy re-ran supabase db push and applied it — no manual re-run was needed. Idempotent forward-only push, as the issue predicted.

Functional check, not just the migrations table:
  Phoca vitulina richardii  -> 'Harbour seal'
  Lontra canadensis pacifica -> 'River otter'
So the subspecies roll up to the species vernacular name, which is what #399 was for. The two-names-for-one-animal symptom is gone.

Related: the same 2026-08-28 Supabase control-plane outage also stalled the ingest for 60 minutes (15:50-16:50 UTC) without tripping the heartbeat — see salish-oyf.

title: animals: cut the first release so consumers can pin an artefact
description:
BLOCKS everything downstream. ADR-0012 says both consumers consume "a released
artefact at a pinned tag"; ADR-0013 says "artefacts are attached to GitHub
releases, not committed as binaries". As of 2026-08-27 salish-sea/animals has
no git tags and no GitHub releases, so there is nothing to pin and the
consumption contract is unimplemented.

`dist/` already holds the right files, generated by `python3 bin/validate.py
--write-dist` with CI failing on drift. `dist/searchable_name.tsv` is precisely
what this repo needs: preferred name plus every alternate, each carrying the
entity's label, kind and rank (competency question C2).

Work: decide the version scheme, attach dist/ (and arguably data/) to a
release, and document what a consumer is promised across versions. ADR-0014
frames the register as a publication rather than a service, which should inform
whether the artefact is expected to be re-fetched or vendored.

Ordering caveat: cutting v0.1.0 before the coverage additions means this repo
pins a release it already knows is incomplete. Either land coverage first, or
cut early and accept a v0.2.0 bump — the latter is probably better, since it
exercises the pin-and-upgrade path while the stakes are low.
notes:
CORRECTION (2026-08-27): .github/workflows/release.yml already exists in the animals
repo and cuts a release on a CalVer tag push ('[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9].[0-9][0-9].*'),
attaching register.db, register-tsv.tar.gz, schema.sql and SHA256SUMS. The README
documents permanent asset URLs at releases/latest/download/<asset>.

So the mechanism is built and this issue is narrower than filed: what is missing is the
TAG. No tags exist yet. The work is to decide the first CalVer edition and push it —
not to build a release pipeline.
close_reason:
Cut 2026.08.1 — the register's first release.

https://github.com/salish-sea/animals/releases/tag/2026.08.1

The issue was filed as 'build a release pipeline'; it was narrower than that, because
release.yml already existed and cuts on a CalVer tag push. What was missing was the tag.

Verified end to end, not just that the workflow went green: all four permanent URLs under
releases/latest/download/ return 200, the published SHA256SUMS verify against the
downloaded artefacts, and register.db opens and reports 699 entities / 684 names /
43 mappings including the new SSA:0000938 Pinnipedia and SSA:0000939 Lutrinae.

Also filled a gap first: #27 and #28 had merged without changelog entries, which matters
because the versioning section tells consumers the changelog is what they watch. Added in
#29 before tagging.

The release note states plainly that no row has been curator-verified and that
validate.py reports 157 unverified rows. This unblocks salish-ayb.5 (materialize the
register), which now has an artefact to pin.

title: animals: crosswalk drift + pending-work maintenance workflow
description:
The register's crosswalks point at moving targets. Nothing currently notices
when one moves.

DEMONSTRATED, not hypothetical (2026-08-27): auditing all 512 rows of
`inaturalist.taxa` against the iNaturalist API found 9 taxa deactivated
upstream, every one carrying a `current_synonymous_taxon_ids` pointer. Four
were the Sagmatias genus split landing at once — `Sagmatias` itself plus
australis, cruciger, obscurus — and `Sagmatias obliquidens` (1368491 ->
1664971) is the one we hold records under. `mappings.tsv` maps only the active
id and is CORRECT; there was no way to know that without asking the API.

WHAT CAN DRIFT
  1. An `inaturalist.taxon:` object becomes inactive or is merged away.
  2. An iNaturalist taxon is renamed, so `object_label` in mappings.tsv goes
     stale while the id stays valid.
  3. An `NCBITaxon:` id in entities.tsv is merged or renamed.
  4. WoRMS moves, which ADR-0008 names as a parallel authority (Q26 on the
     Sagmatias/Aethalodelphis genus is live right now).
  5. New taxa appear in a consumer's corpus with no register entity —
     "pending work" rather than drift.

SPLIT THE WORKFLOW, because 1-4 and 5 need different inputs.

  DRIFT (belongs in salish-sea/animals, self-contained): a scheduled GitHub
  Action reads data/mappings.tsv and data/entities.tsv, batches the ids to the
  iNaturalist and NCBI/OLS APIs (iNat takes 30 ids per /v1/taxa call), and
  asserts is_active plus name == object_label. Reports rather than fails: an
  upstream change is not our error. On a PR it SHOULD fail, though — a newly
  added mapping pointing at an inactive taxon is a real defect and cheap to
  catch at review time.

  PENDING WORK (belongs here): coverage needs the occurrence corpus, which the
  register does not and should not have. Either this repo publishes a taxon
  frequency list the workflow can read, or it runs its own coverage check and
  files `animals:` issues. Prefer the former — it keeps the register's CI free
  of a dependency on our database.

OUTPUT: open or update a single tracking issue on salish-sea/animals listing
what moved, rather than one issue per drifted row. Include the replacement id
so the fix is a one-line edit.

NOTE: repo convention pins every `uses:` to a full 40-character commit SHA of
the action's latest release, with a trailing version comment.

Cousin issue on this side: the mirror-refresh work, which is what let the
Sagmatias deactivation sit unnoticed in our data.
notes:
Implemented: salish-sea/animals PR #27 (branch crosswalk-drift-check).

bin/check_crosswalks.py (stdlib only, matching validate.py) + .github/workflows/crosswalks.yml.
actionlint clean. Verified against seeded bad data: detects the inactive taxon with the
right replacement id, a stale object_label, and a non-resolving id, with drift as warning
and unresolvable as error. Against real data today: 0 drifted, 0 broken.

Weekly schedule keeps ONE crosswalk-drift issue as the worklist and closes it when clean.
PR mode compares against the base branch so only newly-added mappings are held to being
live. An unreachable API fails the run rather than filing an issue.

The coverage half stayed on this side as designed — see salish-ayb.2.
MERGED: salish-sea/animals#27. CI confirms the job split — pull-request job runs, scheduled job skips on a PR.

title: Adopt the animals register as the source of animal identity
description:
ADR-0012 in salish-sea/animals decides it: "This register is authoritative; the
SalishSea.io catalogue reconciles toward it." SalishSea.io stops holding
independent animal identity and becomes a materialization of the register —
same identifiers, same membership model, same definitions, loaded into Postgres
and presented.

Nothing tracked this before. The salish-8vr epic is entirely Orcasound-side
(orcasite, orcahello, register curation); ADR-0012's own consequence for this
repo had no issue.

WHY IT SURFACED NOW (2026-08-27): the map draws single-letter symbols whose
fallback is `vernacular_name[0]`, so a River Otter renders as "N". Fixing the
label exposed that every display name on the map comes from `inaturalist.taxa`
— an upstream mirror — including on our own native submissions. That is decision
008's "no downstream leakage" rule being violated in the most visible surface we
have. The first instinct, a `public.taxon_names` override table, would have
minted a second opinion about animal names, which is precisely what ADR-0012
forbids.

THE REGISTER ALREADY HAS THE ANSWER:
  SSA:0000906  taxon  Lontra canadensis  NCBITaxon:76717
  SSA:0000906  River otter  common  en  SEED
  SSA:0000906  skos:exactMatch  inaturalist.taxon:41777

Curated, sourced, and crosswalked to the exact iNat id our mirror keys on.

COVERAGE, measured against the local mirror 2026-08-27: the register's 19
`kind = taxon` entities cover 59,887 of 61,411 occurrences (97.5%) via the
iNaturalist crosswalk. The 1,524-record gap is 49 taxa, addressed in the
`animals:` children below.

SEQUENCING: take the taxon-name slice first. It is additive, and it does not
touch the individual catalogue (`individuals`, `social_groups`, `designations`,
`group_memberships`, `nicknames`, `parties`) or the public profile URLs keyed on
`primary_designation` — which ADR-0012 also retires, but which is a much larger
migration and should be its own epic once names have proved the pipeline.

CAVEATS TO CARRY: the animals README says "Nothing here is ratified. No row in
data/ has been verified by a curator", and ADR-0012 is Status: Proposed.
Adopting it for display ships uncurated names to production — trivial for
"River otter", less so for ecotype labels.

Refs: animals ADR-0008 (species identity delegated), ADR-0011 (label is a
preferred name, not a display string), ADR-0012, ADR-0013 (releases carry the
artefacts), ADR-0014. This repo: decision 008, decision 009, decision 027.
notes: 7/7 children closed. Register live in production: edition 2026.08.1 (699 entities, 684 names), 91.5% of occurrences resolve a register entity (58,669/64,097, measured 2026-08-29) — ahead of the 84.9% estimate because #399's subspecies fallback landed after it. Decision 033 records the reasoning. Follow-ons deliberately left OUTSIDE this epic: salish-1g8 (nothing automates the load or notices an empty register), salish-0gb (subspecies, a curator call). The individual-identity half this epic deferred is now salish-ox2.
close_reason: Closed

title: Land marine-mammal scope: decision 027, policy §6.5, EML coverage, product copy
description: Execute the resolution of epic salish-pjl (grill session 2026-08-13): widen taxonomic scope to PSEMP marine mammals, keep whale-centric positioning, do not ingest PSEMP data. Covers decision record 027, rights-policy §6.5 amendment + matching dwc view migration, EML taxonomicClassification blocks, PRODUCT.md/about.html/obs-panel.ts factual claims, CONTEXT.md segment species-gate.

title: Get a decision on orcasound/orcasite#1001
description:
#1001 understates the cost: it claims 'only slug conventions and a moderator habit', but preserving moderator uncertainty ('J123?', '+L?') implies a schema change — plausibly a certainty attribute on item_tags, plus somewhere for a tag to carry a register identifier.

Attribution matters here: that requirement is OURS as the owner of annotation semantics (decision 028), not the register's. animals ADR-0018 grants the register exactly two claims on an annotation — cite an identifier, and record the edition behind a derived fact — and ADR-0009's five-column table is explicitly illustrative. An earlier version of this issue credited the certainty column to ADR-0009; that was wrong, and repeating it upstream would re-create the confusion ADR-0018 exists to end.

Resolution is by editing the #1001 body in place rather than reposting: the thread is not unanswered (dthaler endorsed it, scottveirs engaged at length), the body is simply stale. It also still proposes unconfirmed/false-positive tags, which animals Q21 declined — a detector false positive is a bout-level flag, a mis-set category is a wrong field value, and a mystery signal is tagged at the species level.
notes: Voice resolved (salish-8vr.1 → decision 028): salishsea-io posts and carries #1001; the register does not address Orcasound directly. Post under this repository's name, citing 028 and 013. Still gated on salish-8vr.4 landing Q18's substance — one voice only helps if it has something coherent to say.
close_reason: Resolved 2026-08-14. #1001 rewritten in place as the narrative hub; the ask split into six independently-deliverable upstream issues (orcasite #1013 kind+iri, #1014 certainty, #1015 picker, #1016 classify existing tags, #1017 machine class on detections; orcahello #597 send class label) plus two register issues (animals #19 missing entities/names, #20 designation matching). Corrected the cost estimate, attributed the certainty requirement to this repo per decision 028, and withdrew the unconfirmed/false-positive ask per the Q21 three-way split. Decision still pending upstream — that is now tracked per-issue rather than in one thread.

title: [bug] Calendar count query times out for anon: date-cast predicate defeats the observed_at indexes
description:
occurrence_days filters '(observed_at AT TIME ZONE PST8PDT)::date BETWEEN from_day AND to_day'. No index matches that expression — migration 20260610001507 deliberately dropped the date-cast indexes as vestigial when the app moved to timestamp-range filtering, and the region function (20260731000000) reintroduced the cast.

Result: seq scan on maplify.sightings plus a nested loop against taxa discarding 101,001 rows. 180ms warm / 14,734 buffers for a 42-day window. anon has statement_timeout=3s, so a cold or contended execution exceeds it — SALISHSEA-IO-11, one event 2026-08-02.

Filtering on the equivalent timestamptz range instead uses sightings_observed_at_gmt, inaturalist_observations_observed_at, encounters_observed_at and taxa_pkey: 79ms / 12,464 buffers, and index scans rather than seq scans cold.
design:
Keep the (from_day, to_day) date signature so no client changes. Convert to a half-open timestamptz range inside the function: observed_at >= from_day-at-PST8PDT and observed_at < (to_day + 1)-at-PST8PDT.

Verified equivalent over the entire corpus (2012-2026, ~30 DST transitions): 2,568 days, 61,671 occurrences, zero rows differing in either direction.

Rejected reading occurrence_index (28ms/731 buffers) — it lags ingest ~6 minutes, which decision 021 rejected so a contributor's own sighting moves their circle immediately.
acceptance_criteria: occurrence_days uses index scans on the observed_at indexes; returns byte-identical results to the current definition; anon can call it for a 42-day window well inside 3s.
close_reason: Fixed in 6a66908 (PR #362), migration 20260803000000; verified applied in prod and the deployed occurrence_days uses the half-open timestamptz range predicate. Issue was left open because beads doesn't close from commit trailers.

title: Revoke inert anon/authenticated write grants on public relations
description:
Production grants `anon` and `authenticated` INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on 44 `public` relations. Nothing needs them and no migration created them.

Found 2026-07-30 alongside salish-0ew; deliberately left out of that fix so a parity migration did not also change production's permissions.

## Not a vulnerability

Checked every RLS policy in `public` on 2026-07-30:

- Every table carrying these grants has RLS **enabled**.
- **No policy permits an anon write.** Every anon policy is `FOR SELECT`. The `FOR ALL` policies on `observations` and `observation_photos` are scoped to `authenticated` with ownership predicates (`user_uuid = auth.uid()`, or a contributor-join).
- The remaining relations are views (`occurrences`, `occurrence_days`, `individual_occurrences`, `group_occurrences`, `ecotype_occurrences`, `occurrence_identifications`, `occurrence_unresolved_codes`). They are UNION/aggregate views, so they are not auto-updatable and a write fails regardless of grant.

So the grants are inert. This is cleanup, not an incident.

## Why bother

They are a loaded footgun. The moment someone adds a permissive policy to one of these tables -- entirely reasonable in isolation -- the write grant is already sitting there and the table becomes anon-writable. Defence in depth wants the grant absent, so that a policy mistake alone is not sufficient.

Also included: `GRANT SELECT ON public.contributor_email_addresses TO anon, authenticated`, reproduced in migration `20260730120000` purely to match prod. It is inert today (RLS on, zero policies, default deny) but should not exist.

## The care this needs

`authenticated` genuinely writes to `observations` and `observation_photos` -- the sighting form's path. Revoking too broadly breaks contribution, and the failure would be silent for anonymous readers and loud only for logged-in contributors, so it will not show up in a smoke test that does not log in.

Work out exactly which grants the write paths depend on before revoking anything. `sighting-form.ts` goes through `rpc('upsert_observation')`, which may be SECURITY DEFINER and therefore not need direct table grants at all -- confirm rather than assume, and check the delete and photo-attachment paths too.

Revoke in a migration (so local/CI/prod stay reconciled), not out of band -- out-of-band changes are exactly what caused salish-0ew.
acceptance_criteria:
- The write paths (`upsert_observation`, delete, photo attachment) are traced and documented, establishing which grants `authenticated` actually requires.
- A migration revokes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from `anon` on all 44 relations, and from `authenticated` on everything the traced paths do not need.
- `SELECT` on `public.contributor_email_addresses` is revoked from `anon` and `authenticated` in the same migration.
- A logged-in contributor can still create, edit and delete a sighting with photos, verified against a database built from migrations.
- Anonymous read of the map, list and calendar is unaffected.
notes:
Write-path analysis done 2026-07-31; implementation not started.

FINDING: public.upsert_observation is SECURITY INVOKER, not DEFINER (prosecdef=false, owner=postgres). It therefore runs with the caller's privileges, so 'authenticated' genuinely needs direct table grants — the guess in this issue's description that it might be DEFINER, and so need none, was wrong.

It writes exactly two tables: public.observations and public.observation_photos. Separately, src/obs-summary.ts:316 does a direct .from('observations').delete().

So the minimum 'authenticated' actually needs is:
  INSERT, UPDATE on public.observations
  INSERT, UPDATE on public.observation_photos
  DELETE on public.observations
and 'anon' needs none of the 44 write grants at all.

BLOCKED ON A DECISION (do not start without it):
  (a) Narrow revoke — strip anon entirely, trim authenticated to the five grants above. Low risk, keeps the current security model.
  (b) Make upsert_observation SECURITY DEFINER — then authenticated needs no direct write grants and every write goes through one audited function. Stronger, but it changes the write path's security model and wants its own decision record.

Reverted to open 2026-07-31 rather than left in_progress: the analysis is recorded, but nothing should be implemented until (a) or (b) is chosen.
close_reason: Done in PR #444, merged as 1cd9ea9 and verified in production: anon holds zero effective table writes, authenticated writes only observations/observation_photos, contributor_email_addresses is readable by nobody, and a signed-in create+photo+delete round-trip still succeeds. Follow-up salish-cuu covers the default privileges that caused it.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text:
Concrete evidence, and it is not inert. On 2026-09-10 a client could write `notified_at` on the brand-new public.feedback table in production — enough to submit a report pre-marked as handled so the notifier would never file it. Verified against prod inside a rolled-back transaction.

The cause is the one this issue is about, and the reason it went unnoticed is worth recording: local and prod disagree on the default privileges for new tables in `public`.

    local  ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for postgres in public:  anon=Dxtm/postgres
    prod   ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for postgres in public:  anon=arwdDxtm/postgres

`a`, `r`, `w`, `d` are INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE. The local stack has had them removed from its defaults; production has not. So every table this project has created in `public` was granted full read/write to anon and authenticated at CREATE time in prod, and no amount of testing as `SET ROLE anon` on a laptop will show it — the laptop is correctly configured.

That means the grants are only "inert" where an RLS policy happens to withhold the rows. Any table with a permissive policy, or one added later, is exposed by default rather than by decision.

20260910020000 fixes public.feedback specifically (REVOKE ALL, then GRANT INSERT on named columns). The sweep across the rest of public.* is this issue, and it should check prod, not local. 🤖

title: Migrations do not reproduce prod's grants — a DB built from migrations serves no data
description:
A database built from `supabase/migrations` alone does not serve traffic: `anon` cannot SELECT `public.occurrences`, and the REST API answers `permission denied for view occurrences`.

Found 2026-07-30 while mirroring prod into the local stack.

## Evidence

SELECT grants to `anon`/`authenticated` on `public` + `dwc`:

- **prod: 48**
- **fresh `supabase db reset` from migrations: 14**

**34 grants exist only in prod** — 17 relations x 2 roles. The migrations-only set is a strict subset of prod's; nothing is granted locally that prod lacks. They cover essentially the whole public API surface: `occurrences`, `contributors`, `individuals`, `designations`, `observations`, `observation_photos`, `identifications`, `parties`, `social_groups`, `group_memberships`, `providers`, `collections`, `organizations`, `user_contributor`, `contributor_email_addresses`, `occurrence_identifications`, `occurrence_unresolved_codes`.

(An earlier revision of this issue said 15 and 33. That was an artifact of psql's `Time:` output being captured into the comparison file, inflating the local count by one. Corrected 2026-07-30 after CodeRabbit flagged the arithmetic on PR #356.)

`grep -rn "GRANT.*occurrences" supabase/migrations/` finds grants for `individual_occurrences`, `group_occurrences` and `ecotype_occurrences` -- but **never for `public.occurrences` itself**.

## Why it has gone unnoticed

The grants were applied to prod out of band. Every later migration touches the view with `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`, which **preserves existing grants** -- so nothing ever disturbed them in prod, and nothing ever recreated them anywhere else.

This directly violates the convention already written in CLAUDE.md: "SELECT grants ship in the same migration that creates a table (Supabase RLS defaults silently zero out joins otherwise)."

## Impact

- Prod cannot be rebuilt from migrations. If it ever had to be (disaster recovery, a new environment, a staging clone), the frontend would come up dead.
- Local dev and CI are not representative. Anything exercising the anon REST path against a freshly reset DB tests a different permission model than prod.
- The gap is invisible from prod, which is the only place that looks correct.

## NOT a security problem

`contributor_email_addresses` is granted to `anon` in prod, but it has RLS enabled with **zero policies** -- default-deny, so `anon` gets no rows. Checked `contributors` (RLS, 1 policy), `user_contributor` (RLS, 1 policy), `observations` (RLS, 3 policies). No leak. The issue is reproducibility, not exposure.

## Fix

PR #356 — migration `20260730120000_public_select_grants.sql`. Verified: a fresh reset now yields grants byte-identical to prod (48 = 48, empty diff both directions), and `/rest/v1/occurrences` returns `[]` with the anon key.
acceptance_criteria:
- A migration adds every SELECT grant prod has and migrations lack, so `supabase db reset` produces a database whose anon/authenticated grants match prod exactly (48 = 48, empty diff in both directions).
- After a bare `supabase db reset`, `/rest/v1/occurrences` with the anon key returns HTTP 200 and a well-formed result — `[]` on an unseeded reset, rows when data is present — rather than the `permission denied for view occurrences` error it returned before. The check is on the permission path, not on row count.
- A guard exists against regressing: either a CI assertion diffing grants against a checked-in expected set, or a smoke test hitting the anon REST path on the freshly reset CI database.
- The other two drift items found alongside this are recorded (see notes) and either fixed or explicitly accepted.
notes:
Two smaller drifts found in the same sweep. A full column-level diff (389 columns each side) showed ONLY these:

1. `happywhale.encounter_sample` -- exists in prod, no migration creates it. One `id integer` column, 5,610 rows, referenced nowhere in the repo. Looks like an ad-hoc sampling leftover. Decide: drop it in prod, or add a migration.
2. `happywhale.individuals.primary_id` and `.nickname` are `varchar(100)` in prod; migrations declare `varchar(50)`. Only `nickname` needs it (2 rows over 50 chars, max 60); `primary_id` maxes at 28. Note `public.occurrences` depends on `primary_id`, so widening it in a migration means dropping and recreating the view -- `ALTER TABLE` alone fails with "cannot alter type of a column used by a view or rule".

`scripts/pull-prod-db.sh` (PR #355) works around both -- excludes the table, widens `nickname`. Those workarounds should be deleted as each drift is reconciled in a migration. The grant replay step in that script is now redundant with migration 20260730120000 but is kept as a guard against future out-of-band drift.

Related: salish-6j6 covers revoking the inert anon/authenticated write grants and the `contributor_email_addresses` SELECT grant.

Reproduce the grant diff:
```
supabase db reset --no-seed
# then diff information_schema.role_table_grants for
# table_schema in ('public','dwc'), grantee in ('anon','authenticated'),
# privilege_type='SELECT'  -- prod vs local
# NB: run psql with timing OFF, or '\timing' output lands in the file and
# inflates the count by one. That artifact caused the original 15/33 figures.
```
close_reason:
Headline bug fixed and deployed: migration 20260730120000_public_select_grants.sql (PR #356, merged 2026-07-31) is applied in prod, and a fresh reset reaches grant parity (48 = 48) with the anon REST path returning 200. Acceptance criteria 1 and 2 met.

Criteria 3 (a CI guard against regression) and 4 (reconcile the two other drifts) were NOT met and are split out as salish-pee and salish-y39 rather than held open here — the reproducibility bug this issue is about is resolved.

title: iNaturalist ingest fails intermittently on live-window pagination drift (SALISHSEA-IO-2D)
description: Sentry SALISHSEA-IO-2D (escalating, ~25 events/2d, ~4% of the */5 cron runs): fetchAllObservationPages throws 'iNaturalist pagination incomplete: fetched N page(s) for total_results=X'. Root cause: the ingest window ends at current_date (today), so the dataset mutates between sequential page-number requests. total_results drifts or per-page counts stop summing to it, and isPaginationComplete (correctly) refuses the snapshot. Reproduced against the live v2/observations API. Fix: re-page the whole window a bounded number of times (transient, self-heals on a fresh pass) before throwing; keep the pure completeness invariant unchanged. Durable follow-up: switch to id-keyset pagination (order_by=id&id_above) which is atomic over a live tail and sidesteps the 10k page cap.
design: Bounded whole-fetch retry in the shell (fetch-inaturalist.ts), reusing retry.ts backoff. Only isPaginationComplete==false triggers re-page; parse/HTTP/cap errors still abort immediately per decision 011.
notes: PR #327 (branch ingest/inat-pagination-drift-retry) — bounded whole-window re-page. Awaiting CodeRabbit review before merge. Not deployed until merged to main (deploy.yml runs 'supabase functions deploy ingest').
close_reason: Fixed in PR #327, merged to main and deployed to prod (supabase functions deploy ingest succeeded, run 29068586608). Bounded whole-window re-page on pagination drift. Follow-up (id-keyset pagination) tracked separately.

title: occurrence_index matview: cheap timestamp/location lookup for stored claims
description: The occurrences view is a 4-way UNION with no usable index on its computed id, so joining it materializes the whole thing whenever consumed unfiltered. Today group_occurrences/individual_occurrences avoid this only because their stored-identifications branch has an empty outer (0 curator claims). The moment curation adds rows, even the filtered per-subject pages degrade, and ecotype_occurrences can't include stored claims at all (it dropped that branch to fix a prod timeout — decision 017 / migration 20260708040216). Fix: a small MATERIALIZED VIEW occurrence_index (id PK, observed_at, location) over public.occurrences, unique-indexed on id, refreshed on the same cron tick as occurrence_identifier_candidates. Repoint all stored-claims branches to join occurrence_index instead of occurrences. Prerequisite for the curation UI.
close_reason: occurrence_index matview shipped in PR #326 / migration 20260708052333; all stored-claims branches repointed, ecotype aggregate regained stored claims

Full page per catalog individual: designations/aliases, nicknames+stories, sex/birth/status, mother/children, matriline+pod chain, recent occurrences via occurrence_identifications rendered with obs-summary, presence-by-month grid (new SQL view), OG previews + human rewrite in Lambda@Edge, linkified identifier codes in sighting text. title: Dedicated ingest DB role for the Edge Function (least privilege)
description: Decision 011 specifies the ingest shell connects as a dedicated privileged ingest role, not the postgres superuser. Today supabase/functions/ingest/index.ts falls back to SUPABASE_DB_URL (superuser). Create an 'ingest' login role with only the grants the shell needs (mirror schemas maplify/inaturalist, ingest.runs, taxa lookup), set its password out-of-band, set INGEST_DB_URL in Edge Function secrets, verify a cron run succeeds under the new role, then remove/rotate the superuser fallback.
close_reason: Live in prod. Migration 20260706130000 (PR #311) creates least-privilege 'ingest' login role (mirror schemas, ingest.runs, collection_rule, gis USAGE, RLS policy on inaturalist.taxa). Password set out-of-band via Management API; INGEST_DB_URL edge secret set to the session-pooler DSN per decision 011. Verified: prod dry-runs of both sources OK under the role, pg_stat_activity shows usename=ingest, cron runs #28/#29 success post-flip. Superuser fallback removal split to a follow-up issue.

title: Cutover: switch pg_cron from SQL ingest to the Edge Function; remove SQL ingest path
description: Clean atomic cutover per decision 011. One migration: schedule pg_net invocation of the ingest Edge Function (Maplify + iNat) AND cron.unschedule the old load-recent-maplify-sightings / load-recent-inaturalist-observations jobs together — never two live reconcilers. Downtime acceptable (10-day windows self-heal on first new run). Validate via manual dry-run against real windows before flipping. After bake-in, remove the now-dead in-DB HTTP fetch functions (fetch_date_range, fetch_observation_page, update_sightings/update_observations HTTP paths, ensure_taxa/fetch_taxa) — Postgres keeps only storage + the pure relational views. Rollback = single migration revert.
acceptance_criteria: pg_cron invokes the Edge Function; old SQL cron jobs unscheduled in the same migration; dead in-DB HTTP fetch functions removed; live map unaffected after cutover; rollback path documented.
notes:
CUTOVER LIVE + confirmed healthy (2026-07-06). #308 merged; deploy failed once on transient Supabase link OOM (fail-safe: cron stayed on SQL), succeeded on rerun. Prod cron switched to pg_net jobs (SQL load-recent-* gone). ISSUE: pg_net not installed in prod (local stack pre-enables it) → cron failed 'schema net does not exist' ~15:00-15:10; ingest briefly down (self-healing). FIX: enabled pg_net in prod out-of-band + codified in migration 20260706120000 (PR #309). Confirmed: both sources cron-driven success in ingest.runs (maplify 277/282, inat 413), all net._http_response 200. First iNat run reconciled -17 obs (one-time drift convergence, expected). Lesson saved to memory (local-prod-extension-parity). REMAINING: retirement migration only (#309 merged; 89d.4 heartbeat shipped in #310).

BAKE-IN PLAN (2026-07-06): heartbeat (89d.4) merged + verified end-to-end; retirement migration (drop dead SQL ingest fns) intentionally deferred to ~2026-07-13 so the SQL path remains restorable during bake-in. Dedicated ingest role split to salish-wco; Sentry split to salish-vif.
RETIREMENT SHIPPED 2026-07-31 in PR #358 (merged): migration 20260731120000 drops the 9 dead Maplify/iNaturalist in-DB functions. Verified against prod first — closed dependency cluster, no cron, no triggers, Edge Function uses raw SQL and calls none of them. HappyWhale's 3 HTTP functions deliberately excluded (never part of this cutover, no ingest.runs rows, no TS replacement) — split to salish-mzz. seed.sql emptied: it called three of the dropped functions and made CI hit live third-party APIs on every build.
close_reason: Retirement shipped in PR #358 (merged 2026-07-31). Migration 20260731120000 drops the 9 dead Maplify/iNaturalist in-DB HTTP functions. HappyWhale's 3 split to salish-mzz — never part of this cutover, no ingest.runs rows, no TS replacement. seed.sql emptied, removing live third-party API calls from every CI build.

title: iNaturalist ingest: pagination + full taxon-closure resolution
description: Extend the ingest skeleton to iNaturalist, reusing the Maplify shell/core. Adds the two hard pieces: (1) pagination-completeness — fetch every page through total_results; any page failure aborts (write nothing); an empty first page (total_results=0) is complete/authoritative. (2) taxon resolution moved into TS: extract referenced taxon+ancestor ids (pure), diff against inaturalist.taxa (pure), shell loops fetch->recompute-still-missing until the full ancestor closure resolves, ALL before opening the persist txn (no HTTP inside the DB write). A taxon-API failure counts against fetch-completeness. Persist observations + observation_photos (parent/child) + taxa in one atomic txn with guarded reconcile. Implements decision 011 for iNaturalist.
acceptance_criteria: All in-scope observations in a window are ingested regardless of count; taxon FK never dangles; a partial page fetch or taxon-API failure writes nothing; vitest covers the completeness predicate, taxon-closure diff, and pagination; integration test proves observation+photo persist + reconcile bounds.
notes: Shell implemented: supabase/functions/ingest/fetch-inaturalist.ts (pagination + taxon-closure loops), index.ts branches on source. persist.ts toPhotoPayload now dedupes photos by id (live iNat shares a photo id across observations → bulk ON CONFLICT crash; caught by live run). PR #307. Live-validated: 42-page dry run (8269 results), real write, closure loop re-fetched a deleted taxon, failure paths. 283 tests green.
close_reason: Both slices merged: core+persist (#306) and Edge Function shell (#307). iNaturalist ingest runs end-to-end via the Edge Function — pagination loop + taxon-closure loop, live-validated against the real API. A third live-run bug caught (photo id reused across observations). Follow-up 1wz (fetch-maplify timeout tidy). Remaining in epic: 89d.3 cutover + deferred 89d.1 follow-ups (ingest role, Sentry).

title: Ingest skeleton + Maplify: imperative shell / functional core
description: Build the reusable ingest skeleton and prove it end-to-end on Maplify (simplest source: single-shot fetch, no pagination, no taxon graph). Deliverables: (1) functional core in scripts/ingest/ (Maplify JSON -> normalized sighting rows, coordinate parsing, reconcile diff, completeness predicate) with vitest unit tests; (2) Deno imperative shell in supabase/functions/ingest/ (fetch + minimal retry honoring Retry-After, structured console logs, Sentry Deno, dedicated-role pooled PG connection, one atomic txn: upserts + guarded reconcile DELETE bounded to window); (3) ingest_runs audit table + writes outside the data txn; (4) INGEST_TRIGGER_SECRET auth; (5) manual/dry-run invocation interface (source+window+dry_run); (6) vitest integration test on local Supabase proving reconcile touches ONLY in-window rows, upsert idempotency, abort-writes-nothing. Implements decision 011 for Maplify. Completeness invariant: non-200/error aborts and writes nothing; empty-200 reconciles authoritatively.
acceptance_criteria: Maplify ingest runs as an Edge Function on the same 5-min cadence; a failed/empty-error fetch leaves existing sightings intact; an empty-200 reconciles the window; manual re-fetch and dry-run work; ingest_runs records every run; vitest unit+integration green in CI.
notes: Slice 3 (Deno Edge Function shell) done → PR #305. supabase/functions/ingest/ (index.ts orchestration + fetch-maplify.ts retry + deno.json import map); scripts/ingest/retry.ts (pure, tested); fetchWindowIds on persist; config.toml [functions.ingest] verify_jwt=false. Live bug caught+fixed: Maplify count is a STRING not number (schema dropped count, fixture made faithful, regression test). Validated live: 401 bad secret, 405 inaturalist, dry-run (97/0 nothing written), real run idempotent, ingest.runs records success+failure. 237 tests green, deno check + tsc clean. Function is DORMANT (deploy.yml doesn't run functions deploy). FOLLOW-UPS: dedicated ingest DB role+grants (shell prefers INGEST_DB_URL); Sentry Deno wiring; then 89d.2 iNat, 89d.3 cutover (deploy fn + pg_cron→pg_net).

title: Deploy pipeline has no test gate, no rollback, and no failure alerting
description:
deploy.yml on push to main runs only 'npm run build' (deploy.yml:35). Tests, e2e, and the type-drift check live only in build.yml on pull_request, so: (a) the merge commit on main is never tested before deploy (PR checks run on the PR head, not the merge result); (b) any push reaching main outside a passing-PR path deploys with zero test verification. The deploy then runs supabase db push -> S3 sync -> CloudFront invalidation -> cdk deploy in sequence with no atomicity and no rollback — a mid-sequence failure leaves DB schema ahead of a stale frontend, or a new frontend against an old edge handler. smoke.yml runs AFTER deploy via workflow_run and only turns the run red — no alert, no issue filed.

Fix: add a test/e2e/type-drift gate to the deploy path (or enforce required PR checks + test the merge result); add post-deploy verification inside the deploy job with failure alerting; consider aligning to the dwca-nightly.yml pattern (concurrency, post-publish verify, auto-filed failure issues), which already does this well.
acceptance_criteria: A broken build cannot reach prod without a failing gate; deploy failures produce an alert/issue; post-deploy smoke gates or auto-reverts on failure.
notes: PR #368 (branch deploy-test-gate) opened 2026-08-04. Decision 024 written. Local actionlint + CodeRabbit clean. Awaiting PR checks + merge; the workflow_call wiring cannot execute until it is on main.
close_reason: PR #368 merged as f2a9ec2 and verified on the first run through the new pipeline (run 30928236183): Test/build success, Build success, Deploy success, Smoke success, Alert skipped, Resolve success. Decision 024 records the design.

title: Reconcile DwC-A go-live with its documented rights preconditions; record a go-live decision
description:
The public DwC-A download link is live (about.html), but two documented preconditions appear unmet and unrecorded:
1) rights-policy.md §1.3 (D-08) requires an explicit notice on the submission form that the observation will be published under CC-BY-NC 4.0 in a DarwinCore Archive, BEFORE the link goes live. src/sighting-form.ts only handles a PHOTO license choice — no observation-publication notice exists.
2) rights-policy.md §4.5 defines a hold requiring a Maplify data-QA pass and a 2-4 week courtesy-notification window to Conserve.IO / Orca Network / Cascadia before exit. No decision record documents the hold was exited, QA passed, or notifications sent.

This is a trust/legal item. Action: add the consent notice to the submission form; reconcile whether the hold conditions were actually met; write a numbered decision record (docs/decisions/) documenting the go-live and closing D-07/D-08. See product/docs audit.
acceptance_criteria: Submission form carries the CC-BY-NC 4.0 / DwC-A publication notice; a decision record documents go-live and the state of the §4.5 hold conditions; D-07 and D-08 closed in rights-policy.md.

title: iNaturalist ingest only fetches page 1 (200 records) — silent truncation
description:
inaturalist.update_observations calls fetch_observation_page(from, to, bbox, taxa, 1, 200) with no pagination loop (supabase/migrations/20260526000000_inat_add_lutrinae.sql:6-13) and ignores the total_results the function already exposes (20260621010000_inat_orcid_capture.sql:44). Any 10-day window with >200 in-scope observations silently drops the overflow. Latent at current volume but an unguarded correctness cliff, and higher risk now that taxonomic scope expanded to all marine mammals (decision 009 added Lutrinae).

VERIFIED against source. Fix in-place: loop pages until fetched >= total_results (or last page empty). Superseded long-term by the TS ingest migration (salish-89d).
acceptance_criteria: All in-scope observations in the window are ingested regardless of count; pagination continues until total_results is satisfied.
close_reason: Fixed in-place: inaturalist.update_observations now paginates through total_results instead of fetching only page 1 (migration 20260705120000). Verified via mock: 450 results → 3 pages/450 rows; empty window → 0 upserts; exactly-200 → 1 page (no infinite loop). Superseded long-term by salish-89d.

title: Maplify ingest deletes ~10 days of live sightings on any failed/empty upstream fetch
description:
maplify.update_sightings runs every 5 minutes over current_date-10..current_date (supabase/migrations/20250914232212_cron.sql:159). Its MERGE ends with 'WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE AND s.created_at BETWEEN $1 AND ($2+1) THEN DELETE' (supabase/migrations/20260620000200_resolution_ingest.sql:141-143). The MERGE source is maplify.fetch_date_range, filtered 'WHERE status = 200' (20250904165159_fetch_data.sql:186). Any non-200 (500/403/rate-limit) or a 200 with an empty results array yields ZERO source rows, so every sighting in the 10-day window becomes NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE and is DELETED. Runs every 5 min, so a transient Maplify outage repeatedly wipes ~10 days of sightings from the live map until Maplify recovers. Self-heals on next good fetch; the nightly export row-floor guard prevents a near-empty archive, so damage is to the live site, not the DwC-A.

VERIFIED against source. The older BEGIN ATOMIC definition (fetch_data.sql) has the same flaw (unconditional DELETE then INSERT).

Fix: guard the reconciliation/DELETE on a confirmed successful, non-empty fetch — distinguish 'upstream returned no rows' (do nothing / skip delete) from 'upstream genuinely removed these rows'. Superseded long-term by the TS ingest migration (salish-89d), but fix in-place now.
acceptance_criteria: A failed or empty Maplify fetch leaves existing sightings intact; DELETE only occurs when the fetch demonstrably succeeded and returned the authoritative set for the window.
close_reason: Fixed in-place: maplify.update_sightings now guards the reconcile DELETE on a successful, non-empty fetch (migration 20260705120000). Verified via mock-based transactional test — failed/empty fetch leaves sightings intact (2 survivors each); a good fetch still reconciles (update/insert/delete-absent). Superseded long-term by salish-89d.

title: Migrate network ingest from Postgres into a TypeScript imperative shell / functional core
description:
Today all external network ingest (Maplify, iNaturalist) runs INSIDE Postgres: pg_cron schedules SQL functions that use the http extension to fetch upstream JSON and MERGE it into tables (supabase/migrations/20250914232212_cron.sql, 20250904165159_fetch_data.sql, 20260620000200_resolution_ingest.sql). This concentrates network I/O, control flow, taxon mapping, dedup, and destructive writes in an environment with no exception handling, no structured logging, no retry/backoff, no test harness, and dangerous failure modes (see the Maplify blind-DELETE and iNat single-page bugs filed alongside this epic).

Goal: move network operations into a TypeScript IMPERATIVE SHELL (fetch, retry/backoff, structured logging, Sentry, success-guarded persistence, orchestration) wrapping a FUNCTIONAL RELATIONAL CORE of pure, unit-testable transforms (upstream JSON -> normalized records, taxon mapping, coordinate parsing, dedup, collection resolution). Postgres becomes a store, not an HTTP client. A fetch that fails or returns empty must NEVER be interpreted as 'upstream deleted everything' — writes are guarded on a confirmed successful fetch.

This is a priority architectural direction. The two data-loss bugs are the concrete motivation; fix those in-place first (they are urgent), then this epic supersedes the SQL ingest path entirely.

Scope to define in child issues: runner/host (scheduled GitHub Action vs Supabase Edge Function vs small worker), how state/cron moves off pg_cron, idempotent upsert strategy from TS, and a test suite for the functional core.
design: Imperative shell = effects (fetch, retry, log, persist, schedule). Functional core = pure transforms over plain data, exhaustively unit-tested. Replace blind 'WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE' with reconciliation only after a verified-complete fetch. Structured logs + Sentry breadcrumbs on every ingest run; per-source success/failure/rowcount metrics. Keep Postgres for storage + the pure relational views (occurrences, segments) that are legitimately declarative.
notes: Design resolved via grilling session 2026-07-05 → docs/decisions/011-ingest-imperative-shell.md. Host: Supabase Edge Function (Deno), scheduled by pg_cron+pg_net every 5 min, also a manually-invocable curator endpoint (source+window+dry_run). Persist: direct pooled connection as dedicated ingest role, parameterized SQL in TS, one atomic txn for upserts+reconcile, ingest_runs audit row outside it. Safety invariant: reconcile iff fetch provably complete (all pages + iNat taxon closure); non-200/partial aborts and writes nothing; empty-200 is authoritative. Scope: Maplify then iNat; HappyWhale out (pending integration green light). Retry: minimal in-invocation, honor Retry-After. Auth: dedicated INGEST_TRIGGER_SECRET. Tests: vitest only (unit core + local-Supabase integration for persist/delete-bounds); no pgTAP. Cutover: clean atomic switch, downtime fine (10-day windows self-heal). Core lives in scripts/ingest/ (vitest), shell in supabase/functions/ingest/.
close_reason:
All 4 children complete. Ingest for Maplify and iNaturalist now runs in the Edge Function (TypeScript imperative shell / functional core), scheduled via pg_cron + pg_net, with a heartbeat alert; the in-DB HTTP path was retired in PR #358 (migration 20260731120000). Postgres keeps storage and pure relational views, per decision 011.

Remaining tail, deliberately outside this epic: HappyWhale's 3 in-DB HTTP functions (salish-mzz). HappyWhale was never part of this migration — no ingest.runs rows, never scheduled — so whether it stays a source at all is the prior question.

title: Rich preview fails with CloudFront error for shared occurrence links
description: Sharing https://salishsea.io/?o=inaturalist:377539157 to Facebook renders a broken preview: 'ERROR: The request could not be satisfied' (the standard CloudFront error page). This is the Lambda@Edge OG-meta rich-preview path (docs/decisions/002), which is specified to FAIL OPEN (pass through on any error) — so either that regressed or the failure is a Lambda execution error/timeout CloudFront surfaces as 502/504. Hypothesis to check first: breakage is specific to iNaturalist-prefixed occurrence IDs (inaturalist:NNN) — iNat is modeled-but-export-excluded per SRC-01 (decision 005), so the edge lookup may hit a code path that throws instead of failing open. Repro: crawler user-agent (facebookexternalhit) against the ?o= URL.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed, not iNat-specific): the Lambda@Edge handler (infra/lib/edge-handler/index.ts) intercepts crawler requests on ALL paths except its bypass list (/dwca/, /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt — lines 119-125). og:image is https://salishsea.io/preview.jpg (FALLBACK_IMAGE, line 106). When Facebook's crawler fetches that image URL, the handler has no ?o=, so it returns generic OG *HTML* (lines 137-143) instead of the JPEG. Confirmed: /preview.jpg returns image/jpeg 168717B to a browser UA but text/html 896B to facebookexternalhit. Blast radius: every preview whose og:image falls back to preview.jpg — the generic site card AND any occurrence with no open-licensed (cc0/cc-by) photo, which includes this iNat river-otter. Occurrences with an external open photo URL have an off-host og:image and are unaffected, which is why it wasn't universally caught. FIX: add static image assets to the pre-bot bypass so crawlers always get raw asset bytes (e.g. bypass when request.uri matches /\.(jpe?g|png|gif|svg|webp|ico|avif)$/i). Note: index.test.ts lines 94-162 assert og:image==preview.jpg but never assert preview.jpg itself serves an image — add a regression test that a crawler request to /preview.jpg passes through (returns the request, not synthesized HTML).
Fixed via PR #299 (merged to main, deployed by GH Actions run 28626380144, both Build+Deploy green). Verified live 2026-07-02: /preview.jpg returns image/jpeg 168717B to facebookexternalhit (was text/html 896B); occurrence OG HTML still generated correctly; home page still intercepted. Remaining human step: re-scrape shared links in FB Sharing Debugger to bust cache.

title: Expand scope from cetaceans to all Salish Sea marine mammals (PSEMP)
description:
PRODUCT.md and docs/decisions/001 currently scope the platform to cetaceans only; actual intent is all Salish Sea marine mammals per the PSEMP Marine Mammals Workgroup hub (https://psemp-marinemammalsworkgroup-wa-psp.hub.arcgis.com/): cetaceans + pinnipeds (harbor seal, CA/Steller sea lion, N elephant seal) + otters (sea + marine-foraging river otter). The Lutrinae taxon already hand-added to the iNaturalist query is an early instance.

Open decisions (for a grill-with-docs session, not this migration PR):
- Does 'include everything from PSEMP' mean widen species scope only, or also ingest PSEMP's ArcGIS datasets as a new provider/collection?
- Product identity: reframe as marine-mammal platform, or whale-centric with mammals included?
- Rights: PSEMP data is CC-BY-NC-SA; ShareAlike may be incompatible with the CC-BY-NC export contract (docs/rights-policy.md) if PSEMP records are ingested + redistributed. Resolve at the policy gate before any SQL.

Doc updates gated on the above: PRODUCT.md (What This Is, core value, Out of Scope), supersede docs/decisions/001, CONTEXT.md (model pinnipeds/otters; 'occurrence' currently cetacean-defined; segment travel-speed heuristics don't generalize to hauled-out seals). Implementation gaps: taxon filters across all four ingest sources; species/UI; export attribution + SRC-01-style logic for any PSEMP provider.
close_reason: All three open decisions resolved in decision 027 (grill session 2026-08-13); doc/metadata/copy migration landed in PR #386. Haul-out clustering split out as salish-szv / GH #385.

title: Discovery conversations with Orca Network (Garrett & Berta)
description: The community-uptake direction rests on a partner we don't yet understand — next move is discovery, not engineering. Interview questions: docs/strategy/orca-network-discovery-questions.md (curation workflow & pain; would they value/advocate a map-first tool; Acartia data-flow granularity; does the research-impact story land; what would make them say no).
