title: Filter out-of-scope sightings in isIngestable, and purge the existing ones
description:
Add the scope predicate to public.occurrences: keep a record if it falls inside the Salish
Sea + Strait of Juan de Fuca extent, OR its taxon is a killer whale.

Deletes nothing. maplify.sightings keeps every record Maplify returned for the bbox we
asked for, which is what makes it a mirror; scope becomes a property of our domain.

WATCH
  - The extent must be one definition, not a literal copy-pasted into a view. src/constants.ts
    holds salishSeaExtent for the frontend; the database needs the same numbers without
    the two drifting.
  - Killer whale detection has to survive the taxon being a subspecies (Orcinus orca ater,
    O. o. rectipinnus) and the genus-only stub (Orcinus).
  - The view is already three levels deep in dependents; CREATE OR REPLACE, never DROP.
  - Blocked on the decision record: this changes what the archive publishes.
notes:
SUPERSEDES the view-side approach described above. With deletion acceptable, the filter
belongs in isIngestable: a pure predicate, unit-testable, keeping the data out rather than
hiding it. Precedent is right there — isIngestable already drops the rwsas and wras
sources, and CONTEXT.md records that wras was 'filtered + purged', which is exactly the
shape of this change.

Then one deliberate purge of the ~17,620 existing out-of-scope non-orca records, so the
corpus is not split by the date the filter shipped.

Killer whale detection still has to survive a subspecies (Orcinus orca ater,
O. o. rectipinnus) and the genus-only stub, and it has to work from the NORMALIZED
sighting — isIngestable sees scientific_name and name, not a resolved taxon, so it cannot
consult the taxonomy. Matching 'Orcinus' plus the killer-whale common names is the
available signal, and the same NAME_TO_SCIENTIFIC vocabulary the resolver already uses.
close_reason: isIngestable scope rule + purge migration 20260830200000, PR #419; 14,146 rows in prod, applies on merge

title: Decide and record the ingest scope rule
description:
Write the decision record for "killer whales range-wide, everything else the Salish Sea".

MUST CAPTURE
  - Why the bbox reaches 36N at all: the southern end of the Southern Resident range. It
    is not an accident and should not be narrowed without replacing what it was for.
  - That SRKW cannot be identified at ingest — 6 of 299 out-of-region orca records name
    the ecotype — so the rule is necessarily "killer whales", and say so plainly rather
    than implying we filter to Southern Residents.
  - Why the filter belongs in public.occurrences and not in isIngestable: reconcile would
    delete 174 in-window records and leave a corpus split by date; the mirror should stay
    a faithful record of what upstream returned for what we asked (decision 008).
  - The export consequence, since dwc reads public.occurrences.
  - Where the Salish Sea + Strait of Juan de Fuca boundary comes from. src/constants.ts
    already has salishSeaExtent [-126, 47, -122, 50.5]; decisions 022 and 023 are about
    framing versus filtering and should be reconciled with this rather than duplicated.
close_reason: Decision 036 written (docs/decisions/036-ingest-scope-killer-whales-range-wide.md), PR #419

title: Ingest scope: killer whales range-wide, everything else the Salish Sea
description:
The Maplify ingest bbox is -136,36,-120,54 — from central California to northern BC. That
is deliberate: it covers the southern end of the Southern Resident range. The side effect
is that 39% of what we hold from Maplify is outside the Salish Sea and has nothing to do
with Southern Residents.

Measured against the live feed 2026-08-28 (45,694 records in the bbox):

  inside Salish Sea + JdF [-126,47,-122,50.5]   27,775   60.8%
  outside                                       17,919   39.2%
    of which killer whales of any kind             299
    everything else                             17,620   <- out of scope
      6,785 Humpback · 3,385 Gray Whale · 2,049 Unspecified · 1,899 Humpback Whale ...

THE RULE: consume killer whales from their full range, everything else only from the
Strait of Juan de Fuca and the Salish Sea.

A CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES THE DESIGN: you cannot filter to SRKW at ingest. Only 6 of those
299 orca records name "Southern Resident"; the rest say "Killer Whale (Orca)" with no
ecotype, and no report reliably carries one. So the implementable rule is killer whales,
and the SRKW intent is served by keeping all orcas rather than by identifying them.

WHERE THE FILTER GOES — the important call. Not in isIngestable. It runs before reconcile,
and reconcile deletes any stored id in the window that is not in the fetch, so filtering
there would delete 174 existing records on the first run (a rolling 10-day window) and
leave a corpus with out-of-region records before a date and none after. Filtering
public.occurrences instead deletes nothing, keeps maplify.sightings a faithful mirror of
what we asked upstream for (decision 008), puts scope in our domain where 008 says
translation belongs, and is reversible if the scope ever widens.

CONSEQUENCE THAT MUST BE DELIBERATE: the dwc schema reads public.occurrences — 4 of its 6
relations do — so filtering there changes what the DarwinCore Archive publishes. That is
arguably the point, since the archive should not claim Californian humpbacks under a
Salish Sea remit, but it touches decision 027's coverage statements and rights-policy
§6.5 and cannot be a silent side effect.

Not urgent: decision 022 already filters the map by region, so these records are not
visible today unless a user selects Everywhere. The cost is what we hold and what we
publish, not map noise.
notes:
CONSTRAINTS RELAXED (2026-08-28, from the owner): nobody consumes the DwC-A export yet,
and deleting records is acceptable at this stage.

That removes the premise the 'where does the filter go' reasoning above was built on. I
argued for filtering public.occurrences specifically to avoid deleting 174 in-window
records and to dodge the export consequence. Neither is a real cost right now, so the
simpler design wins:

  1. Filter in isIngestable — a pure predicate over a normalized sighting, unit-testable,
     no SQL, and it stops the data arriving rather than hiding it after the fact.
  2. Purge the existing out-of-scope non-orca records in one deliberate pass, so the
     corpus is consistent rather than split by the date the filter shipped.

This also resolves the decision-008 tension I raised. The mirror is ALREADY a filtered
subset: isIngestable excludes the rwsas and wras sources today, and CONTEXT.md documents
that ('rwsas filtered, wras filtered + purged'). Scope filtering at ingest is the same
move as an existing, documented one — not a new departure.

The export child stays worth doing, but as follow-up rather than a gate.

2026-08-30: PR #419 implements .1/.2/.3 (branch ingest-scope-a4y). Merging it deploys the purge (14,146 rows) — the owner's merge is the go-ahead. Adversarial review found the premise was Maplify-only: iNaturalist fetches the same Acartia box unfiltered, so 'everything else the Salish Sea' is true of Maplify only until salish-a4y.4 is decided.

2026-08-31: PR #419 MERGED as f71db9a (squash); deploy run 33347561391 applies the purge to prod. Remaining child: salish-a4y.4 (iNaturalist scope). Epic closes when that is decided.
close_reason: All four children closed: a4y.1 (rule + decision 036), a4y.2 (isIngestable + Maplify purge), a4y.3 (DwC-A coverage restated), a4y.4 (iNaturalist gets the same rule + 51,637-row purge, decision 044, PR #463, deployed and verified 2026-09-18). The epic's own measurement — 39% of Maplify out of scope — is superseded by what shipped: Maplify purged 2026-08-30, iNaturalist 2026-09-18, and both ingests now enforce the rule at parse. HappyWhale ingest is off; if it is ever turned on it needs the same predicate, which decision 044 says.

title: Nothing loads the register in production, and nothing notices it is empty
description:
From the adversarial review of #398.

Merging and deploying creates the `register` schema and rewrites public.occurrences, but
leaves register.* EMPTY. The view LEFT JOINs, so every name silently falls back to
iNaturalist and the map reads exactly as before. The 84.9% headline reads 0% in production
until a human remembers to run:

  npx tsx scripts/register/load.ts --tag <tag> --emit-sql > /tmp/register.sql
  npx supabase db query --linked "$(cat /tmp/register.sql)"

A graceful fallback is right — a failed load must not blank the map — but it also means
the failure mode is invisible. Nothing checks that register.edition is populated, or that
its tag matches the register's latest release.

WORTH DOING
  - Load as part of deploy, or a scheduled job like the animals crosswalk check.
  - An assertion somewhere that register.edition exists and register.entities is non-empty,
    so "the register never loaded" cannot masquerade as "the register has no name for this
    animal".
  - Optionally compare register.edition.tag against the latest release tag and warn when
    behind. The register is cut on demand, possibly several times a day, so drift is
    expected rather than exceptional.

Note the deploy already ships an Edge Function and runs db push, so there is a natural
place for it. Related: salish-ayb.5, salish-4hq (nothing re-asks iNaturalist either).
notes: Closed by #413, merged as dd3a7e2 and deployed 2026-08-30. Verified in the wild on the deploy's own Register job: resolved 2026.08.1, digest a4504ce1d1b801bd, loaded 699 entities, then verify reported 699/684/43, coverage 58,733 of 64,170 (91.5%), edition current, 'register ok'. Daily cron at 11:00 UTC plus every deploy; workflow_dispatch takes a tag to pin or roll back.
close_reason: Closed

title: Subspecies keep iNaturalist's display name; the register has no exactMatch for them
description:
salish-ayb.5 resolves display names through the register by EXACT iNaturalist taxon id,
covering 84.9% of occurrences. The remainder is almost entirely subspecies, and the result
is visible on one screen: a 2026-07-25 map shows "Harbour seal" (register) beside "Pacific
Harbor Seal" (iNaturalist) — the same animal under two names.

  Orcinus orca ater              Resident Killer Whale          4342
  Phoca vitulina richardii       Pacific Harbor Seal            3398
  Orcinus orca rectipinnus       Bigg's Killer Whale             572
  Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira  North Pacific Humpback Whale    318
  Enhydra lutris kenyoni         Northern Sea Otter              179
  Lontra canadensis pacifica     Western River Otter              55

WHY NOT JUST RESOLVE UP TO THE SPECIES

Because it loses a real distinction. Orcinus orca ater is not "Killer whale" to this
audience — decision 029 wants SRKW and Biggs on the map, which is MORE specific than the
species, not less.

WHY NOT CROSSWALK THE REGISTER'S ECOTYPES TO THESE SUBSPECIES

Tempting and not obviously right, which is why salish-ayb.5 left it alone. The register
has SSA:0000001 Southern Resident and SSA:0000002 Bigg's, both ecotypes, both currently
skos:broadMatch to NCBITaxon:9733 with no iNaturalist mapping. Mapping SSA:0000001 to
iNat's Orcinus orca ater as an exactMatch would be WRONG: ater is the resident subspecies
generally, which includes Northern and Alaskan residents, while Southern Resident is one
population within it. That is a broadMatch, and salish-ayb.5 deliberately resolves only
exactMatch so a wider claim never reaches the map. Bigg's/rectipinnus is closer but the
register calls one an ecotype and iNaturalist calls the other a subspecies; closeMatch is
probably the honest predicate.

So the options, in ascending order of correctness and effort:

 1. Add subspecies taxon entities to the register (SSA:00009xx, kind=taxon) with
    exactMatch crosswalks. Mechanical, and it says nothing about ecotypes.
 2. Give the ecotypes closeMatch crosswalks and teach the view to use them, accepting a
    named exception to the exactMatch-only rule.
 3. Leave it, and let the short-form map labels of salish-ayb.6 normalise the display
    instead — they are ours to compose (animals ADR-0011) and could render both under one
    string without the register asserting anything.

A curator decision for the register owner, not a code change to guess at. Related:
salish-ayb.5, salish-ayb.6, docs/decisions/029-map-symbology.md, animals ADR-0008.
notes:
EXPERT INPUT (2026-08-29, relayed by Peter): Dave Bain's position is
that `ater` and `rectipinnus` are SPECIES, not subspecies.

That is not an outlier, and it changes which of the three options is even
available. Checked against the authorities directly on 2026-08-29:

  NCBI      genus Orcinus (9732) contains ONLY Orcinus orca (9733). Zero
            children under 9733 — no `ater`, no `rectipinnus`, under either
            the binomial or the trinomial. Verified via E-utilities esearch
            and txid9733[Next Level].
  WoRMS     Orcinus orca (AphiaID 137102) accepted. No `ater`, no
            `rectipinnus` at all — not even as unaccepted names. The genus
            carries only glacialis, nanus and three unaccepted subspecies.
  ITIS      Orcinus ater      TSN 1227935, rank SPECIES, usage VALID
            Orcinus rectipinnus TSN 1227934, rank SPECIES, usage VALID
  CoL       Both accepted at species rank.
  GBIF      Backbone does NOT accept either (a match on `Orcinus ater`
            returns NONE; `rectipinnus` fuzzy-matches Orcinus rectipinna as a
            SYNONYM), but the Morin et al. checklist "Revised taxonomy of
            eastern North Pacific killer whales" is registered as a dataset.

So the split is adopted by ITIS and Catalogue of Life and not yet by NCBI,
WoRMS or the GBIF backbone. iNaturalist has taken a third position again — it
holds them as SUBSPECIES (taxa 1602531 `Orcinus orca ater`, 1602533
`Orcinus orca rectipinnus`, both active, both children of 41521), which is the
rank our mirror and therefore our data carries today.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE THREE OPTIONS

  1. Add SUBSPECIES entities — still dead, and now for a second reason. There
     is no NCBI concept (ADR-0008's requirement), and if Bain, ITIS and CoL are
     right then the rank itself is wrong: a subspecies entity would encode
     iNaturalist's contested opinion permanently, in identifiers ADR-0002 makes
     unreusable.
  2. closeMatch on the ecotypes — unchanged, and still refused by ADR-0008 in
     as many words: an ecotype "is not a taxonomic rank ... not a subspecies and
     not making any claim about formal taxonomy. That distinction matters if
     anything here is ever exported to GBIF." We do export to GBIF.
  3. Leave it to presentation — done for now, see below.

  4. NEW, and the one Bain's input opens: add SPECIES entities `Orcinus ater`
     and `Orcinus rectipinnus`, delegating to ITIS (TSN 1227935 / 1227934)
     rather than NCBI. ADR-0008 says "an external authority" and names NCBI and
     WoRMS as examples, not as a closed list — but every one of the register's
     699 entities currently uses an `NCBITaxon:` id, so admitting a second
     authority is a register decision with consequences beyond these two
     animals, and it should be recorded rather than slipped in. It would also
     need a crosswalk predicate to iNaturalist's SUBSPECIES taxa, which are a
     different rank: closeMatch, not exactMatch, and so still outside the view's
     exactMatch-only rule.

DONE IN THE MEANTIME (option 3, deliberately in the presentation layer):
SUBSPECIES_FORMS in src/symbology.ts composes "Resident killer whale" and
"Bigg's killer whale" for the two subspecies, so the observation list stops
showing iNaturalist's Title Case beside the register's sentence case. Keyed on
scientific_name because there is no SSA: identifier to key on. This is a
holding position that costs nothing if option 4 lands — the table is deleted
and the entity_id path takes over.

STILL OPEN, and now the actual question for the register owner: does the
register adopt the species split (option 4, ITIS-delegated), and does it accept
a non-NCBI taxon authority to do it? Note this interacts with Q1
(salish-sea/animals#1, is Southern Resident an ecotype or a community of the
Resident ecotype) and Q27 (#22): if `ater` becomes a species, "Resident" stops
being an ecotype label and becomes a species vernacular, and the ecotype layer
below it has to be re-read.

NOT COVERED by the presentation fix: the ~450 genus and family fallbacks whose
iNaturalist vernacular is a plural or a clade description — "Steller Sea Lions",
"Humpback Whales", "Pilot Whales and allies", "California, Galápagos, and
Japanese Sea Lions", and "Pinnipeds" (the misnomer decision 027 records). Those
need their own answer; a sentence-case transform does not fix a plural.
PRIOR DISCUSSION FOUND (2026-08-29). It is salish-sea/animals#1 (Q1), owner
"S. Veirs, D. Bain" — not orcahello, which has nothing on this in its git
history or its issues.

Q1 already records Bain's position verbatim:

  "Resident and Bigg's killer whales have been proposed as Orcinus ater and
   Orcinus rectipinnus, and D. Bain holds that keeping them as one species is
   not scientifically justifiable."

TWO THINGS THAT MATTER FOR THIS ISSUE.

1. Q1'S PREMISE IS NOW STALE. It says, checked 2026-07-28: "Neither NCBI
   Taxonomy nor WoRMS has adopted the split ... so there is not yet an
   identifier to point a crosswalk at." True of those two, and still true —
   re-verified 2026-08-29. But ITIS and Catalogue of Life HAVE adopted it:
   Orcinus ater TSN 1227935 and Orcinus rectipinnus TSN 1227934, both rank
   SPECIES, both usage VALID. So the stated blocker — no identifier to point at
   — no longer holds, and the "two-row edit" Q1 anticipates is available now
   rather than someday. What it costs is admitting a non-NCBI taxon authority;
   all 699 entities use NCBITaxon: today.

2. Q1 ALREADY MAKES THE ARGUMENT BEHIND salish-frk, independently: "Under a
   species split, 'resident' is the species and SRKW and NRKW are populations
   within it." That is exactly why labelling every `ater` record SRKW was
   wrong. Q1 calls this option (a), and says it is "robust to both outcomes"
   while the colloquial option (b) "would be actively wrong if the split were
   adopted".

ALSO FROM Q1, and not previously noted here: the register has "Southern
Resident" entered TWICE at two different ranks — SSA:0000001 (ecotype) and
SSA:0000010 (community) — while the Resident ecotype does not exist at all.
Q1 identifies that as the cause of the graph break, not a separate bug. Any
crosswalk work here has to land after that is settled, or it will crosswalk one
of two duplicates.

CORROBORATION FROM THE PRODUCT SIDE: salishsea-io#78 (Scott Veirs, 2025-08-07,
closed), which predates the register, asked for both halves of what shipped in
#412 — "I've dropped the capitalization for all classes ... except for the
first letter" (the sentence case SUBSPECIES_FORMS applies) and "I also propose
specifying Southern vs Northern for resident killer whales, since the former is
very common within the Salish Sea, and the latter is quite rare" (the
distinction the SRKW over-claim was erasing).

NOT SEARCHED: Zulip. No CLI, no ~/.zuliprc and no token on this machine, so it
could not be checked from here. If the discussion continued there, it is the
one source not covered.
THE PRIOR DISCUSSION, FOUND IN ZULIP (2026-08-29). Not orcahello — nothing
there. It is orcasound.zulipchat.com, stream acartia-data-cooperative, topic
"iNaturalist integration", 2025-02-20/21, Scott Veirs and Peter Abrahamsen. It
contains a fact that none of our notes, and neither animals#1 nor ADR-0008,
had captured, and it REVERSES the recommendation made here on 2026-08-29.

  Scott Veirs, 2025-02-21: "I was surprised to find the Bigg's ecotype as a
  'species' option. I wonder if this is related to the recent proposal to
  declare the ecotypes separate species, which seems to have FIZZLED since last
  summer/fall into using the proposed scientific names to describe SUBSPECIES
  of Orcinus orca."

Verified against the source he links, the Society for Marine Mammalogy Taxonomy
Committee's 2024 Annual Review (2024-09-09), which is the authority for marine
mammal taxonomy and the reason iNaturalist holds the trinomials:

  "Although Morin et al. (2024) proposed their recognition as distinct species
  of killer whales, such proposal was NOT FOLLOWED by the Taxonomy Committee
  because there were concerns whether this represents a species- or
  subspecies-level designation. The reasons were mainly due to (1) a possible
  episodic gene flow among the ecotypes, and (2) the need to conduct a more
  comprehensive comparative analysis on a global scale ... Therefore, pending
  further investigation ..., the two ecotypes are considered PROVISIONALLY as
  distinct subspecies of Orcinus orca and named following Morin et al. (2024)."

WHAT THIS DOES TO OPTION 4. The note added earlier today proposed adding
SPECIES entities delegating to ITIS (TSN 1227935 / 1227934), on the strength of
Bain's position plus ITIS and Catalogue of Life. RETRACT THAT RECOMMENDATION.
The field's own taxonomy committee considered the species rank, gave two
specific reasons for declining it, and adopted the names at subspecies rank
provisionally. ITIS and CoL are the outliers for this clade, not the vanguard,
and the register would be picking the losing side of a live dispute in
identifiers ADR-0002 makes permanent and ADR-0010 makes unreusable.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY RIGHT. ADR-0008 already says it: taxon_id is "a record of
where the authorities place a thing, not a belief". The authorities disagree —
SMM and iNaturalist say subspecies-for-now, ITIS and CoL say species, Bain and
Morin et al. say species — and the register's job is not to arbitrate. The
honest options remain (3), presentation, which shipped in #412, and doing
nothing in the register until SMM revisits. If SMM later elevates them, ITIS is
already there and the crosswalk is the two-row edit animals#1 anticipates.

The presentation fix is rank-agnostic and survives either outcome: "Resident
killer whale" and "Bigg's killer whale" are correct whether these are species
or subspecies, and `ater` is a wider concept than SRKW under both readings, so
salish-frk stands too.

SECOND FINDING FROM THE SAME REVIEW, and it touches this issue's data directly:
the proposal to elevate Delphinus delphis bairdii to species (Jefferson et al.
2024) FAILED to reach the required 2/3 majority, "mainly due to the lack of
nuclear DNA evidence". It remains a subspecies. We hold 51 occurrences of it,
displayed as "Eastern Pacific Long-beaked Common Dolphin" — the same shape of
problem as the orca subspecies, with the same answer.
DECIDED 2026-08-29 (Peter): settle animals Q1 as option (a), then
crosswalk the ecotypes to iNaturalist's subspecies. Option 1 (presentation
only, shipped in #412) becomes the interim rather than the end state; option 2
(mint subspecies entities) is dead; the ITIS species route retracted earlier
today stays dead.

THE ARGUMENT, in one line: the Society for Marine Mammalogy's 2024 review — the
same document that DECLINED species rank — writes "the two ecotypes are
considered provisionally as distinct subspecies of Orcinus orca". The authority
itself equates these ecotypes with these subspecies, so a register crosswalk
records what SMM already says rather than asserting a taxonomy of its own,
which is what ADR-0008 was guarding against.

WHY THE RANK DISPUTE DOES NOT GATE THIS. SMM says subspecies provisionally;
Bain and Morin et al. say species; ITIS and CoL say species; NCBI and WoRMS say
nothing. ADR-0008 already frames taxon_id as "a record of where the authorities
place a thing, not a belief". A closeMatch between coextensive concepts is true
under either rank, so nothing here has to be revisited if SMM later elevates
them.

SEQUENCE. Q1 is the gate, not this issue: there is currently NO register entity
corresponding to iNaturalist's `ater`. "Southern Resident" exists twice
(SSA:0000001 ecotype, SSA:0000010 community), the Resident ecotype does not
exist at all, and SSA:0000010 has no membership row pointing up — the graph
break Q1 diagnoses. Crosswalking `ater` to SSA:0000001 would re-introduce, in
the data layer, exactly the SRKW-for-ater narrowing that salish-frk removed
from the map.

EXPECTED RESULT: register name coverage 91.5% -> ~99.3% (58,669 -> 63,640 of
64,097 occurrences), SUBSPECIES_FORMS deleted from src/symbology.ts, and every
name on the map sourced from the register.

BLAST RADIUS UPSTREAM, measured 2026-08-29: five rows reference SSA:0000001
(entities, two names, one membership, one mapping) and two reference
SSA:0000010. deprecations.tsv is still header-only, so this is its first use.
SSA:0000003 is free and sits in the ecotype block.
close_reason:
Done and verified in prod 2026-09-21. Every subspecies in the corpus now takes the register's name: Orcinus orca ater, O. o. rectipinnus, Phoca vitulina richardii, Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira, Enhydra lutris kenyoni and Lontra canadensis pacifica all resolve. Coverage 99.71%, and the 'Harbour seal beside Pacific Harbor Seal on one screen' complaint this issue opened with is gone.

Route taken was option 2 of the three this issue listed — give the ecotypes closeMatch crosswalks and teach the view to use them — but not in the shape the issue imagined. The issue assumed that meant 'a named exception to the exactMatch-only rule'. It did not: the register minted a RESIDENT ecotype (SSA:0000003, Q1) that is coextensive with ater, so no exception was needed and SSA:0000010 Southern Resident was never crosswalked. The issue's own warning — that mapping Southern Resident to ater would be a broadMatch and wrong — is still correct and is still honoured.

WHAT IS LEFT IS A DIFFERENT PROBLEM and has no issue yet. 183 occurrences (0.29%) are genus/family stubs showing iNaturalist's plural or clade description: 'Steller Sea Lions' (51), 'New World River Otters' (14), 'California, Galapagos, and Japanese Sea Lions' (13), 'Oceanic Dolphins and Porpoises' (11), 'common seals' (10), 'Porpoises' (9), 'Humpback Whales' (8), and Orcinus with no vernacular at all (9, falls back to the group label 'Killer whale'). Decision 033 called these out as needing a different answer. File one if it matters; they are a naming question for the register (does it want entities at genus/family rank?), not a crosswalk question.

title: [bug] A retired taxon aborts the whole iNaturalist ingest run
description:
`taxaUrl` (supabase/functions/ingest/fetch-inaturalist.ts) builds
`/v2/taxa?id=<comma-list>`. On /taxa the `id=` QUERY PARAM filters to ACTIVE taxa: a
retired id comes back as `total_results: 0`, with nothing to indicate it exists. The
`/taxa/{ids}` PATH form returns the same taxon flagged `is_active: false` with
`current_synonymous_taxon_ids`. Both v1 and v2 behave this way — it is the route, not the
version.

`resolveTaxonClosure` treats "requested but not returned" as unresolvable and THROWS:

    iNaturalist taxon closure unresolved: N taxa not returned

and the docstring is explicit that this counts against completeness, so the shell writes
nothing. A single referenced taxon retired since the last run therefore aborts the entire
ingest, not just that record.

Verified live 2026-08-28 with taxon 1368491 (Sagmatias obliquidens, retired in favour of
1664971):

    v2 /taxa?id=1368491      -> total_results 0, empty
    v2 /taxa/1368491         -> is_active false, current_synonymous_taxon_ids [1664971]
    v2 /taxa/1368491,41777   -> both returned; the path form takes comma-separated ids

HOW LIKELY IS IT

Not high, and not negligible. iNaturalist reassigns observations to the successor when it
retires a taxon (`/observations?taxon_id=1368491` returns 0), so an incoming observation
normally references a live taxon. The exposure is the window between a retirement and the
reassignment finishing, and any observation whose taxon is retired while our fetch is in
flight. Nine retirements have accumulated over the mirror's lifetime, so the event itself
is not rare.

FIX

Switch `taxaUrl` to the path form — `${TAXA_URL}/${ids.join(',')}?fields=…` — which takes
the same comma list and returns retired taxa.

That alone is not enough: `TAXA_FIELDS`
(supabase/functions/ingest/fetch-inaturalist.ts:86) projects only
`(id,ancestor_ids,parent_id,rank,name,preferred_common_name)`, so a retired taxon would
come back with nothing to distinguish it from a live one. The projection needs
`is_active` and `current_synonymous_taxon_ids`, and `NormalizedTaxon`
(scripts/ingest/inaturalist.ts:201) needs the corresponding fields — it carries neither
today.

The storage side is already in place: migration 20260828000000_taxa_deactivation.sql
shipped `inaturalist.taxa.is_active` and `current_taxon_id`, with
`CHECK (current_taxon_id IS NULL OR NOT is_active)`. So the closure can store a retired
taxon flagged and repointed at `current_synonymous_taxon_ids`, the way
scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts already does.

Worth a test that a retired id in the referenced set does not abort the run.

Related: salish-ayb.4 (the columns — now CLOSED, the migration shipped),
salish-4hq (nothing re-asks about known taxa).
Recorded in the inaturalist skill's Known Gotchas #10.

Re-verified 2026-08-29: code unchanged at fetch-inaturalist.ts:187 (query-param form) and
:301 (the throw); the live API still returns total_results 0 for `?id=1368491` and
`is_active: false` for `/taxa/1368491`.
notes: PR #407 (branch fix/retired-taxon-closure): path form + is_active/current_synonymous_taxon_ids through NormalizedTaxon and persist; closure follows current_taxon_id (NOT DEFERRABLE FK). Comment-only migration 20260829010000. Verified live: obs on 1368491 resolves 20 taxa, flags 1368491->1664971 and 1317295->41513, no replacement outside the closure. Awaiting CI/merge.
close_reason: Fixed in #407 (main 2c5279b), deployed to production 2026-08-29 (Deploy 33264333252 green incl. smoke; the comment migration 20260829010000 verified in prod). taxaUrl asks by the /taxa/{ids} path form; is_active + current_synonymous_taxon_ids flow through TAXA_FIELDS -> NormalizedTaxon -> persist; the closure follows current_taxon_id so the NOT DEFERRABLE FK resolves. Verified live: an observation on the retired 1368491 resolves 20 taxa and flags both retirements in the chain (1368491->1664971, genus 1317295->41513). Still open by design: records on a retired taxon are not repointed and a taxon already in the mirror is never re-asked — salish-4hq / inat-taxa-status.ts.

title: [bug] Maplify taxon resolution uses the stale field, so moderator species corrections are discarded
description:
Ingest resolves a Maplify sighting's taxon by joining `maplify.sightings.scientific_name`
onto `inaturalist.taxa`. When an Orca Network moderator corrects a species, the correction
lands in `name` (and in `comments`), while `scientific_name` keeps the ORIGINAL, now-wrong
identification. We take the wrong one.

Found 2026-08-28 while checking provider provenance for salish-ayb.2.

12 records where `name` and the resolved taxon are different animals. Six carry explicit
correction language, and the direction is the same in every one — `name` is the correction,
`scientific_name` is what was superseded:

  id      name (correct)                  joined on scientific_name    comment
  204037  Gray Whale                      Megaptera novaeangliae       "Edited by Alisa Lemire Brooks to correct species. Reported as humpback..."
  188375  Gray Whale                      Megaptera novaeangliae       "Orca Network note: reported as humpback but was gray whale - Alisa"
  188401  Gray Whale                      Megaptera novaeangliae       "Edit, this was a gray whale per photos and other reports. Alisa"
  158632  Humpback                        Eschrichtius robustus        "[Orca Network] Edit, reported as grays but were the two humpbacks."
  158629  Humpback                        Eschrichtius robustus        "[Orca Network] Edit, reported as grays but these were the two humpbacks."
  144659  Minke Whale                     Megaptera novaeangliae       "{Photo confirms minke, corrected species - alb]"
  152658  Southern Resident Killer Whale  Balaenoptera acutorostrata   "Edit to confirm these were orcas, J pod (Orca Network)"
  144521  Gray Whale                      Megaptera novaeangliae       (no correction language)
  152946  Humpback                        Orcinus orca                 (no correction language)
  179732  Humpback                        Orcinus orca                 (no correction language)
  195928  Humpback                        Orcinus orca                 (no correction language)
  139704  Finback Whale                   Balaenoptera acutorostrata   (no correction language)

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND 12 ROWS

  1. These are the highest-quality records in the corpus, not the worst — a human with
     photos reviewed them and said what the animal was. Discarding exactly those
     corrections inverts the value of the moderation.
  2. They reach the DwC-A export and therefore GBIF, so we publish a gray whale as a
     humpback under our own name.
  3. 12 is what a same-animal disagreement makes VISIBLE. A correction from one humpback
     record to another humpback record leaves both fields agreeing and is undetectable
     this way, so 12 is a floor, not a count.

NOT AS SIMPLE AS "JOIN ON name INSTEAD"

`name` is free text with real variants — 'Finback Whale', 'Grey', 'Killer Whale (Orca)',
'Marsouin commun' (French), 'Unspecified'. It resolves to a taxon less reliably than
`scientific_name` does, which is presumably why the join was written this way. Options:

  - Prefer `name` only when the two disagree and `name` resolves confidently.
  - Parse the correction out of `comments` — the project already parses that field at read
    time (CLAUDE.md: comments is immutable, parse at read time, never UPDATE), and the
    language is formulaic: "Edit...", "corrected species", "reported as X but was Y".
  - Flag disagreements for review rather than resolving automatically.

Whichever is chosen, a disagreement should not be silently resolved in favour of the
superseded field.

Repro:
  SELECT id, name, scientific_name, comments FROM maplify.sightings
  WHERE (name,scientific_name) IN (('Gray Whale','Megaptera novaeangliae'),
    ('Humpback','Orcinus orca'),('Humpback','Eschrichtius robustus'),
    ('Minke Whale','Megaptera novaeangliae'),('Finback Whale','Balaenoptera acutorostrata'),
    ('Southern Resident Killer Whale','Balaenoptera acutorostrata'));

Related: salish-lv0 (export drops records), salish-ayb.4 (the taxa mirror is also stale,
for a different reason).
close_reason:
Fixed in #394, backfilled in prod, tooling in #395.

RESOLVER (#394, merged and deployed): resolveScientificName now treats upstream
placeholders ('N/A') as absent, prefers the common name when it disagrees with
scientific_name (moderator corrections land in name), folds case/spacing/apostrophes,
maps retired genus names to what iNaturalist carries, and covers the live vocabulary
including Spanish and French. Genus-level upstream categories (Whale Alert's Common
Dolphin / Right Whale / Bottlenose Whale) deliberately stay at genus.

BACKFILL (applied to production 2026-08-28): 4,973 sightings without a taxon -> 4,544.
427 gained a taxon, 208 reassigned, 0 lost. All seven records whose comments record a
moderator correction now carry the species the moderator reported. Recomputed plan is a
clean no-op.

Ordering mattered: #394 had to deploy first, since persist.ts upserts
taxon_id = EXCLUDED.taxon_id over a rolling window and would have reverted part of the
backfill otherwise.

FOUND ALONG THE WAY, not in the original report: 'N/A' as a literal scientific_name (128
records), 'Grey' in the map but not 'Gray' (174), Lagenorhynchus/Sagmatias not carried by
our taxa mirror (43), non-English and mis-decoded names (34). The original 12-record
symptom was the smallest part.

LEFT OPEN: 196 Southern Resident records moved Orcinus orca -> O. o. ater. That unifies
records previously split by nothing but whether upstream filled scientific_name, but it
is a change of claim and was flagged in the PR rather than presented as part of the bug.

title: Capture the symbology prototype findings and write decision 029
description:
The prototype answered two questions with numbers. Fold the findings into
docs/decisions/029, then implement.

FINDING 1 — "label segments instead of their points" does almost nothing, as
specified. A singleton is a segment of one, so every occurrence is a segment
head and still gets a label. Measured:

  day          occ  segments  TRACKS  singletons
  2026-07-20    55        52       3          49
  2026-07-22    77        59       6          53
  2026-07-25    83        73       6          67
  2026-07-26    61        56       3          53
  2026-06-15   106        74      10          64

Labelling segment heads turns 83 labels into 73. On 2026-07-25 exactly ONE
segment carries an identifier. The lever that works is labelling only
MULTI-POINT tracks — 6 labels instead of 73 — leaving singletons as bare dots.
That also answers the pinniped question for free: decision 027 gates segments to
six cetacean species, so an otter sighting is a singleton by construction and
never had a track label to lose.

FINDING 2 — sizing markers by location uncertainty CANNOT be built on the data
we hold, and would assert the wrong thing if it could:

  provider     n       with accuracy   distribution
  maplify      34,791  0               hardcoded NULL in the view
  direct       438     0               —
  happywhale   5,601   5,601           three discrete values: 2, 16, 161 m
  inaturalist  20,581  16,410          p50 31 m, p90 2.9 km, p99 28.7 km,
                                       max 7,313 km

57% has no value; HappyWhale's three buckets are coordinate-precision
artefacts, not uncertainty estimates. At zoom 10 (~100 m/px at 48N) the median
iNat circle is 0.3 px while the p99 is a 287 px disc — no transfer function
serves both. Deeper: `accuracy` is where the REPORTER was, not where the animal
was. For shore-based whale sighting the dominant error is range-to-animal, and
`observed_from` is populated on 100 records, all native. A 31 m circle around an
orca reported from Lime Kiln would be a confident, precise, wrong claim.

SECONDARY
  - Two-letter group codes (KW/BW/SE/OT) are legible at 22 px and unambiguous,
    which demotes GH #79's icon library from blocker to polish.
  - Layer-level `declutter: true` removes the overlapping-label collision
    without the hand-tuned pixel offsets in style.ts.
  - Travel lines are gated at `resolution > 100` and so never draw at the
    default zoom. Some of GH #271 "travel lines are faint" is actually "travel
    lines are absent".
  - `Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira` (319 records) is missing from
    `travelSpeedKmH`, so North Pacific Humpbacks silently never seed a segment
    though `Megaptera novaeangliae` does.

UNRESOLVED, for the record to settle: a 2-point, sub-hour segment is a thin
claim to be drawing as a journey — the threshold probably wants 3+ points or a
minimum distance.

The prototype is throwaway. Per the prototype skill, the full variant set is
the primary source and belongs on a branch out of main; only the validated
decision lands here.
notes: Decision 029 written and PR'd: #393. Prototype parked on prototype/map-symbology.

title: Map symbology: replace the single-letter markers
description:
The single-letter bubble in `symbolFor()` (src/identifiers.ts) fails outside
killer whales. It is not merely opaque — it is AMBIGUOUS. Measured over 61,411
occurrences, the scheme collapses to 18 glyphs:

  H  18,579 records, 3 taxa — Humpback Whale AND Harbor Porpoise
  S   8,030 records, 10 taxa — Harbor Seal, Sea Otter, Sperm Whale, Steller
                               Sea Lion, Striped Dolphin, ...
  G   6,978 records, 4 taxa
  C   4,506 records, 8 taxa
  N   3,189 records, 7 taxa — the River Otter that started this

A 15 m whale and a 1.5 m porpoise share the most common glyph on the map. Two
further defects: upstream lowercase vernaculars leak through as `c` ("common
seals") and `s` ("sea otters"), making case load-bearing by accident; and `T`
means Biggs pod in the orca branch but "Toothed Whales" in the fallback, so the
collision reaches the part of the scheme that does work.

A throwaway prototype (src/prototype-symbology.ts, ?variant=A|B|C|D) was built
2026-08-26/27 to decide this from pictures. It settled two things — see the
findings issue.

Related: GH #79 (species icons), GH #271 (travel lines are faint), GH #123
(highlight last observation, closed), GH #385 / salish-szv (haul-out
clustering), salish-uzt (map perf).
notes:
Decision 029's core landed in PR #402 alongside salish-ayb.6: taxon-group palette, two-line segment-head label, symbolFor() retired, layer-level declutter, list badge matching the map. The epic can close once #402 merges.

Remaining symbology work is in 029's Open section, not yet filed: what makes a track worth drawing (a 2-point sub-hour segment is a thin claim), and density beyond a typical day (#31's historical view). GH #79's icon library stays deferred — 029 demoted it to polish.
close_reason:
Decision 029 implemented and deployed. PR #401 (travel speeds, travel lines, infrastructure markers) and PR #402 (the palette, the two-line segment-head label, symbolFor retired, layer-level declutter, short map forms).

VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-27: taxon.entity_id present, 58,604 of 64,027 occurrences (91.5%) carry a register entity, and the live map draws 'Biggs · T34A7, T37A4, T99s / Seen 5× over 2h' and 'Humpback / Seen 3× in under an hour'. The single-letter markers are gone.

029's two Open questions are now their own issues, plus one thing real data surfaced that the synthetic day did not: pooled matriline identifiers make the identity line ~45 characters on a busy Biggs encounter.

title: Decision record: the register names the animals, we compose the display
description:
Write the salishsea-io decision record for adopting the register as the source
of animal identity, so the reasoning is not rediscovered.

MUST CAPTURE
  - Why `inaturalist.taxa` cannot be the display-name source: it is an upstream
    mirror (its own RLS policy is named "Ingest worker may maintain the taxa
    mirror"), and decision 008 forbids mirror semantics surfacing in UI. Today
    every branch of `public.occurrences` — including native submissions and
    Maplify — reads `vernacular_name` from it.
  - Why a local `public.taxon_names` override was REJECTED: it would mint a
    second opinion about animal names, which ADR-0012 exists to prevent. This
    was the first proposal and it was wrong; record it so it is not proposed
    again.
  - Why hand-editing `inaturalist.taxa` was rejected, on three grounds: it
    violates decision 008; it only survives ingest by accident of `DO NOTHING`,
    which is one reasonable bugfix away from reverting every display name with
    no test to catch it; and that same `DO NOTHING` is why the mirror is stale
    in the first place.
  - The division of labour: the register asserts the canonical name (ADR-0011
    prefLabel), we compose presentation. Capitalisation, truncation, sort order
    and disambiguation are ours by ADR-0011's own text.
  - That adoption ships currently-uncurated data — the animals README states
    no row has been curator-verified and ADR-0012 is Proposed.

Relates to GH #156 (animal names in local languages): the register's
names.tsv already carries a `language` column and ADR-0020 makes a localised
preferred name a sparse name row, so i18n rides the same mechanism rather than
needing a parallel one. Note that in the record; do not scope it here.
notes: Written as docs/decisions/033-register-names-the-animals.md; PR #411. Captures all six required points, plus the thing ADR-0012 asks be recorded on this side: decision 008 governs the per-source mirrors and not the register. The hand-editing rejection is sharper than filed — taxa-refresh.yml (#409) now UPDATEs vernacular_name weekly, so it is no longer 'one bugfix away'. #156 noted as riding ADR-0020, not scoped. Follows salish-ox2.
close_reason: Closed

title: Materialize the register into Postgres and resolve display names through it
description:
The mechanism ADR-0012 describes: "the same identifiers, the same membership
model, the same definitions, loaded into Postgres and presented."

Scope here is deliberately the taxon-name slice only — not the individual
catalogue.

WORK
  - A `register` schema holding entities, names and mappings, loaded from a
    pinned release artefact (blocked on salish-ayb.3). `dist/searchable_name.tsv`
    is the file: preferred plus every alternate, each with the entity's label,
    kind and rank.
  - Join `public.occurrences` to a register entity via the
    `inaturalist.taxon:<id>` crosswalk, resolving deactivated ids first
    (blocked on the mirror-refresh issue).
  - Display name comes from the register's `common` name row, replacing
    `inaturalist.taxa.vernacular_name`. That is what turns "North American
    River Otter" into "River otter" and stops decision 008's leak.
  - Keep the load reproducible and re-runnable — pinning a new release should
    be a routine operation, not a migration.

DO NOT use `hidden` name rows for display. They exist for matching input
(competency question C2 — telling candidates apart when a moderator types), not
for presentation output. `humpback` being present as a hidden row is not
permission to render it.

Fixes as a side effect: casing inconsistencies inherited from iNaturalist
("common seals", "sea otters", "Grey whales" arriving lowercase), spelling drift
("Pacific Harbour Porpoise" beside "Harbor Porpoise"), and "Resident Killer
Whale" on 4,115 records where the community says Southern Resident or SRKW.
close_reason:
Merged (#398), deployed, and loaded in production.

PROD: register 2026.08.1 loaded — 699 entities, 684 names, 43 mappings, 39 crosswalked
taxa. 54,362 of 64,001 occurrences (84.9%) now display a register name; 7 have no name at
all, which is unchanged (genus stubs iNaturalist has no vernacular for either). The map
says 'River otter'.

TWO ADVERSARIAL REVIEWS ran over this. What they caught, in order of how close it came to
shipping:

1. Row multiplication. public.occurrences LEFT JOINs the crosswalk, so two rows for one
   iNaturalist taxon id would have silently duplicated every occurrence of that animal.
   38 entities in this edition already carry two 'common' names; they are individuals with
   two nicknames and none are crosswalked, so the view was unique by luck. DISTINCT ON now
   guarantees it. A partial unique on (entity_id) WHERE type='common' was suggested and
   NOT taken — it would reject this edition outright.

2. The migrations had never run as a unit. Both files were edited after being recorded as
   applied locally and the view had been repaired out of band, so the SQL bound for prod
   had executed nowhere. Verified with supabase db reset.

3. A load-bearing comment truncated mid-sentence, caused by rebuilding the migration from
   head -20 of its own header.

4. object_id LIKE 'inaturalist.taxon:%' plus split_part accepted
   'inaturalist.taxon:41777:legacy'. Now one anchored, length-bounded regex — unbounded
   digits would have overflowed ::integer and broken every read of public.occurrences.

CORRECTED CLAIMS: the dependency chain is three levels, not one; the OG card renderer also
reads vernacular_name, so link previews change and cached cards lag until TTL; the grants'
stated rationale was false (occurrences is a definer-rights view and register is not an
exposed PostgREST schema).

FOLLOW-UPS: salish-0gb (subspecies keep iNaturalist names — 'Harbour seal' beside 'Pacific
Harbor Seal' on the same map), salish-1g8 (nothing loads the register in prod or notices
it is empty; this load was manual).

title: Refresh the iNaturalist taxa mirror: deactivations and merges never propagate
description:
`scripts/ingest/persist.ts:345` upserts taxa `ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING`, with
the comment "taxa are stable reference data". They are not. A taxon row is
written once and never updated, so iNaturalist deactivations, merges and
renames never reach us.

MEASURED 2026-08-27, all 512 rows of `inaturalist.taxa` against /v1/taxa:
9 are inactive upstream, each carrying `current_synonymous_taxon_ids`.

  1368491  Sagmatias obliquidens        -> 1664971   38 records
  1317295  Sagmatias (genus)            -> 41513      0
  1368489  Sagmatias australis          -> 1672273    0
  1368490  Sagmatias cruciger           -> 1672272    0
  1368492  Sagmatias obscurus           -> 1664972    0
  508823   Inia geoffrensis boliviensis -> 508822     0
  520333   Myiopsitta monachus luchsi   -> 1651787    0
  531609   Pusa hispida saimensis       -> 1661364    0
  1289590  Leucocarbo bransfieldensis   -> 1246814    0

Only 1368491 carries data — and 2 of its 38 records are OUR OWN direct
submissions, so a contributor picked a taxon iNaturalist has since merged away
and our native records now point at a dead concept. The other 36 are iNat
observations. All 38 currently show as "Pacific White-sided Dolphin" alongside
210 more under the active id 1664971: one animal, two rows, in our own data.

The schema cannot even represent the problem: the table is
`(id, parent_id, scientific_name, vernacular_name, rank)` — no `is_active`, no
synonym pointer.

WORK
  - Add `is_active` and a current-taxon pointer to `inaturalist.taxa`.
  - Stop discarding updates. `DO NOTHING` must become a real upsert of the
    mirror fields, matching how observations already refresh on newer
    `updated_at`.
  - Backfill the 38 records onto 1664971 and mark the 9 rows inactive.
  - Decide whether the ingest resolves a deactivated taxon at write time or
    whether the view resolves at read time. Write time is preferable: it keeps
    `public.occurrences` from carrying the logic, and decision 008 wants
    translation at the boundary.

Worth doing on its own merits, independent of the register — but it also blocks
a clean join from occurrences to register entities, since a deactivated id
matches no crosswalk row and the record silently fails to join with no error.
close_reason:
Migration 20260828000000_taxa_deactivation.sql adds is_active + current_taxon_id with
CHECK constraints (a replacement implies inactive; a taxon is not its own replacement).
scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts refreshes status from the API and repoints
referencing rows at write time.

Applied locally: 9 taxa flagged inactive, 36 iNaturalist + 2 native records repointed,
0 records left referencing a dead taxon. Pacific White-sided Dolphin is now a single
taxon with 291 occurrences instead of being split across Sagmatias, Lagenorhynchus and
Aethalodelphis. Idempotent.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ISSUE AS FILED:

1. 'Stop discarding updates — DO NOTHING must become a real upsert' was wrong.
   resolveTaxonClosure fetches only taxa we do NOT already hold, so an existing row is
   never offered to the conflict clause at all. DO UPDATE would have changed nothing
   while looking like a fix. The comment claiming 'taxa are stable reference data' is
   corrected instead, and the real gap — that nothing re-asks — is filed separately.

2. The ingest CANNOT maintain these columns. Its v2 /taxa endpoint omits inactive taxa
   from results entirely rather than flagging them: asking v2 for two ids where one is
   retired returns one result and total_results 1. Only v1 reports deactivation. That
   asymmetry is why the drift was invisible, and it is recorded in the migration's
   column comments and the script's header.

Also: current_taxon_id is a foreign key and the mirror holds only taxa we reference, so
7 of the 9 replacements are not mirrored. Those are recorded as retired with a null
pointer — honest, and nothing references them.

title: animals: cover the salishsea-io corpus — missing species and unresolvable stubs
description:
The register's 19 taxon entities cover 97.5% of our occurrences. The remaining
1,524 records across 49 taxa fall into two shapes, and the second one already
has a pattern in the register.

MISSING SPECIES — straightforward additions:
  Balaenoptera musculus      Blue Whale                    261
  Grampus griseus            Risso's Dolphin               210
  Tursiops truncatus         Common Bottlenose Dolphin     109
  Lissodelphis borealis      N. Right Whale Dolphin         54
  Delphinus delphis (+ ssp. bairdii)  Common Dolphin        69
  Physeter macrocephalus     Sperm Whale                    13
  ... plus a long tail below 25 records each.

UNRESOLVABLE STUBS — "sighted but not resolvable further", the exact role
`Aves` (SSA:0000907) and `Laridae` (SSA:0000908) already play for hydrophone
audio. This extends an existing pattern rather than needing a new concept:
  Otariidae     Eared Seals    219
  Phocoidea     Pinnipeds      186
  Cetacea       Cetaceans       70
  Mysticeti     Baleen Whales   34
  Phocidae      Earless Seals   28
  Lutrinae      Otters          28
  Eumetopias    (genus only)    51

CAUTION on Phocoidea: decision 027 records that iNaturalist labels it
"Pinnipeds" but it is strictly the true-seal superfamily, and iNat returns
Otariidae under it. The register should not repeat the misnomer — if an entity
is added for it, the label follows the actual clade and the note explains why
the iNat crosswalk is to a misnamed concept.

Each addition needs: an entities.tsv row with an NCBITaxon id, a names.tsv
`common` row, and a mappings.tsv `skos:exactMatch` to the ACTIVE iNaturalist
taxon (see the drift workflow issue — four Sagmatias ids are deactivated).
notes:
salish-sea/animals PR #28. 21 taxon entities (15 species + 6 unresolvable stand-ins);
corpus coverage 97.5% -> 99.6% of 61,411 occurrences. Verified with check_crosswalks.py
--added-since (its first real use): all NCBI ids resolve, all iNat crosswalks active.
CI green: pull-request job passes, validate passes.

Two judgement calls flagged for the curator in the PR: Pinnipedia rather than iNaturalist's
Phocoidea (NCBI has no Phocoidea, so ADR-0008's taxon_id requirement cannot be met by that
concept), mapped as closeMatch; and the 'otter' fold collision, which validate.py caught
under ADR-0019 and which is resolved by declaring the shared spelling on both entities.

195 occurrences across 26 genus/family stubs left out on purpose — whether 'Megaptera,
species undetermined' wants its own entity or is ADR-0009 uncertainty-on-the-annotation is
a design question for the register owner, raised in the PR.

title: orcasite#1017: close out dthaler's follow-up (in the meeting or in writing)
description:
rainhead's last comment on #1017 acknowledges the previous reply was written without having read dthaler's KEIR remark or the rest of his long follow-up, and promises to address it. A meeting with Dave Thaler, Paul, and others (on or after 2026-08-19) is the natural venue for the open questions; whatever gets settled there should be written back to the issue so the thread stays the record.

Outstanding points from dthaler's follow-up:
- KEIR: 'kier' was a typo fixed in orcahello#573; dthaler says KEIR and PIGU are 4-letter birder codes (Dave Bain's system). KEIR has NOT been verified against the IBP list — the earlier check only ruled out KI__ codes, not KE__. Verify what species KEIR denotes before the register carries it (see salish-8vr.21).
- 'moderated' boolean (or isomorphic): required per-detection state orcasite lacks; seeded-vs-moderated tags are indistinguishable without it.
- Per-3-second segment predictions (timestamps/labels/confidences within the 60s sample) exist in OrcaHello's DB, absent from orcasite — dthaler flags this as a blocker to merging the two databases (OrcanodeMonitor, PODS-AI false-positive work already suffer from the join).
- 'resident' class: PODS-AI emits 'resident'; model only trained on SRKW, so it means SSA:0000001. orcahello#595 (won't add to hierarchy), orcahello#596 (portal interprets resident as srkw), pods-ai#381 (report srkw directly).
- dthaler rejects 'tags stay bout-only' as an end state: 3-second-granularity moderator tags are desirable (Tong's ask), just too much moderator work today (Dave Bain).
- The pivot question got a first reply; the fuller discussion is salish-8vr.22.
notes:
2026-09-20: Scott Veirs settled the pivot question: orcasite stays, and the good parts of the orcahello portal fold into it (relayed by Peter 2026-09-20; deliberately NOT a salishsea-io decision record -- it is Orcasound's call, so orcasite#1017 is where it must be written). Writing that back to #1017 is now part of this issue, along with dthaler's still-unanswered points (moderated flag, per-3s segment predictions) which orcasite inherits by absorbing the orcahello UI's job.
2026-09-20 (Peter): Scott Veirs will communicate the orcahello-vs-orcasite moderator-UI decision HIMSELF when he returns from sabbatical, around 2026-10-01. Do NOT post it to orcasite#1017 or #935 on his behalf, and do not draft it for him. What stays with this issue is rainhead's own promised reply to dthaler's follow-up (KEIR, the 'moderated' flag, per-3s predictions, the PODS-AI corrections) -- that part does not wait on Scott.

title: Decide: which moderator UI is the end state — orcasite or orcahello?
description:
Opened by dthaler on orcasite#1017 (post-2026-08-14). The assumption that the orcasite moderator UI stays and the orcahello (Blazor) one goes away was based on where developer cycles were — and that situation has now exactly reversed: multiple volunteers who know C# but not elixir, plus a recent run of orcahello moderator-UI improvements. Options he poses: reverse the end-goal (make the orcahello portal capable of moderating human detections), stick with the current goal, or something else. rainhead's reply on the issue: wants to talk it through in person / face to face; meanwhile doesn't mind building where the work is being done, and once design decisions are made it is not too much work to do it in both.

AFFECTS: salish-8vr.11's scope reduction (the Blazor half was dropped as dead work on the 2026-08-13 premise that orcasite becomes the single moderation UI — that premise is now explicitly reopened) and salish-8vr.19 (which system absorbs detection review). The register-integration design itself (identifiers, multi-valued classifications, certainty) is UI-agnostic and unaffected.
close_reason: Decided 2026-09-20 by Scott Veirs for Orcasound, relayed by Peter: orcasite owns the moderator UI; fold the good parts of the orcahello portal into it. No salishsea-io decision record, deliberately -- it is not this project's decision, and a second-hand copy here would become the only written version. Scott will communicate it himself on his return from sabbatical, around 2026-10-01. Consequences for us: salish-8vr.11 keeps its reduced scope; salish-8vr.19 is unblocked; orcasite inherits dthaler's 'moderated' flag and per-3s segment predictions.

title: Revisit: does orcasite need polymorphic item_tags for detection review?
description:
Opened 2026-08-14 by dthaler on orcasite#1017: "it's important for the orcasite database and moderator UI to have this functionality or we won't be able to move off the other moderator UI."

Consolidating on orcasite as the single moderation UI (confirmed 2026-08-13) means orcasite must absorb OrcaHello's detection review — and a human confirming or rejecting a detection is a human determination ON a detection, which orcasite cannot currently record.

My earlier position (tags stay bout-only; machine class is a field on the detection) holds for MACHINE assertions but does not cover this. ItemTag's ItemTagItem calculation already anticipates the change: "Update constraints/output to Union type once we have other taggable items."

Two distinct things attach to a detection — model assertion and human determination — and keeping them apart is the design, not an argument against making item_tags polymorphic.

Asked dthaler what else the OrcaHello moderator UI does that orcasite would need to cover; only the detection review path has been read so far.
close_reason: Duplicate of salish-8vr.19 — the first create succeeded despite reporting a tip instead of a confirmation.

title: Revisit: does orcasite need polymorphic item_tags for detection review?
description: Opened 2026-08-14 by dthaler on orcasite#1017: 'it's important for the orcasite database and moderator UI to have this functionality or we won't be able to move off the other moderator UI.' Consolidating on orcasite as the single moderation UI (confirmed 2026-08-13) means orcasite must absorb OrcaHello's detection review — and a human confirming or rejecting a detection is a human determination ON a detection, which orcasite cannot currently record. My earlier position (tags stay bout-only; machine class is a field on the detection) holds for MACHINE assertions but does not cover this. ItemTag's ItemTagItem calculation already anticipates it: 'Update constraints/output to Union type once we have other taggable items.' Two distinct things attach to a detection — model assertion and human determination — and keeping them apart is the design. Asked dthaler what else the OrcaHello moderator UI does that orcasite would need to cover; only the detection review path has been read.
notes:
Context on TagHierarchy: dthaler authored it 2026-07-31 in orcahello#561, because 'moderators have been leaving the tags field blank because it was time consuming to fill it in' — independent confirmation of the affordance principle salish-8vr.9 / orcasite#1015 rests on. pigu resolves already (SSA:0000909 Cepphus columba carries PIGU as a hidden name); kier was a typo for keir, fixed in orcahello#573 (see salish-8vr.21 / salish-8vr.23 for KEIR verification).
ANSWERED 2026-08-19 — dthaler listed what the OrcaHello moderator UI does that orcasite would need to cover (not necessarily complete):
- orcasite#953: SRKW yes / no / UNSURE — moderated tags do yes/no but not 'unsure', so a separate property
- a per-detection 'moderated' boolean (or anything isomorphic) is REQUIRED — without it seeded predictions and human determinations are indistinguishable
- spectrogram showing which segments of the clip have calls, with jump-to
- shows who reported the candidate (PODS-AI vs OrcaHello)
- shows how many segments had calls + overall machine confidence %
- free-form labels beyond the preset hierarchy
- 1-click add/remove of labels (no typing in typical cases)
- two-factor auth
- separate views for unmoderated vs confirmed / false-positive / moderated-as-unknown
orcasite#935 is the umbrella for discrepancies.
Also 2026-08-19: dthaler REJECTS 'tags stay bout-only' as an end state — 3-second-granularity moderator tags are desirable (Tong's ask); Dave Bain says only that it is too much moderator work today. And OrcaHello stores per-3s-segment predictions orcasite lacks — a DB-merge blocker.
The answer to this bead's question may depend on salish-8vr.22 (which UI is the end state).
ATTRIBUTION ASYMMETRY (verified in code 2026-08-19): OrcaHello attributes review per-DETECTION, not per-tag — one Moderator (AzureAD UPN) + one Moderated timestamp on the detection document, and DetectionsController.cs:486 overwrites metadata.moderator on every save (last writer wins, no history). With PODS-AI seeding Tags, a saved review attributes the WHOLE tag set to that moderator — actively-confirmed vs passively-left-seeded is indistinguishable per tag. orcasite is strictly richer: item_tags.user_id with identity (user_id, tag_id, bout_id) — per-tag, per-user rows; two moderators can independently apply the same tag; destroy limited to own rows (server/lib/orcasite/radio/item_tag.ex). Implication: 'moderated boolean or isomorphic' is the FLOOR (all OrcaHello can offer); per-tag/per-user attribution is what actually keeps a model's seed distinguishable from a human's confirmation. Migration one-way door: historical OrcaHello tags can only arrive as 'attributed to the detection's last moderator, per-tag confirmation unknown.'
DESIGN CANDIDATE 2026-08-19 (rainhead): taggings as EVENTS. Append-only {actor (human user | model+version), item, register identifier, stance (present/absent/unsure), certainty/confidence, time-scope, timestamp}; current tag set is a fold. Dissolves in one shape: seeded-vs-confirmed (actor kind), the 'moderated' boolean (derived: any human event exists), #953 yes/no/unsure (stance), bout vs detection vs 3s-segment (time-scope on the event, not a schema fork), attribution (one actor per event), and OrcaHello's hand-rolled 'originals remembered for model improvement' (natural log property). Reframes the epic's separation principle: model assertion vs human determination kept apart by ACTOR KIND within one shape rather than by table. Precedent: iNaturalist identifications (append-only per-user, withdrawal not deletion, community taxon = fold); DwC Identification class consumes an event stream naturally; decision 013 gets easier. Costs: fold semantics are real design work (does human supersede model? is removal a retraction event?); bigger upstream ask than a column while elixir cycles are scarce (salish-8vr.22) — though item_tags is already close (per-user rows + timestamps; delta ≈ never hard-delete, add stance + actor-kind); OrcaHello history still arrives coarse (one event per detection, last moderator). Raise at the meeting alongside .22.
2026-09-24: RESOLVED as a proposal, filed as orcasound/orcasite#1051 'Record what happens to a bout and its tags as events, and publish them'. The taggings-as-events candidate above became: an append-only event log on the bout aggregate (bout_opened / time_range_revised / ended / recategorized / withdrawn, tag_applied / certainty_revised / removed) plus tag_identified on the vocabulary; each event carries the change plus a snapshot of the bout's current state and a version; exposed as a keyset-paginated JSON:API resource that salishsea.io polls. Also asks for item_tags FKs to become non-null, certainty on item_tags (#1014), and item_tags on the bouts include. bout_published was rejected: bouts are public at creation on purpose (tune in now); an empty end_time does NOT mean live, and liveness is a separate moderator-workflow question, deliberately not decided in #1051. Polymorphic item_tags for detection review is NOT part of this and stays open. Discovered 2026-09-24: orcahello has a merged Draft v0.4 bout-spec (orcahello#645, mhanch, approved by dthaler, 2026-09-16) proposing an orcasite Postgres model in its §6b (reporters, annotations, append-only detection_reviews, candidate_bouts); it never references #1001/#1013-#1017 or the register, and no orcasite maintainer was asked to review. Peter is alarmed by that process; raising it is his, separately from technical feedback. Spec link pinned: https://github.com/orcasound/orcahello/blob/f7c409a9bbd1f810029f70197ee94432f29ed00b/ModeratorFrontEnd/specification/bout-spec.md . ash_events 0.8.2 needs ash ~> 3.33; orcasite is on 3.5.43; Peter has a cloud agent preparing the Ash upgrade.
2026-09-25: paulcretu (orcasite) reviewed #1051: asked whether the consumer needs what-changed or just that-it-changed (updated_at + soft delete); suggested ash_paper_trail over ash_events; suggested naming actions after events (CQRS). Peter agreed on CQRS. Library comparison posted on #1051: ash_events = one table across bouts/item_tags/tags with actor + action name, public_fields for JSON:API/GraphQL, audit-only mode avoids replay overhead, but drops notifications on a single hard destroy (so bouts need soft delete, ash_archival 2.0.3 ok on Ash 3). ash_paper_trail = three version tables, better at showing a record's earlier versions, which nobody asked for. Ash 3.33 landed on main 2026-09-25 (orcasite#1052); #1053 (security deps) and #1054 (adds ash_events dep, no log yet) are stacked and open. Awaiting Paul's reply on the three-PR split.
2026-09-25: Dave Bain on orcahello#650 (issuecomment-5839563408): bouts are DYNAMIC and moderation is ongoing in three stages -- (1) SRKW presence out to conservation pros ASAP, (2) pod-specific labels from recognisable calls, (3) measurements of shared calls (e.g. L? -> L) -- spread over minutes to years. Moderating a session at a bout's edge EXTENDS it; between two bouts it may MERGE them (gap < 15 min). => the #1051 event model gains bout_merged (or withdraw + time_range_revised), and certainty_revised is expected routinely, not rarely. Also: 3-second intervals are AI triage only; moderator tags apply to the 60-s candidate as a whole today -> the #650 shape comment (bout-level moderator tags) stands. Automated detections should not join a bout until confirmed; a bout is 'finalized' only after expert moderation -> a review-completed mark is in their model too.

title: Reconcile normalize_designation() with the register's fold (ADR-0019)
description: ADR-0019 publishes the fold as THE matching rule and names our normalize_designation() as the thing to reconcile. Two divergences: (1) direction — ours pads (T65A5 -> T065A5) where the fold strips leading zeros (T090 -> t90); same goal, opposite convention, and only one can be the shared rule. (2) The trailing 's'. ADR-0019 refuses to fold it because T090s names the matriline and T090 its matriarch — 126 pairs depend on staying apart. supabase/migrations/20260708000104_identifier_candidate_cache.sql:41 strips 's$' before matching against grp.designation; verify whether that survives into matching, which ADR-0019 says it must not. Ours also does not handle apostrophes or hyphens at all. Acceptance: our implementation reproduces dist/fold_test.tsv exactly (a scratch Python version already does, so the rule is cheap — the question is what changes in SQL and what it breaks). Interacts with finding F9 in docs/design-notes/occurrence-identification-findings.md, which proposed searchable_name.tsv as the lookup table; ADR-0019 supersedes that with a rule instead of rows.
notes: 2026-09-23: PR #493. register.fold (SQL) + src/fold.ts (moved from scripts/register) + edge copy; normalize_designation dropped; candidate matview and 5 dependent views rebuilt; designations.code_folded / social_groups.designation_folded stored for lookups. Prod impact: 2 of 469 codes change (T1242s, T1241 were lpad-truncated to T124). Decision 052.
close_reason: Done in #493 (decision 052). Deployed 2026-09-23: normalize_designation is gone, the candidate cache is rebuilt on register.fold, T1242s and T1241 no longer match, and profile paths resolve by the folded columns (/individuals/t65a, /individuals/T046A, /matrilines/T65As, /ecotypes/biggs all 301 to their canonical addresses).

title: Link native and iNaturalist contributor records for the same person
description:
A person who observes through both SalishSea.io and iNaturalist has two contributors rows with nothing connecting them. inat_login is a dedup key for iNat rows only (D-15: native rows leave it NULL) and it is UNIQUE, so a native row cannot even be tagged with a login an iNat row already holds.

This is what blocks 'source the ORCID from iNaturalist where possible' from being machinery rather than a curation habit: the ORCIDs we hold sit on iNat rows, the archive exports native rows, and nothing joins them. The 20260621010000 migration called itself a seed for 'future cross-provider identity resolution' — this is that work.

contributors.entity_id (uuid, unused) may be the intended hook. Also decide whether resolution merges rows or adds a link table; merging interacts with the UNIQUE on inat_login.
acceptance_criteria: A person observed through both providers resolves to one identity, and a native occurrence can carry an ORCID sourced from that person's iNaturalist profile.
close_reason: Duplicate of salish-8fm, which predates it and already names the right shape (contributor_links, never name-similarity FK per decision 006). The recordedByID context has been folded into 8fm.

title: Tracked .beads/issues.jsonl export is stale — auto-export isn't reaching git
description:
CORRECTED 2026-08-13: an earlier version of this issue claimed the .gitignore comment was false and that issues.jsonl was untracked. That was wrong — it IS tracked (git ls-files confirms), and the comment at .gitignore:49-58 is accurate. The real problem is narrower.

The tracked export is stale: content dates from 2026-08-04, and the last commits touching it are #368 and 9b2edde. Every bd mutation since — including this session's — exists only in the local Dolt DB and refs/dolt/data, not in the JSONL that .gitignore calls 'the recovery floor'.

Likely cause is in the comment itself: 'git hooks disabled via git config --unset core.hooksPath'. bd's auto-export writes the file but its 'git add' is refused or never runs, which is the exact silent failure the comment says happened before, when a stray rm -rf on 2026-07-27 was what surfaced it.

Fix: determine whether bd's export hook can commit under the current hooks config; if not, either re-enable the hook path or add an explicit export+commit step to the session-close protocol in CLAUDE.md. Then commit a fresh export.
acceptance_criteria: A current issues.jsonl is committed, and either the hook commits it automatically or CLAUDE.md's session-close protocol says who does.
notes:
Cause found 2026-08-29: a bare `bd export` writes to STDOUT, not to .beads/issues.jsonl. Anything piping it (`bd export | tail`, `bd export >/dev/null`) leaves the tracked file untouched while looking like it worked, and the file then drifts silently until someone diffs it. The tracked export was 14 minutes stale this session before it was noticed. The correct invocation is `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`. Whatever fix lands here, that flag is the thing a hook or alias has to carry.
FIXED 2026-08-29. Root cause: bd 1.2.2's `bd hooks run pre-commit` does no export — verified by running it directly (exit 0, no write, nothing staged) — and bd's own auto-backup last ran 2026-08-04 at 98 issues per .beads/export-state.json, against 187 today. So the mechanism the .gitignore comment assumed was never running. core.hooksPath IS set to .beads/hooks; hooks were not disabled, contrary to that comment.

Fix: an explicit export+stage step in .beads/hooks/pre-commit, placed BELOW bd's BEGIN/END markers so `bd hooks install` cannot clobber it. It warns loudly on failure and never blocks the commit. Also corrected three documents that each stated the opposite of the others: .gitignore carried a stale block saying beads is untracked directly above the block saying it is deliberately tracked; CLAUDE.md's architecture line said 'JSONL is a local-only backup, not a tracked export'; and docs/agents/issue-tracker.md said the file 'is gone'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Permalink occurrence lookup can't use an index (Sentry SALISHSEA-IO-37)
description:
hydrateFromOccurrenceId (src/salish-sea.ts:524) runs .from('occurrences').select().eq('id', 'inaturalist:340900993'). In the public.occurrences view, id is a computed string ('inaturalist:' || observations.id, and likewise per branch), so Postgres cannot push the predicate down to any index: it materializes all four UNION branches — maplify, inaturalist, happywhale, native — including the per-row photo-aggregation subqueries, then filters. Warm caches keep it under the anon role's 3s statement_timeout; a cold permalink hit blew it on 2026-08-06 (Sentry SALISHSEA-IO-37, https://beam-reach.sentry.io/issues/SALISHSEA-IO-37). Structural — will recur as permalink traffic grows.

Candidate fixes: expose an indexable source/source_id pair the client filters on (predicate pushes down per branch), or route permalink hydration through an indexed function similar to the occurrence_index path (mind decision 021's freshness constraint).
notes: Related precedent: SALISHSEA-IO-11 was the same failure shape (predicate defeating indexes under the 3s anon timeout), fixed in migration 20260803000000_occurrence_days_range_predicate.sql.
close_reason: Fixed by migration 20260812150000_occurrence_id_lookup_indexes.sql (commit 4f6e000): four expression indexes matching the pushed-down per-branch quals; verified with EXPLAIN on prod and locally with enable_seqscan=off.

Register hierarchy is changing under this: salish-0gb.1 settles animals Q1 as (a), closing the ecotype vocabulary at TWO — Bigg's and Resident — with SRKW and NRKW as communities beneath Resident. orcasite#1001's premise of 'four ecotypes (SRKW, Biggs, offshore, NRKW)' will not survive it. CORRECTION to the note above (2026-08-29). It said orcasite#1001's "premise of
'four ecotypes'... will not survive" the Q1 change. That was a misreading and
should not be acted on.

below"), and the four-ecotype phrasing Q1 quotes comes from discussion around

THE REAL DEPENDENCY, which is a data-shape one and was already anticipated by
