title: Migrate from npm to pnpm
description:
npm's lockfile is host-specific for optional platform deps: running `npm install` on darwin prunes packages reachable only through optional wasm32-wasi/platform bindings, then linux CI computes an ideal tree that wants them and `npm ci` fails EUSAGE. This has now broken main twice (8cc5572/41924ba, fixed in bc86cb2) and previously via the @rolldown/@emnapi pruning noted in engineering lessons. Upstream: npm/cli#4828, open since 2022.

pnpm records every platform variant unconditionally, so the failure mode cannot occur. Migrate the root project and infra/, update all five workflows, and switch the Dependabot npm ecosystem over.
design:
pnpm over Yarn Berry (PnP fights Vite tooling; node-modules linker forfeits the benefit) and over Bun (adds a second, less battle-tested runtime to CI, cutting against the project's 'minimize volatile dependencies' constraint).

Scope:
- pnpm import to convert package-lock.json -> pnpm-lock.yaml (root and infra/)
- packageManager field in package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml if infra/ becomes a workspace
- .github/workflows: build.yml, deploy.yml, smoke.yml, dwca-nightly.yml, ingest-heartbeat.yml -- pnpm/action-setup + 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile', cache: pnpm in setup-node
- .github/dependabot.yml: npm ecosystem reads pnpm-lock.yaml (supported for lockfileVersion 9)
- docs: README.md, infra/README.md, CLAUDE.md build/test block, docs/runbook/deploys.md, docs/engineering-lessons.md
- decision record in docs/decisions/
acceptance_criteria: All five workflows green on main; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds in a clean clone on linux; package-lock.json deleted; decision record written; docs reference pnpm commands.
close_reason: Merged as PR #370 (a4fb368) and deployed to production successfully on 2026-08-04. First pnpm deploy green end to end: Build, Test, Deploy (supabase db push + S3/CloudFront + pnpm exec cdk deploy), Smoke. Decision record docs/decisions/025-pnpm-over-npm.md. Also brought infra/ under Dependabot, which had never been covered.

title: No CI guard against SELECT-grant drift between migrations and prod
description:
salish-0ew shipped migration 20260730120000_public_select_grants.sql, which brought a fresh `supabase db reset` to grant parity with prod (48 = 48). Nothing stops it drifting again.

The gap that caused salish-0ew was invisible precisely because prod looked correct: grants were applied out of band, and every later `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` preserved them, so nothing ever disturbed prod and nothing ever recreated them elsewhere. The same thing can happen again the next time a grant is applied by hand.

The only guard today is the grant-replay step in scripts/pull-prod-db.sh, which runs locally when someone mirrors prod. It makes the mirror work; it does not fail anything.

Opportunity: as of PR #368 build.yml is also the deploy gate, so an assertion added there blocks production, not just PRs. It already runs `supabase db start` and applies supabase/ci-seed.sql, so the reset database is in hand.
acceptance_criteria: A CI check fails when the grants produced by a fresh reset differ from an expected set — either a checked-in expected-grants fixture diffed in build.yml, or an assertion hitting the anon REST path against the freshly reset CI database. Lives in build.yml so it gates deploys as well as PRs.
notes: This is acceptance criterion 3 of salish-0ew, which was closed with criteria 1 and 2 met. Reproduce the original diff per that issue: information_schema.role_table_grants for table_schema in ('public','dwc'), grantee in ('anon','authenticated'), privilege_type='SELECT'. Run psql with timing OFF or the '\timing' line inflates the count by one.
close_reason: Merged in PR #450: supabase/read-grants.test.ts pins prod's effective SELECT grants (44 relations + nicknames minus story) and CI's fresh reset reproduces them; CLAUDE.md convention updated.

title: Restore seeking to an arbitrary date: click-to-edit the date readout
description:
Replacing the date input with a calendar (salish-dq2, decision 021) removed the only way to jump to a distant date. The corpus spans 2012-2026, so reaching the earliest data now takes 169 clicks on the month arrow.

Make the 'Thu, Jul 30, 2026' readout under the grid click-to-edit: it swaps in a native <input type=date> bounded by the same range the calendar enforces, commits on change, and reverts on Escape or blur.
design:
Option B of the options discussed 2026-07-31. Chosen over year steppers (still 14 clicks to 2012, no information) and over a drill-up month/year picker (option A — more capable, since it would also show WHICH months have data, but a bigger build). B does not foreclose A; the drill-up can host a typed-date field later.

Bounds come from EARLIEST_OBSERVATION_DATE and observationToday() so the input and the grid cannot disagree.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking the date readout swaps in a focused date input; entering a date selects it and reverts to the readout; Escape and blur revert without changing the date; the input cannot select outside 2000-01-01..today.
close_reason: Shipped 2026-08-01 in PR #360 (a568095), the day the issue was filed; never closed. Verified against the acceptance criteria in src/obs-panel.ts at 175223a: the readout is a .selected-date button that swaps in a focused type=date input (startSeekingDate + focus on updateComplete); change commits and reverts (onSeekDate); Escape reverts and returns focus to the readout (onSeekKeydown + updated()); blur reverts (@blur=stopSeekingDate); min/max are EARLIEST_OBSERVATION_DATE..observationToday() AND onSeekDate re-guards the same bounds, because min/max only style an out-of-range value. Gap noted, not blocking: no unit or e2e coverage for the seek path — filed separately.

title: Regions filter the data, and shade the map outside the active region
description:
Follow-on to #352 (Go-to place bubbles) and encompassing GH issue #16 ("Shade map area outside the bounds of the data").

## Why

Today the region bubbles are pure navigation: clicking one zooms the map and nothing else changes. Two problems follow.

1. Absence reads as absence. A user who pans past the edge of our ingest coverage sees empty water and concludes there were no whales there, when in fact we carry no data there at all. That is GH #16.
2. The region is not a durable piece of state. Pan away and the framing is gone; there is nothing to share, nothing in the URL, and no way to say "show me Puget Sound" as a question about the data rather than about the viewport.

Promoting regions from viewport presets to a filter fixes both: the region becomes the scope of the query, and the area outside it is shaded to say plainly "we are not showing you anything here."

## What

A selected region filters the occurrence data and masks the map outside itself. It persists across pan and zoom, survives reload, and is shareable.

Salish Sea is the default.
design:
Decided with the user 2026-07-30:

**1. The mask means "the region you selected", not "where our coverage ends."**
One concept, one mask. Picking a region both filters the data and shades everything outside it. Rejected: a separate permanent coverage mask derived from source/taxon extents layered under a lighter region outline (truer to #16's framing, but two overlapping shaded areas to design and caption); and shading the intersection of region and coverage (single mask whose meaning shifts depending on which constraint binds).

**2. Regions stay lon/lat rectangles.**
Reuse the existing `Extent` constants in src/constants.ts. The filter is exact and predictable and this ships without sourcing new geodata. Accepted cost: a rectangle shaded over the Salish Sea is crude -- it clips Puget Sound's south end and includes Vancouver Island's interior. Rejected for now: real polygons (Salish Sea water body, NOAA SRKW critical habitat) -- better-looking and semantically real, but needs sourcing, licensing, simplification and a home (static GeoJSON vs a PostGIS table). Also rejected: bbox filter + polygon mask, which makes the shading and the filter disagree at the edges (points visible inside a shaded corner).

**3. The filter applies to the map, the observation list, AND the calendar's day counts.**
Everything the sidebar shows must agree. If the calendar counted sightings the map is not drawing, a day would read "busy" and click through to empty water -- the exact confusion this issue exists to remove. See the RESOLVED section in the notes: only the calendar needs a schema change; the map and list filter through plain PostgREST.

**4. Every bubble filters.** Puget Sound, Salish Sea, San Juans, SRKW Range -- one control, one meaning. Picking San Juans hides a sighting off Victoria 20 miles away; acceptable because the mask makes the hiding visible. Rejected: coarse regions filter while fine ones only navigate (two visually identical bubbles doing different things).

**5. "Salish Sea" as a filter means `salishSeaExtent` = [-126, 47, -122, 50.5]** -- NOT the `salishSRKWExtent` = [-124, 47, -122, 49.5] the bubble uses today. Settled 2026-07-30, resolving open item (a). The tight SRKW-clipped extent was chosen in #352 to frame "the water the sightings are actually in", which is right for a viewport and wrong for a filter: as the default it would silently drop the Strait of Georgia north of 49.5 and the whole western Strait of Juan de Fuca / Swiftsure Bank west of -124. Implementation note: decide explicitly whether the *zoom* keeps the tight extent while the *filter* uses the wide one, or both widen. Two extents for one bubble needs a comment saying why, or it reads as a bug.

**6. There is an "Everywhere" escape hatch.** Settled 2026-07-30, resolving open item (b). Without it the widest region is SRKW Range [-125.5, 36, -122, 54] while ingest reaches `acartiaExtent` [-136, 36, -120, 54], leaving real data permanently unreachable from the UI. "Everywhere" drops the region filter entirely (and draws no mask). Costs one more bubble in an already-full row -- worth watching at 390px width, where the Go-to row is already the tightest thing in the panel.

**Assumed, not asked:** selecting a region still zooms the map to it, as the bubbles do today. The filter is what is new; the navigation is retained.
acceptance_criteria:
- Selecting a region filters the map features, the sidebar observation list, and the calendar's per-day volume circles, consistently.
- The filter persists across pan, zoom, day changes, reload and back/forward; it is encoded in the URL and a shared link reproduces it.
- The map area outside the active region is visibly shaded, in a treatment that reads as "we are not showing data here", satisfying GH #16.
- Salish Sea is the default on a fresh load with no region in the URL, using `salishSeaExtent` per design decision 5.
- The `occurrence_days` change is verified against prod-scale data: the month predicate still pushes down through the GROUP BY into each UNION branch with the bbox added, and a month still returns within the latency budget decision 021 set (~120-170 ms). NOT an index requirement — prod has no spatial index and this issue explicitly does not add one; see the measurements in the notes.
- Decision record written; docs/decisions/README.md updated; GH #16 closed by the PR.
notes:
Open items to settle during implementation, in rough priority order:

**a. The "Salish Sea" extent is wrong for a filter.** The bubble uses `salishSRKWExtent` = [-124, 47, -122, 49.5], deliberately, because #352 wanted framing on "the water the sightings are actually in". As the DEFAULT FILTER it silently drops real data: everything in the Strait of Georgia north of 49.5, and the whole western Strait of Juan de Fuca / Swiftsure Bank west of -124. `salishSeaExtent` = [-126, 47, -122, 50.5] is the honest choice for filtering. Consider keeping the tight extent for the zoom and the wide one for the filter, or just widening both. Resolve before implementing -- it decides what the default hides.

**b. No escape hatch was chosen.** The widest bubble is SRKW Range [-125.5, 36, -122, 54]; ingest reaches `acartiaExtent` [-136, 36, -120, 54]. With every bubble a filter and no "Everywhere" option, data in that gap becomes unreachable from the UI. Either add an "Everywhere" bubble, or accept and document that the app only ever shows the SRKW range at widest.

**c. URL state.** The region needs a param (`?r=puget-sound` or similar) alongside `d`/`x`/`y`/`z`/`o`, with slugs, validation and a popstate path. See `parseUrlParams`/`setQueryParams` in src/salish-sea.ts.

**d. `?o=` pointing outside the active region.** `hydrateFromOccurrenceId` can land on an occurrence the current filter excludes. Widen the region to fit it, or clear the filter, or refuse -- needs a decision.

**e. Realtime and the sighting form.** The `occurrences_changed` broadcast refetch must carry the region. A contributor can save a sighting outside the active region (the form validates against `acartiaExtent`) and then not see it -- decide whether saving widens or clears the filter.

**f. Mask rendering.** An OpenLayers layer drawing world-minus-region. Needs a treatment that reads as "no data here" rather than "disabled", and must not swallow map interactions or the basemap's own legibility.

**g. Out of scope:** individual/matriline profile page maps, and the DwC-A export.

**h. Write a decision record** for the mask-means-selected-region and rectangles-for-now calls before implementing -- per CLAUDE.md, decisions get written when made.

---

## Measured on prod, 2026-07-30 (corpus: 61,389 occurrences; 39,608 maplify + 20,569 iNat)

Bbox filtering is cheap, but NOT because of an index -- there is no spatial index and, as the view is written, there cannot be one.

| query | time |
|---|---|
| A. `occurrence_days`, one month, no region (today's calendar) | **169 ms** |
| B. same month + Salish Sea bbox | **75 ms** |
| C. Salish Sea bbox with NO day filter (whole corpus) | **3,448 ms** |
| D. bbox on `maplify.sightings` base table (`&&` envelope) | 20 ms (seq scan, 39.6k rows) |
| E. bbox on `inaturalist.observations` base table | 11 ms (seq scan, 20.6k rows) |

**Adding the region makes the calendar query faster, not slower** (169 -> 75 ms). The bbox cuts rows before they reach the view's nested-loop joins against taxa/providers/collections/organizations, which are seq-scanned per row -- the maplify branch alone reports 5.8M "Rows Removed by Join Filter". Those joins, not the spatial predicate, are what the month query actually spends its time on.

**There is no spatial index in prod.** 74 indexes across public/maplify/inaturalist/happywhale; zero GiST, zero on any `location` column.

**An index would not help anyway, for two independent reasons:**
1. `public.occurrences.location` is not a geography -- it is a computed composite, `row(gis.ST_X(location::gis.geometry), gis.ST_Y(location::gis.geometry))::lon_lat`. Any predicate against the view's `location` is an expression over the base column and can never use an index on it. Using one would mean pushing the predicate into the base tables, inside the view or inside a function.
2. The Salish Sea bbox matches **38,272 of 61,389 rows (62%)**. At that selectivity the planner would choose a seq scan over a GiST index regardless.

**Do not add a spatial index as part of this work.** It would be dead weight at this corpus size. Revisit if the corpus grows an order of magnitude or if regions become polygons (design item 2), where `ST_Intersects` against a real shape is a genuinely more expensive predicate.

**Row C is the trap to avoid:** any region query that omits a date bound costs ~3.5 s. Every code path that filters by region must also bound the day.

---

## RESOLVED 2026-07-30: PostgREST can filter the composite. No RPC needed for map or list.

Tested against a full production mirror in the local stack (`scripts/pull-prod-db.sh`). The earlier worry that `location` being a composite rather than jsonb would force everything through RPC functions was **wrong**.

**`->` works and is exact.** A four-sided bbox via the REST API returned `Content-Range: 0-0/38275`, matching `SELECT count(*)` in SQL for the same bbox exactly (38,275):

```
/rest/v1/occurrences?select=id
  &location->lon=gte.-126&location->lon=lte.-122
  &location->lat=gte.47&location->lat=lte.50.5
```

In supabase-js: `.gte('location->lon', -126).lte('location->lon', -122)` and likewise for `lat`.

**`->>` is a silent trap. Do not use it.** The same query with `->>` returned `Content-Range: */0` -- zero rows, no error. `->>` yields text, so the bounds compare lexically instead of numerically and quietly match nothing. Worth a comment at the call site.

**Consequence for scope:** the map query and the observation list need NO migration -- plain PostgREST filters on `from('occurrences')`. Only the calendar needs a schema change, because `occurrence_days` aggregates and the bbox must apply before the `GROUP BY`; the view exposes only `day` and `occurrence_count`, so there is nothing for a client-side predicate to bite on. That is a function taking bbox arguments, and it is the ONLY database work this issue requires. Design item 3 stands as written.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #357 (merged 2026-07-31). Regions filter the map, observation list and calendar day counts; ?r= in the URL; map outside the active region is shaded. Closes GH #16. Decision record: docs/decisions/022-regions-filter-data.md.

title: CI runs two different Supabase CLI versions
description:
build.yml starts the database with the CLI that supabase/setup-cli puts on PATH (pinned 2.53.6), but 'npm run gen-types' resolves node_modules/.bin/supabase first — the devDependency (2.107.0). So the DB is started by one CLI and its types generated by another, and neither is obviously the intended one.

This is what made salish-cr0's sibling bug hard to see: setup-cli exports SUPABASE_INTERNAL_IMAGE_REGISTRY=ghcr.io and 2.53.6 honours it for 'db start', while 2.107.0 ignored it for 'gen types' (supabase/cli#5785) and pulled postgres-meta from public.ecr.aws, hitting the 1 pull/sec anonymous limit.

deploy.yml also uses setup-cli 2.53.6 for 'supabase link', 'functions deploy' and 'db push' against production, so any unification has to weigh bumping the CLI that runs prod migrations.
design: Options: (a) drop setup-cli from build.yml and use npx supabase everywhere, setting SUPABASE_INTERNAL_IMAGE_REGISTRY=ghcr.io explicitly since that env var is currently a setup-cli side effect; (b) bump setup-cli's pin to match the devDependency. (a) gives one version and makes the registry choice explicit; (b) is smaller but leaves two sources of truth.
acceptance_criteria: A single Supabase CLI version is used across build.yml, and the version is traceable to one place.
notes: PR #382 open: https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/pull/382 — devDep ^2.114.0, build.yml uses it via pnpm exec (registry env now explicit at job level), deploy.yml's setup-cli resolves the version from pnpm-lock.yaml. Close on merge.
close_reason: Merged in PR #382 (ceafe7e): build.yml uses the supabase devDependency via pnpm exec, deploy.yml's setup-cli resolves the version from pnpm-lock.yaml — one CLI (2.114.0), one source of truth.

title: Ingest: legible operator-facing errors for non-JSON 200 responses (2F)

Requires amending decision 011's completeness invariant: replace expectedPageCount/isPaginationComplete (which depend on a stable total_results) with a terminal-short-page proof. Update the functional core + unit tests + a decision record.
design: Completeness becomes: fetched ascending-id pages until a terminal page returned fewer than per_page rows. total_results no longer load-bearing. Keyset by immutable id gives a consistent forward snapshot for reconcile (decision 011's real requirement).

title: Write paths fail silently — no user feedback on delete/refetch/geolocation errors

title: Refactor sighting-form.ts (815-line god component) and add tests
description:
src/sighting-form.ts is the largest, most complex file and has no tests. It mixes ~6 concerns: TanStack form wiring, three OpenLayers features (#observerFeature/#subjectFeature/#bearingFeature, firstUpdated:760-790, onCoordinatesChanged:728-758), photo upload + EXIF (appendPhotos:629-657), coordinate parsing (:124-139), bearing/distance geometry, and geolocation. It carries 27 non-null assertions on OL state (getGeometry()! etc.), each a latent runtime crash if OL state diverges.

Extract the map-feature controller and the photo pipeline into testable units; add tests for coordinate parsing, the payload-building onSubmit (:351-383), and validation. Note the lon/lat message bug and 'as any' are split into a separate quick-win bug. Coordinate with the ingest-migration functional-core discipline where relevant.
acceptance_criteria: sighting-form.ts split into focused units; the submit/validation/coordinate logic has unit tests; non-null assertions reduced or guarded.

title: Fix lon/lat validator message + as-any on the sighting write path
description:
Two quick correctness fixes in src/sighting-form.ts, separable from the larger refactor:
1) The longitude validator reports 'Expected a latitude between…' (sighting-form.ts:135) — wrong axis in the user-facing message on the longitude branch.
2) The core write path casts the hand-built payload through 'as any': supabase().rpc('upsert_observation', occurrence as any) (sighting-form.ts:146). The payload (built at :368-380) is never checked against UpsertObservationArgs (types.ts:37-46), which already exists. Type the payload so the compiler validates the write.
These are quick wins on the most safety-relevant path.
acceptance_criteria: Longitude validation error names longitude; upsert payload is typed as UpsertObservationArgs with no 'as any'.
notes: Merged in #422 (6e16a98) and deployed.
close_reason: Merged in #422. Longitude branch names longitude and quotes the longitude bounds; upsert payload is typed as UpsertObservationArgs with no 'as any' — fixed at the root by patching the nullable function args in PatchedDatabase. Validator exported and tested.

title: Add missing indexes on FK/JOIN columns used by the export and live map views
description: Columns joined by the nightly full-scan export and per-request map queries lack indexes: maplify.sightings.taxon_id (joined in dwc._maplify_occurrences + live views); public.observations.taxon_id and .contributor_id (dwc._native_occurrences / dwc.multimedia); inaturalist.observations.taxon_id (live occurrences view — only observed_at is indexed); happywhale.encounters.species_id/individual_id/user_id (live occurrences/presence views — only a date index). Low absolute cost today but these are exactly the columns the joins hit; add indexes (ship them the way collection_id already does).
acceptance_criteria: Each listed FK/join column has a supporting index; EXPLAIN on the export and occurrences view shows index usage rather than seq scans on these joins.
close_reason:
Measured against production 2026-09-18 and rejected; decision 045 records it.

The two access patterns the issue names do not want these indexes. The live map query enters each source table by its existing observed_at index and joins TO taxa on taxa_pkey — the referenced side — so sightings.taxon_id is the probe value, not a searched column, and an index on it cannot participate (38 rows in 14.6ms). The nightly export needs every row, so seq scan + hash join against a 513-row taxa hash is the correct plan and an index could only make it worse.

The usual justification for indexing a FK — a delete on the referenced table forcing a full scan of the referencing one — never fires: zero deletes ever on inaturalist.taxa (513 rows), public.contributors (17,037), happywhale.individuals (693), users (515) and species (127). contributors has 3.4M updates but id never changes, so no FK check.

Cost is real: maplify.sightings has taken 866,755 updates and inaturalist.observations 62,531 inserts, five minutes apart. Seven indexes there is write amplification for a read benefit that does not exist.

The one selective filter on a named column — fetchLastOwnOccurrence on contributor_id — runs over 364 rows after Postgres prunes the three NULL branches; its 132ms is the view's join cost, which salish-4h3 and salish-xfo are about.

Revisit on a changed premise, not on principle: a delete path opening on a referenced table, HappyWhale ingest being turned on, or a feature querying a source table BY one of these columns.

title: Add CloudFront security response headers (HSTS, frame-ancestors, nosniff)
description: The CDK Distribution sets no responseHeadersPolicy (infra/lib/infra-stack.ts:75-100). CSP is delivered only via <meta> in index.html, so frame-ancestors is ignored (spec: meta cannot set it), and there is no Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, or X-Content-Type-Options header anywhere — no clickjacking protection and no HSTS. Add a CloudFront ResponseHeadersPolicy in CDK with HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options policy, and ideally move CSP to a response header.
acceptance_criteria: Prod responses carry HSTS, nosniff, and frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options; verified via curl -I against salishsea.io.

title: Inner joins in the DwC export can silently drop occurrence records
description:
dwc._native_occurrences inner-joins public.contributors on contributor_id (20260621000000_dwc_view_rebuild.sql:98), but contributor_id was relaxed from NOT NULL to nullable (20260619203013_source_table_fk_columns.sql:44). A native observation with contributor_id IS NULL now vanishes from the published archive with no error, despite the migration comment asserting data stays 100% populated. Same shape: both export branches inner-join dwc.taxa_classification on taxon_id (:99, :197); maplify.sightings.taxon_id is NULL whenever taxon mapping fails (mapping covers only ~5 hardcoded names, 20260620000200_resolution_ingest.sql:107-113), so unclassifiable sightings are silently excluded.

Excluding unclassifiable rows is defensible, but the silence is not. Fix: count and log dropped rows per branch (emit to the build log / a metrics row) so silent shrinkage is visible, and decide explicitly whether null-contributor natives should be an error or a re-enforced NOT NULL.
acceptance_criteria: Export logs the count of rows dropped by each join; a regression that zeroes a branch is visible rather than silent.
close_reason: Merged in PR #451: dwc.export_coverage counts admitted/exported/dropped-per-join per branch; build.ts logs it and fails only when a branch with source rows exports none. Null-contributor natives: logged, not an error; contributor_id stays nullable.

title: Emit edge-handler build output outside the source tree (stop shipping tests to Lambda@Edge)
description:
infra/lib/infra-stack.ts:33 deploys the edge handler via lambda.Code.fromAsset('edge-handler'), which bundles the WHOLE directory to Lambda@Edge — including index.test.ts/.js and .d.ts. Two problems: (1) test files ship to a Lambda@Edge viewer trigger, which has a hard 1MB code limit; (2) tsc emits compiled JS next to sources, which shadowed the source under jest until moduleFileExtensions was fixed (see PR #299 / gh-299).

Fix options: emit to a dist/ outDir and point Code.fromAsset at dist/edge-handler, OR bundle the handler with esbuild at synth time so the source stays .ts-only and no committed/emitted JS is needed. Either way the deployed asset should contain only the handler runtime, not tests or sources.

Acceptance: cdk synth succeeds; the synthesized Lambda asset excludes test files and .ts sources; edge-handler jest suite still green. Add a check (test or synth assertion) that the asset contains index.js and not *.test.*.
close_reason: Closed

The reading-list step of GH #511: each Southern Resident whale, matriline and pod page carries a short, dated list of the best sources about it. Undecided (per #511): where the list lives (a committed file keyed by register identifier is the current proposal, beside the generated rows per decision 070), how it rolls up (matriline shows members' sources? pod shows matrilines'?), and where 'all Southern Residents' entries go; rewrite the research chronology's notes in a public voice, keeping 'unverified' flags.

Follows BeeAtlas ADR 0026 where its lessons don't depend on the renderer: a PMTiles extract we build and refresh, served from the Fly machine, attribution carried by the sources. OpenLayers draws it via ol-pmtiles + ol-mapbox-style; no move to MapLibre. title: A lost production deployment on a scheduled workflow (ingest heartbeat, register refresh) holds later runs silently; nothing watches for it
description: deploy.yml's watch job (salish-t3g.11, runbook gotcha 4) covers only deploy runs. ingest-heartbeat.yml and register-refresh.yml also bind the production environment with cancel-in-progress: false, so if GitHub loses one of their deployments, later runs queue behind it. A lost heartbeat run means monitoring stops alerting without saying so. Options: drop the environment binding where only a secret is needed (repo-level secret), cancel-in-progress: true for the heartbeat (idempotent, nothing to interrupt), or a staleness check elsewhere.

title: One definition of the Pacific day: occurrence-ids, manifest and snapshot import occurrence-days's DAY_ZONE/DAY_EXPR instead of carrying copies
description: occurrence-days.ts now holds DAY_ZONE and DAY_EXPR as module constants; occurrence-ids.ts, manifest.ts and snapshot.ts each carry a hand copy 'as in occurrence-days.ts'. Stelis's identity check holds occurrence-days to salishsea.rkt's OCCURRENCE-DAY, but nothing holds the three siblings to it: a zone or format change in one and not the others puts an id in a day whose file does not hold it. Export the constants and import them — and add occurrence-days.ts to those three tasks' #:code lists in Stelis's salishsea.rkt, or a change to the constant would not invalidate them.
close_reason: PR #628 (1ff17facd376055fe849bea72b0ae9051ca3686a): scripts/read-path/pacific-day.ts holds DAY_ZONE and dayOf(); occurrence-days, occurrence-ids, calendar, manifest and snapshot import it; a test holds it to src/constants.ts's OBSERVATION_TIME_ZONE. Stelis 9a2d0f5 lists it among those tasks' (and happywhale's) code; fly/stelis-commit moved to it.

title: Ecotype page compares its matrilines on the map
description:
Peter, 2026-10-06: like BeeAtlas's genus pages, an ecotype page should show its matrilines' sightings on a map, one colour each, so differences in their behaviour (range, habitat, season) are visible.

Today /ecotypes/0000002/Biggs lists its 132 matrilines A-Z and draws one undifferentiated map of 8,164 pooled points (decision 017). The links file (read-path/profiles/ecotypes/<id>.links.json) carries no matriline per point.

BeeAtlas (beeatlas _pages/genus.njk, data/species_maps.py, ADR-0022): a prerendered SVG map, hues spaced evenly by position, and the species list with its swatches as the legend. Nothing is interactive.

Prod, 2026-10-06 (group_occurrences, is_present, reports that name a matriline as a unit):
- 70 of the 132 matrilines have any sightings; 32 have 50 or more. Leaders: T065A 1249, T099 1116, T137 975, T046 742, T124D 534; then a long tail.
- Of the 6,582 sightings that name a matriline, 1,852 (28%) name two or more, because Bigg's travel together. A single dot has no single colour.
- A report that names only an individual reaches a matriline only through the register (decision 050). Whether the comparison counts those is a choice to make.

Design question, open: 70 hues can't be told apart (BeeAtlas hits the same limit in big genera). Options:
(a) Small multiples: one small static map per matriline in the list, prerendered like BeeAtlas's SVGs. Needs no colour, no JS, and shows a co-travelling sighting on each matriline's map. Best for comparing range.
(b) A coloured overlay on the existing map, about 6 matrilines at a time (the top ones by default) picked from the list, the rest grey. Lets you see two groups on one map, but needs the island to know each point's matrilines.
(c) Both: (a) on the page, (b) as a compare view.

Caveat for the page's copy: sighting density follows observers (Puget Sound shorelines, ferries) as much as whales. Comparing matrilines is fairer than reading one map alone, since they share the same observer effort, but it is still not a range map. The honesty invariant (decision 015) applies.

Related: SRKW as a second ecotype (salishsea-io#511) makes an ecotype-vs-ecotype comparison possible too.
close_reason: PR #629 (0c5182f): a small static map per reported matriline on the ecotype page, all at one Salish Sea extent, most-reported first; decision 067; Stelis 8546cfa. Option 2 (colour overlay) not built.

title: Retain the preview handler's old Lambda@Edge versions instead of failing to delete them on every deploy
description: Every deploy that changes infra/lib/edge-handler spends ~6 minutes in CloudFormation cleanup: the edge stack (edge-lambda-stack-c82eb…, us-east-1) tries to delete the previous AWS::Lambda::Version of OgMetaFunction, Lambda refuses while CloudFront still holds replicas ('Lambda was unable to delete … replicated function'), it retries three times three minutes apart, then gives up and marks the stack UPDATE_COMPLETE with 'One or more resources could not be deleted' and a CDK warning about resources that may incur charges. Seen on 19 deploy days since 2026-06-18 (stack events), most recently 2026-10-06 17:20-17:26 UTC; the function has 35 versions. Fix: in infra/lib/infra-stack.ts give the edge function's version a RETAIN removal policy (currentVersionOptions: {removalPolicy: RemovalPolicy.RETAIN}, or the equivalent on the experimental EdgeFunction), so CloudFormation never attempts the delete. Versions accumulate exactly as they already do; prune old ones in bulk now and then once CloudFront has released them (aws lambda delete-function --qualifier N succeeds after replicas clear, typically hours).
notes: docs/runbook/deploys.md 'Gotcha 1 — DELETE_FAILED on an old Lambda@Edge version' already explains the symptom; update it when this lands.

title: occurrence-days, occurrence-ids and calendar write only the keys Stelis names (after its keyed-relation observation)
description: Blocked on Stelis's step 2 (a relation observed by key column). Then: honour STELIS_REBUILD_KEYS (write the named days/shards/months into the existing dir instead of swapping the directory whole), let prune-keys! remove emptied days, and declare the tasks partial in salishsea.rkt.
notes:
Merged #626 (0dc7dd5), deploy run 37537116109 in progress with Stelis 775b18c. Verified on a live copy before merge: 4,408 computed keys == 4,408 day files; full run byte-identical to the deployed files (1.2 s laptop); partial run restores named days only (0.2 s), creates an added day, removes an emptied one, sweeps .partial and days.previous. Expect on Fly: first build after deploy swaps whole (its basis is the per-column map, so every day is named, past the 500 limit); from the second build '⇒ partial: rebuilding N key(s)' and 'N of K named day(s) rewritten in place'. Follow-up salish-9uu.8.3 (one day constant across scripts).
LIVE 2026-10-06 22:24:54Z (Fly v88, Stelis 775b18c): the first build in which the occurrences changed went straight to '⇒ partial: rebuilding 1 key(s)' then 'days/: 1 of 1 named day(s) rewritten in place, 41 occurrences; the rest as they were' — about a second, no identity-check remark (the directory matched the keyset). It went partial at once rather than swapping whole first because the three preceding builds had re-derived occurrences (identical rows) and so recorded per-day maps at the digest the consumer had consumed.
close_reason: Live on Fly v88: a changed sighting rewrites its one day file in place, ~1 s instead of writing 4,408 and swapping.

title: Build the Fly image alongside the deploy job, not after it
description: From the Fable review of salish-t3g.5: fly deploy --build-only --push touches nothing in production, but the fly job runs it after the whole deploy job (db push, S3, cdk), so every push waits Test → Deploy → a full remote image build → lock → switch before smoke. Split fly/deploy.sh's build from its switch: a build-and-push job beside deploy, keyed by the same tag (commit + Stelis pin), and the lock-and-switch after the deploy job. Saves several minutes per deploy; nothing is wrong without it.
close_reason: Live 2026-10-06: #618 (image built beside Test via fly/deploy.sh build, switch after deploy; S3 site build/sync retired) + #620 (ca-certificates so sentry-cli uploads). Run 37509261134 green; first run's total 5m35s; Sentry artifact bundle uploaded from the shipped build.

title: Retire the Supabase config the OG handler and card renderer no longer read
description: salish-9uu.5 moved both Lambdas' native-sighting fallback from Supabase to the write API, so infra-stack.ts's synth-time baking of SUPABASE_URL/SUPABASE_ANON_KEY into edge-handler/config.js (and the --context supabaseAnonKey the deploy passes), the renderer's SUPABASE_* environment, and infra.test.ts's assertion on it are dead. Left for a separate change: another agent had infra-stack.ts open on 2026-10-06, and nothing reads the values now.

title: A save-triggered build publishes faster: no quiet period for a save, and skip the ingests
description: After the public read bridges the gap, shorten it: the coalescer's 10 s quiet period was tuned for Realtime bursts and is pure delay for a save the API itself reports; and a save-triggered build need not run the three ingests (they run every five minutes anyway), only the native path: snapshot from the store, derive, day file, id shard, calendar, manifest. Keep the 120 s spacing and the lock retry. Stelis side: a target set below the ingests, or --from semantics.
notes:
Stelis side done: --downstream <task> (st-wzk, stelis f364281, pushed). salishsea side committed on branch save-build-downstream (3040699): build.sh passes args, BUILD_COMMAND='/app/fly/build.sh --downstream snapshot', coalescer quietMs 0, docs. CodeRabbit CLI hit the org's rate limit / spending cap at 16:0xZ (17 min wait); retry scheduled before opening the PR. Deploy needs STELIS_SHA=f364281 (full: f364281da8602db8c4b360d2e73e47fb94426e3b). Verify on Fly: time 'flock /data/build.lock /app/fly/build.sh --downstream snapshot' by hand.
Done 2026-10-06: PR #613 merged (dc23535, rebased onto #612's pin file; fly/stelis-commit = f364281). Fly v83 deployed; the Dockerfile's --downstream check passed in the image build. Hand run on the machine: 'Building the whole graph — 13 task(s), downstream of snapshot', snapshot + manifest ran, eleven cached, 8 s wall / engine 2.4 s / tasks 6.2 s with nothing changed in the store; a real save adds the derivations (~20 s). Local review (CodeRabbit CLI rate-limited) findings fixed in the second commit.
close_reason: Delivered and live (Fly v83): the save-triggered build is --downstream snapshot with no quiet period and a 30 s spacing.

title: A home for the withheld catalogue text (D-21) before Postgres goes (064/065)
description: Decision 064 left in Postgres the catalogue text rights policy D-21 keeps off every page: an individual's Bigg's-sheet notes, a nickname's story. It is curated, not user-written, so by 065's rule it is not the store's. Where it lives once Postgres is retired is undecided: Peter's call.

title: Retire Postgres from the build's code once it is no longer the way back (065)
description: After the cutover (salish-9uu.3.8, 2026-10-05) Postgres is frozen and kept only as the way back. Once that is given up: delete scripts/read-path/listen.ts, snapshot.ts's Postgres path (and READ_PATH_STORE as a switch), scripts/feedback/notify.ts and its Postgres tests, the VITE_WRITE_SOURCE=supabase branches in the frontend; declare the store in Stelis's salishsea.rkt as an 'authoritative producerless input of the snapshot; drop the occurrences_changed broadcast; decide what becomes of the Supabase project.

title: A maintenance mode for the build machine: builds pause, the site keeps serving, the health check keeps answering
description: Operator work on the Fly machine — backfilling a mirror over months, repairing the snapshot, measuring a task — competes with the five-minute build for a 1 GB machine and the build lock, and today the only tool is flock around each command. Peter, 2026-10-04, pointing at beeline PR #132 (a maintenance responder that answers the health check so flipping the mode no longer hangs a deploy): do something similar here. The salishsea version is simpler because the site is static: with READ_PATH_MAINTENANCE=1 in the machine's environment, fly/start.sh starts Caddy and the redirect server only — every published file keeps serving, Fly's check on / keeps passing, so 'fly machine update --env' completes in one boot — and does not start supercronic, the change listener or the boot build, so the snapshot, the mirrors and /data/build.lock are free. Caddy serves /status/maintenance.json while the mode is on; the heartbeat reads it and reports a planned window instead of filing 'stale'/'unpublished' issues (still alarming if a window runs longer than a day). Leaving the mode (update the env back) boots normally, with the boot build. The read-path runbook replaces 'take the lock' for anything longer than a query with 'enter maintenance'. Visitors notice nothing; covered_through stops advancing for the window.
notes: 2026-10-04 (Fable): DONE, #578 (e85bb45), live Fly v56. Exercised on the machine: 'fly machine update --env READ_PATH_MAINTENANCE=1 -y' completed in one boot (no hang: / kept answering Fly's check), site 200, /status/maintenance.json 200 with since; no supercronic, listener or racket running; a measurement ran with MemAvailable 724 MB and nothing competing. '--env READ_PATH_MAINTENANCE=0 -y': flag 404 again, the machine's other env (FLY_PROCESS_GROUP, PRIMARY_REGION) preserved, and the boot build ran within two minutes (ingest runs at 22:30–22:31Z). The heartbeat's maintenance branch is unit-tested; its live path was not triggered (the window lasted ~3 minutes, under the 30-minute checks).
close_reason: Maintenance mode shipped (#578) and exercised live: in and out in one boot each, site serving throughout, builds paused, heartbeat aware.

title: read_path grants test 'sees every row of what the occurrences derive from' is flaky in the full suite
description: supabase/read-path-grants.test.ts > 'read_path sees every row of what the occurrences derive from' failed once in a full local run on 2026-10-04 (after db reset + supabase/ci-seed.sql), then passed alone twice and in the next full run. Likely races another DB-backed test file writing to the same source tables concurrently (vitest runs files in parallel). Not yet seen in CI. Fix: compare within one snapshot/transaction, or serialise the DB-backed files.

title: Docs sweep after the cutover: architecture line, decision amendments, runbooks
description: What a reader finds today disagrees with what runs. CLAUDE.md:111 and PRODUCT.md:59 still describe S3/CloudFront hosting, an edge function that rewrites profile paths and 301s designations (removed in #555), and a nightly workflow building the DwC-A. Decisions 008 and 055 carry no 'amended by 061' pointer (docs/decisions/README.md rows still read 'accepted'); 015 and 034 have no amendment though #555 removed most of what they describe; 061's consequence 'runs recorded by Stelis's build history and the operator build log' was sidestepped by the separate runs log (#559) and should say so. derive/dwc.sql:6 cites derive-dwc.test.ts, which does not exist — the twin check is in derive-occurrences.test.ts:78-91. No runbook names the mirror backfill (ingest-maplify.ts / ingest-inaturalist.ts take <start> <end>; the flock /data/build.lock dance; iNaturalist's pace), which 061 relies on for 'a lost mirror is rebuilt'. And ingest-runs.ts:99-102 publishes error.message at salishsea.io/status/ingest-runs.json — fine while every source is unauthenticated, worth a comment so a future authenticated source does not land its token there. Found in the 2026-10-04 review of salish-xv35.
notes: 2026-10-04 (Fable): PR #574 — CLAUDE.md architecture line and PRODUCT.md deployment constraint rewritten for Fly + the build; decisions index rows 008/012/015/034/049/055 carry their amendments; 015 and 034 amended in-file (edge rewrite and 301s moved to Fly); 061's heartbeat consequence amended (run log beside the mirrors, two records of one fact); dwc.sql cites the right test; ingest-runs.ts notes the public error text; new docs/runbook/read-path-build.md (what runs, state and provenance, the build lock for operator queries after the 2026-10-04 OOM, backfill commands, the name-guard hold, measuring a task). Not done here: docs/data-provenance.md (not read this session; check it next time something touches provenance).
close_reason: #574 (f5313a6): architecture line, decision index rows and in-file amendments, 061's heartbeat consequence, dwc.sql's test reference, the public-error-text note, and docs/runbook/read-path-build.md.

title: A contributor's just-saved sighting for 'today' errors until the next build after Pacific midnight
description: src/salish-sea.ts's signed-in branch awaits fetchDayOccurrences and the live native query together, and read-path.ts fetchDayOccurrences throws when the requested day is past the manifest's covered_through. Between Pacific midnight and the 00:01 build (fly/crontab) a contributor who just saved a sighting for the new day sees an error instead of their row — before #551 they read Supabase and saw it at once. Bounded to a few minutes by the cron and the change listener, but it is a regression of exactly decision 055's case (the contributor sees what they wrote). Treat an uncovered day as empty for the overlay rather than an error, or fall back to the live query alone for that day. Found in the 2026-10-04 review of salish-xv35.
close_reason: #573 (ed47913): the signed-in branch treats a not-built-yet day as empty on the file side and shows the live native rows with a notice; NotBuiltYet is its own error class. Deployed with the next Fly release.

title: A silently capped Maplify response over the anti-entropy month would delete ~1,100 sightings in one transaction
description: reconcileWindow (ingest-maplify.ts:104-122) deletes every stored id in [start, end+1) absent from the response, and fetch-maplify.ts has no completeness proof beyond 'the response parses whole' — Maplify does not say how many rows exist. Postgres's ingest had the same exposure over ten days; xv35.15's month-long anti-entropy window (#547) makes a truncated or capped response delete a month's sightings (about 1,100 unfiltered) in one transaction, repaired only on the next successful fetch of that month, which the random month choice may not revisit for a long time. Options: a plausibility floor (refuse to delete more than N% of a window's stored rows in one run, as the integrity gate does for record counts), or re-fetch a window a second time before honouring its deletes. Found in the 2026-10-04 review of salish-xv35.
close_reason: A scheduled run refuses to delete more than 10% of a window's stored sightings (window of 20+); a manual backfill has no floor. MERGED cfc7723, deployed.

title: With the agreement gates gone, the build's SQL is the only version of the rules: four places it could answer differently from Postgres (all settled 2026-10-04)
description: Until the cutover, every answer the build computed was checked row for row against Postgres's. Those checks are gone, so the build's SQL is the only version of the rules, and nothing would notice if it answered differently from what Postgres used to. Four places where it could, all settled 2026-10-04: (1) Which animal a code points at — when a code in a sighting's text matches more than one animal or matriline, the SQL picked one at random; no code matches two today, but the build decides 'nothing changed' by comparing file contents, so a random pick could churn files after a register edition reassigns codes. DONE #575: a fixed order. (2) How names sort — when a bout carries two identifiers ('J pod', 'J27') their order in the file depends on the text sort; the build sorts by Unicode's rules (ICU) and Postgres on Supabase might have sorted by glibc's. DONE: production's pg_database says its collation provider is ICU (en_US.UTF-8), the same rule; recorded at the collation in occurrences.sql. (3) Which taxon an entity belongs to — the review thought the build skipped a step Postgres takes; both read, they match. Nothing to do. (4) Wide spaces in codes — Postgres treats an em-space as a space when folding a name; the build's regex engine treated only ASCII spaces as spaces. DONE #575. Also asked: build the same data twice and compare files (Stelis's determinism rule). Shown by the 2026-10-04 boot builds: the derivation reran on unchanged data and produced identical output, and the tasks after it cut off on that.
notes:
2026-10-04 (Fable): (1) DISTINCT ON now ORDER BY occurrence, code, individual_id, social_group_id — deterministic whatever the data holds; the CI twin test (derive-occurrences.test.ts) still checks agreement with Postgres. (4) register_fold's whitespace class is [\s\p{Z}]+, Unicode like Postgres's and src/fold.ts's. (3) Checked against migration 20260921010000: Postgres's taxon_for calls taxon_entity_for ONCE and then reads the mapping; the twin joins taxon_for on taxon_entity's answer — the same chain, no second hop. No change. (2) COLLATE en_us: unresolved; needs SHOW lc_collate on production (one read-only query, Peter's call) — if glibc en_US.UTF-8, the twin's ICU collation orders ties like ['J pod','J27'] differently and should switch to a byte-order tiebreak that both sides agree on. Build-twice: the 2026-10-04 boot build (Fly v54) reran derive-occurrences on the hold token alone and cut off on identical output, and calendar, the id index, the candidates and the links each reran on a changed input and cut off — the derivation rebuilds the same bytes from the same data; a formal twice-build on a copied snapshot has not been run.
2026-10-04 (Fable): SHOW lc_collate answered via pg_database on production: datcollate en_US.UTF-8, datlocprovider = 'i' — the database's collation provider is ICU (PostgreSQL 17.6). The twin's COLLATE en_us is DuckDB's ICU en_US: the same rules. No change; a comment at the collation records the fact so nobody asks again. All four items settled.
close_reason: All four settled: DISTINCT ON ordered and Unicode whitespace folded (#575); taxon_for matches Postgres; production's collation provider is ICU en_US (pg_database, 2026-10-04), so COLLATE en_us is the same rule — recorded at the collation in occurrences.sql.

title: occurrence-ids.ts and snapshot-tables.ts run DuckDB without the measured budget
description: On the 1 GB no-swap Fly machine, two scripts create DuckDB instances with no budget() call, so DuckDB's limit is 80% of RAM and nothing spills: scripts/read-path/occurrence-ids.ts:27 and scripts/read-path/snapshot-tables.ts:325, the latter used by all four page tasks and profile-index. Both then hold full result sets in JS. Inputs are small today, so no incident; but decision 061 says peak memory of every script is measured before deploy, and salish-xv35.10 / Stelis b530ded covered 'seven tasks' precisely because these were not included. Apply duckdb-budget.ts, measure peak RSS on Fly for the page tasks, record the numbers on this bead. Found in the 2026-10-04 review of salish-xv35.
notes: 2026-10-04 (Fable), after #567 deployed (Fly v52, Stelis 0d38269): peak RSS run alone under the build lock, into a scratch EXPORT_DIR, sampled from /proc VmHWM (the image has no time(1)): occurrence-ids 163 MB (65,872 ids, 256 shards); individual-pages 268 MB (510 pages); matriline-pages 198 MB (132 pages). DuckDB is capped at 64 MB in each, so what remains is node: the page render holds every document and page in memory. MemAvailable before the runs: 670 MB. individual-pages is the second-largest task on the machine after derive-occurrences (380 MB, salish-xv35.17) and dwca (376 MB); if a page kind grows, stream pages out rather than raise the cap.
close_reason: Caps applied (#567, Stelis 0d38269); peaks measured on Fly and recorded in notes.

title: The Orcasound mirror filters to biophony at ingest, where Maplify's and iNaturalist's keep everything upstream said
description: ingest-orcasound.ts:129 calls reconcile(corpus.bouts, []), whose upsert is fetched.filter(isIngestable) (scripts/ingest/orcasound.ts) — category === 'biophony'. For Maplify, Peter's 2026-10-02 amendment to decision 061 moved exactly this kind of scope decision out of the mirror and into the derivation ('a mirror is exactly a mirror'), and iNaturalist followed. Orcasound's mirror does not hold what upstream said. A bout re-filed anthrophony→biophony is handled, so this is a policy inconsistency rather than a data loss, but the next person reading 061 will expect one rule. Move the filter into derive/sources.sql or occurrences.sql, keep the whole corpus in the mirror, and amend 061's Orcasound sentence. Found in the 2026-10-04 review of salish-xv35.
notes: 2026-10-04 (Fable): DONE, #579 (5553aa5), live Fly v57 (Stelis 16d8c38 unchanged). On the machine after the boot build: the mirror holds 163 biophony, 45 anthrophony and 22 geophony bouts — the 67 non-biophony ones are exactly the '67 new records' the ingest's receipt reported, so the biophony set the derivation keeps is unchanged; build.occurrences has 100 Orcasound rows. The CI twin test (mirror written from Postgres's biophony-only table, labelled as such) still derives Postgres's answer row for row. An old mirror is migrated before the fetch, so a failed first fetch could not have left the derivation an unreadable mirror.
close_reason: Orcasound's scope rule moved from the mirror to the derivation, as Maplify's and iNaturalist's (#579); the mirror keeps every category, the derivation keeps biophony; verified live.

title: derive-occurrences peaks at 380 MB on Fly since it reads the SQLite mirrors
description: Measured 2026-10-03 on Fly (shared-cpu-4x, 1 GB, no swap): derive-occurrences run alone peaks at 380 MB RSS (MemAvailable low 402 MB); in a build the engine adds ~184 MB, so roughly 220 MB would be left. macOS measured 386 MB vs 324 MB before the switch to mirrors (#554). It succeeds, but the margin is thin. Find what grew (likely DuckDB's sqlite scanner materializing mirror tables, or the iNat taxa UNION) and cap or stream it.
notes:
2026-10-04: dwca task (new) peaks 376 MB RSS on Fly run alone (min MemAvailable 429 MB), same order as derive-occurrences; both load DuckDB extensions (dwca: spatial).

2026-10-04 review: not resolvable by reading. The JS side is small (streamed extractions, parentOf map, id arrays). The 128 MB cap does not cover the sqlite extension's own allocations, and source_inaturalist_taxa (a view over a SQLite scan plus the Postgres-taxa union) is referenced from six places and re-scanned each time. First experiment: materialize the four source_* views as TEMP TABLEs once after attachSources — one scan each, then buffer-managed under the cap — and compare RSS.
2026-10-04 (Fable) measured on Fly against copies of the live snapshot (338 MB file) and mirrors, under the lock: floor (node + DuckDB + ICU + sqlite loaded, everything attached, nothing run) 120 MB; whole derivation 369-389 MB. Per stage, RSS vs DuckDB's own accounting: after the JS text extraction +65 MB (DuckDB counts 11); after the final occurrences query +157 MB (DuckDB counts 39). Memory cap 96 MB OOMs in the final query at 77.8/91.5 used, so ~100 MB of buffer pool is genuinely needed; 128 is right. Hypotheses tested: materializing the source_* views as temp tables → 445 MB (worse); exporting them to parquet inside the process → 450 MB (the export itself, via the sqlite scanner, cost 150 MB of RSS DuckDB did not count); reading pre-made parquet with NO sqlite extension loaded → 365 MB. So the SQLite attach is worth ~20 MB, not the problem; the final query's working set and the extraction step held in-process are. Candidates left: run the extraction in its own process (peaks don't add; ~-65 MB), build the table branch by branch rather than one five-way UNION (untested), allocator flush knob (testing).
2026-10-04 (Fable), conclusion. Per-INSERT profile of the final step: the Maplify insert +82 MB RSS, the iNaturalist insert +81 MB, the other three ~0; DuckDB's accounting stays ~40 MB throughout, and neither block is returned afterwards. Tested against that: allocator_flush_threshold=4mb + background threads → 370 MB (−15); glibc trim/mmap/arena tunables → 364 MB (−20; the x86_64 DuckDB build allocates through its own jemalloc anyway); pre-made parquet with no SQLite extension loaded → 365 MB (−20). So the two blocks are live working set of those branches' pipelines (joins, photo lists, the JSON document), not allocator retention, and not the SQLite scanner — Peter's parquet hand-off would save ~20 MB and is not worth a second data path. What would move it: (a) run the JS text extraction in a child process writing its table to a temp file — peaks don't add across processes, ~−65 MB, mechanical; (b) split the Maplify and iNaturalist branches into materialized temp stages so less is live at once — speculative, needs its own measurement; (c) accept: 365–389 MB against ~650 MB available when a build starts, tasks sequential, cap of 128 MB verified necessary (96 OOMs). Recommendation: (a) if we want margin back, else (c). Copies and throwaway script removed from the machine.
2026-10-04 (Fable), Peter: find equivalent behaviour without JS rather than move the extraction out of process. Done: RE2's \b in place of Postgres's \m/\M; the two differ only where a non-ASCII letter or digit touches a code or a direction word, and over all 52,988 production texts (911 with non-ASCII) they answer identically. derive/extract.sql holds the two macros; occurrences.sql and dwc.sql call them where Postgres calls the functions; derive/extract.ts and its streamed table are gone. Expected: the derive process no longer grows 65 MB before its heaviest query; to be measured on Fly after deploy.
2026-10-04 (Fable): the SQL extraction (#577, Stelis 16d8c38, Fly v56) did NOT reduce the peak: derive-occurrences measured 415 and 421 MB in maintenance mode (nothing competing, MemAvailable 724 MB), against 369–389 with the JS step. The regexes now run inside the Maplify and iNaturalist inserts and add to that live working set, where the JS step's 65 MB was retained heap after the fact. Next: compute the two extractions once into a small temp table before the views, and join it as the views did before — regex work done and released before the heavy inserts. Measuring.
2026-10-04 (Fable), closing. Same-session comparison under the lock: extractions inline in the inserts 366–373 MB; computed once into a temp table and joined 369–376 MB — no difference, and both ~45 MB below the 415–421 measured in maintenance mode an hour earlier with the same code. So run-to-run variance on this machine is ±40 MB and swamps any placement effect; the JS step's removal neither helped nor hurt. What is known for certain: floor 120 MB; ~100 MB of buffer pool genuinely needed (96 OOMs); the Maplify and iNaturalist inserts each add ~80 MB of live working set DuckDB does not account for; the SQLite attach is worth ~20 MB; allocator knobs ~15–20 MB. Nothing to stream or cap. Accepting: 365–420 MB against ~650–720 MB available when a task starts, tasks sequential. Reopen if the data grows or the margin shrinks; the lever then is restructuring the Maplify and iNaturalist branches into materialized stages, measured one at a time.
close_reason: Measured and understood: the peak is the derivation's own working set in two branches plus a 120 MB floor, not the mirrors or the extraction; accepted at 365–420 MB against ~650 MB available. JS extraction removed along the way (#577).

title: Read-path scripts' entry-point check fails silently on a path needing URL encoding
description: CodeRabbit on #546: every scripts/read-path/*.ts ends with if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) await main(). import.meta.url is percent-encoded; argv isn't. A checkout path with a space (or any character needing encoding) makes the comparison false, main() never runs, and the script exits 0 having done nothing, which a Stelis task records as success. Not reachable today (/app on Fly, ~/dev locally), but silent. Fix repo-wide with pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href, or a shared isMain(import.meta.url) helper.
close_reason: #549: every script uses import.meta.main (Node ≥24.2; Fly 24.13.1, workflows ^24.10). Verified from a path with a space, through a symlink, and under tsx.

title: Local-Supabase test files race each other under parallel vitest
description: Found 2026-10-02 (xv35.7). vitest runs files in parallel against one database, and ~20 test files commit rows (scripts/ingest/persist.test.ts, most of supabase/*.test.ts) while others count or snapshot the same tables (supabase/read-path-grants.test.ts compares read_path's counts with anon's; scripts/read-path/derive-occurrences.test.ts snapshots and compares). Locally, a full run fails one of those 1-3 times in 5; e.g. a persist.test Maplify row whose comments change after Postgres resolved its collection shows as 'maplify: 1 differ in collection'. CI on main has passed 15 of 15, so it bites mostly on a busy local DB. The two equivalence tests (ingest-maplify, ingest-orcasound) now write inside an always-rolled-back transaction (scripts/read-path/rolled-back.ts). Options: the same helper for the other writers; or a vitest project that runs DB-touching files serially.

title: Every salishsea commit rewrites ~375 profile pages: the release id is stamped into the hashed bundle
description: Found 2026-10-02 (xv35.12 verification). Stelis --history on Fly: every deploy's boot build (builds 332, 354, 362, 365) changes 305 individual pages and 70 matriline pages; the builds between deploys leave all keys identical. #545 changed no src/, so the page bytes depend on something per image build — likely the Vite-built shell or its manifest (hashed as code by the page tasks), e.g. a per-build Sentry release or non-reproducible asset hashes. Harmless today (pages are correct), but a published page should be a function of the data and the source. Next: fly ssh, copy one changed page before/after a deploy (or diff dist/ across two image builds) to see what moves.
notes:
CAUSE FOUND 2026-10-02 (Opus): the bundle is reproducible per commit, not per image build. Three Stelis-only redeploys of salishsea 2164f5a left the page tasks cached (their Vite shell + manifest, hashed as code, were identical). The churn comes from fly/deploy.sh passing GITHUB_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD), which the Vite build stamps into the bundle as the release a feedback report names (decision 039). So any salishsea commit, even one touching no src/ (#545), changes the bundle's hash, then each kind's shell, then every page with a map island (305 individual + 70 matriline). Harmless. Options if it matters (undecided, Peter's call): (a) leave it, a deploy is rare next to data changes; (b) keep the release id out of the hashed bundle, e.g. read it from a small unhashed file or a meta tag at runtime, so assets change only when code does; (c) stamp the hash of src/ rather than the commit.
Peter, 2026-10-03: put the release id in a manifest file (or similar) rather than the hashed bundle, so the bundle's hashes and the page shells change only when code does. Check first what injects it: vite.config's __RELEASE__ define (GITHUB_SHA) and possibly @sentry/vite-plugin's release injection; Sentry.init needs the release at init, so a runtime fetch of an unhashed /release.json (or similar) has to come before it, or Sentry gets it from a non-hashed source. Touches the live site's JS: confirm before shipping.
close_reason: #552 (f8fed7f): release id moved to dist/release.json, read at runtime by feedback (non-blocking) and Sentry (event processor); Sentry plugin inject:false. Two builds differing only in GITHUB_SHA differ only in release.json. Deployed AWS (smoke green) and Fly. Still to observe: next no-src deploy leaves page tasks cached.

title: Travel speeds for more species and groups, typical and maximum separately
description: travelSpeedKmH (src/constants.ts) holds one figure per taxon, used as a typical speed and, tripled, as a maximum. Those differ, and the orca figures came from Dave Bain with some margin added. Needs: separate typical and maximum speeds; figures for more species and groups (e.g. Bigg's vs residents, which differ in how they move); and a recorded source for each. The research note on PR #533 (docs/research/segment-tracking-and-position-evidence.md) cites Williams & Noren 2009: 5.8 km/h for northern residents. Context: salishsea-io#445.

title: Upgrade beads 1.2.2 -> 1.3.1 once Homebrew ships 1.3.1, then unpin
description:
beads is brew-pinned at 1.2.2 (see bd memory beads-homebrew-pin). 1.3.1 was tagged 2026-09-30 upstream; Homebrew still had 1.3.0 that day. Skip 1.3.0 (beads#6142, write-dead store; fixed in 1.3.1 by https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/6547).

Release notes: https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/tag/v1.3.0 (Upgrading Notes, Breaking changes for v1.2.2 users).

Procedure:
1. brew update && brew info beads — confirm stable is 1.3.1+.
2. WITH 1.2.2, in every store (salishsea-io, salishsea-io-read-path, -research, -segments, beeatlas, beeline, stelis): bd dolt push; bd export --all -o .beads/backup/pre-1.3-$(date +%Y%m%d).jsonl
3. Confirm no other machine runs bd against these stores' Dolt remotes (mixed versions refuse each other).
4. brew unpin beads && brew upgrade beads; which -a bd
5. In each store: bd version; bd doctor; bd dolt push (from this one migrating machine).
6. Behaviour changes to absorb: bd search includes closed by default; bd update --status enforces close policy; dated defers re-wake onto bd ready.
7. bd forget beads-homebrew-pin; update .beads/README.md / docs/agents/issue-tracker.md if anything there changes.
close_reason: Upgraded to 1.3.1 on 2026-10-02: Mac (brew, salishsea-io/beeatlas/beeline/stelis stores migrated v53->v66 and pushed) and maderas (~/.local/bin/bd, beeline store; 1.2.2 kept as bd-1.2.2). Pre-1.3 exports in each store's .beads/backup/pre-1.3-20261002.jsonl. Left unpinned.

title: Find what takes a heavy read-path build's free memory to ~236 MB on Fly
description: Measured 2026-10-01 on two data-changed builds (occurrences moved, so days/calendar/ids/pages rerun): min MemAvailable 241 MB and 236 MB, both minutes after the snapshot finished, during occurrence-days or the page tasks. The memory note recorded 337 MB as the minimum for a full build after #521 (streaming day files), so something lost ~100 MB, and it isn't the snapshot (226 MB peak after #532, below its pre-#531 249 MB). Measure each heavy task's VmHWM on Fly (occurrence-days, the four page tasks, calendar, ids) the way snapshot was measured in #532 (sample /proc/<pid>/status; run as app with HOME set), and compare with the earlier figures. Not urgent: 236 MB is margin, the outages happened near zero. But xv35.2 adds a derive task to every data-changed build, so know the budget first.
notes: Peter 2026-10-01: a bigger Fly machine is acceptable, but only as an intentional decision after measuring — not the first response. So this bead's output is the per-task measurements and, where a task can be made leaner, the fix; if one genuinely needs the memory, propose the bump with the numbers.
close_reason: Answered and fixed (#541, Stelis b530ded). The low point was occurrence-days (366 MB on Fly, uncapped DuckDB) beside Racket (~130 MB). Capped it and calendar via scripts/read-path/duckdb-budget.ts (one helper for all seven scripts): calendar 275 -> 239 MB; occurrence-days 426 -> ~380 MB on macOS, because most of its memory is node-api holding the sorted result (152 MB for the same query in the DuckDB CLI); string_agg assembly was byte-identical but 854 MB. Post-deploy Fly re-measurement was invalidated by CPU throttling (92% steal) — see xv35.5. A further cut needs a different streaming design for occurrence-days.

title: DB-backed test files share committed state and race in parallel
description: taxon-resolution.test.ts commits inaturalist.taxa writes while other files run. #527 scoped occurrence-store's stale-mark count to its own transaction (24/25 → 1/145 paired failures); the residual is likely its global drift() check. Options: roll back taxon-resolution's writes, or run DB-backed files serially.

title: Bump pnpm/action-setup to v6.1.0 in the remaining workflows
description: ingest-heartbeat.yml moved to v6.1.0 (ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413) in the salish-1zgd PR; nine other workflows still pin v6.0.10 (0977fd99…).

title: Herring spawning grounds as a reference layer (GH #453)
description: The second layer GH #453 names (https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/issues/453). Decision 058 built the switch; adding a layer is a row in src/reference-layers.ts plus a layer in obs-map. Blocked on a data source: the 'herring spawning polygons we'd once prototyped' (Scott Veirs, #385) are not in any repo we hold — ask Peter/Scott where the prototype lives. Candidate: WDFW's Pacific herring spawning grounds GIS data. Check its licence against docs/rights-policy.md before shipping. Polygons, so the layer needs a fill style that doesn't read as a region mask, and should not be click-targets over sightings.

title: Any Postgres login role can make the database send HTTP requests, through pg_net's PUBLIC grants
description:
Supabase installs pg_net with USAGE on schema net, and every privilege on net.http_request_queue and net._http_response, granted to PUBLIC by supabase_admin. So any role that can log in can queue an HTTP request that the database itself sends: today the ingest role, and the read_path role added for the read-path build (decision 056). anon and authenticated hold it too, but can't reach the net schema through PostgREST.

We can't revoke it: supabase_admin owns these objects and made the grants. What we can do is keep login credentials scarce and on machines that need them, and pin the exposure so it can't widen unnoticed — supabase/read-path-grants.test.ts does that for read_path. It goes away when the database leaves Supabase (salish-9uu).

Found 2026-09-28 while pinning read_path's effective privileges.

title: pull-prod-db.sh fails against current production: auth and storage schemas have drifted from the local stack's
description:
Running scripts/pull-prod-db.sh on 2026-09-27 stops at the load step. Production's auth schema has tables the local stack's auth service doesn't (auth.mfa_recovery_code_sets, auth.mfa_recovery_codes) and columns it doesn't (auth.one_time_tokens.expires_at); storage.buckets has versioning_status, which the local one lacks. The local Supabase service images are older than production's. The script also still refreshes public.occurrence_index and public.occurrence_identifier_candidates, which decision 055 removed, so it would fail at the end even with the load fixed.

Found while mirroring production for the read-path build (salish-t3g.1). The workaround used there — a scratch copy that skips every auth-schema COPY block and any table missing locally — got the non-auth data in, but leaves the local database with no user accounts, so it isn't a fix. The likely fix is updating the local stack's service versions (supabase/.temp holds production's), then dropping the matview refreshes.

title: happywhale.individuals is varchar(100) in prod, varchar(50) from migrations
description: Found 2026-09-28 rehearsing salish-4h3's migration on a data-only dump of prod: primary_id and nickname are character varying(100) in production but (50) in a database built from migrations, so prod's rows don't load locally (e.g. nickname 'Sherwina (CA), Lonestar (BC) or Dreamer (Salish Sea)'). Someone widened them by hand. Write a migration that declares (100) — it needs the occurrences views' dependency handled (public.occurrences' happywhale branch reads both columns; since decision 055 that is derived.happywhale_occurrences) — so prod and local agree.

title: Record who applied each Orcasound tag (item_tags applier)
description: Decision 054 says a bout's identification row carries the application's certainty and, once item_tags are on the API, its applier. Since orcasite#1059 the bouts include exposes item_tags with attributes.user_id (an orcasite user UUID). salish-8vr.29 reads only certainty (fields[item_tag]=certainty). Open questions before reading it: what we would store (a UUID is meaningless to a reader; a moderator's display name is a people/rights question under docs/rights-policy.md), and whether public.identifications' asserting-authority fields can hold an upstream person at all. Not needed for the hedge to reach the map.

title: A reviewed-and-empty bout appears as acoustic activity once orcasite marks review complete
description:
Findings F6; decision 053 'why provisional' second bullet; decision 054 keeps 053 provisional on this point only.

A biophony bout with no animal tag is either 'reviewed and found empty' or 'not tagged yet', and only a moderator can say which. Today both are held in acoustic_bouts and shown nowhere (053). orcasite#1051 names a bout_review_completed event / reviewed_at on the snapshot and does not build it. When it exists: the ingest records it, and a reviewed-empty biophony bout appears on the map as acoustic activity with no animal named (an occurrence with zero identifications) rather than being held. Blocked upstream; nothing to do here until orcasite records the mark.

title: dwc-classification test assumes the register lacks beluga; 2026.09.5 added it
description: supabase/dwc-classification.test.ts:153 ('a taxon the register does not know keeps iNaturalist's lineage') uses Delphinapterus leucas as the taxon the register does not know, and asserts that precondition. Register edition 2026.09.5 minted SSA:0000953 Delphinapterus leucas, so the test fails for anyone with 2026.09.5 or later loaded locally (found 2026-09-22 with 2026.09.6). CI loads no register, so CI stays green and hides it. Fix: pick a taxon the register will not plausibly gain, or seed the fallback case instead of relying on the edition.

title: HappyWhale branch resolves a species by joining inaturalist.taxa on its scientific-name string
description: The last iNaturalist-as-dictionary join in public.occurrences, after salish-53t.3 (decisions 048/049): the happywhale branch LEFT JOINs inaturalist.taxa ON happywhale.species.scientific = taxa.scientific_name, then register.inaturalist_taxon_name. HappyWhale is not an iNaturalist source. HappyWhale ingest is OFF, so this touches only the stored mirror; low priority. When revisited: resolve happywhale.species through the register's names (scripts/register/name-index.ts, the Maplify pattern), or crosswalk HappyWhale's species ids in the register. 🤖

title: The keyset runaway-bound test is 3.2s against a 5s timeout, and flakes under load
description:
supabase/functions/ingest/fetch-inaturalist.test.ts 'throws when the sweep never terminates (runaway bound)' sweeps MAX_KEYSET_PAGES = 1000 pages of 200 records: 200,000 records through JSON.stringify, JSON.parse and Zod validation. Measured in isolation on 2026-09-18 it takes 3,221 ms against vitest's default 5,000 ms testTimeout — 36% headroom. Under full-suite parallelism it tips over: observed failing twice in a row and passing six other times in the same session, same code.

It is the only test in the suite anywhere near the limit, so a green run says nothing about the next one, and a CI failure here looks exactly like a real regression in the completeness invariant (decisions 011, 018) — which is the last place a flake should live.

Decision 044's isIngestable adds a bounded-extent check per record, so 200,000 cheap calls the test did not make before 2026-09-18; that nudges a test that was already close, it did not create the problem.

Options, none chosen: raise testTimeout for this file; give the sweep a seam so the test can assert the bound with a smaller MAX_KEYSET_PAGES; or shrink the page fixture, since what is under test is the bound and not the parsing. The third looks best — the test's subject is 'the loop refuses to run forever', and 200-record pages are incidental to that.
close_reason: Closed

title: The date-seek path has no test coverage
description:
salish-dy2's click-to-edit date readout (src/obs-panel.ts, shipped in PR #360) has no unit or e2e test. Four behaviours are load-bearing and all are silent if broken: the readout swaps in a focused input; change commits and reverts; Escape reverts and returns focus to the readout; blur reverts. The bounds guard in onSeekDate matters most — min/max only style an out-of-range value rather than refuse it, so the guard is the only thing stopping a typed 1985 date from walking the selection outside the range date-calendar will render, which is exactly how the day steppers once escaped it (see the comment on EARLIEST_OBSERVATION_DATE).

Cheap to cover: obs-panel is a Lit component and the repo already unit-tests components. Found while closing salish-dy2 as already-shipped.

title: Smoke can fail open against a cold Lambda@Edge right after deploy
description:
Deploy run 35378658781 (2026-09-18) went red on e2e/og-previews.spec.ts:137 — a bot UA on /individuals/0010193/T065A got the generic shell instead of T065A's profile meta. Passed on re-run with no change; five manual probes afterwards returned the profile meta in 0.2-0.55s.

Mechanism: the handler budgets its Supabase call as max(FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS - warmupMs, MIN_FETCH_BUDGET_MS) with FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=3000 (infra/lib/edge-handler/index.ts:39,117). Smoke runs immediately after the deploy replaces the distribution, so it can hit a cold replica whose warmup eats most of the 3s, leaving the floor; the lookup then times out and the handler fails open to the generic shell by design (decisions 015, 034).

Not the history backfill: the profile lookup queries individuals?entity_id=eq..., which never touches inaturalist.observations or maplify.sightings, and the backfill runs finished before 18:00 while smoke ran at 18:15.

Undecided: whether smoke should retry this probe, warm the edge before asserting, or be left to flake and be re-run by hand. Nobody has counted how often it happens — this is the first instance identified as a genuine smoke failure rather than a superseded run.

title: Map layer toggle for reference overlays (GH #453)
description: Public issue: https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/issues/453. Haul-out sites from public.haulouts (each linking to its page) and the herring spawning polygons, switchable. Desktop first; mobile layout is GH #67.

description: Decision 040 consequences: story text and radius tuning land via migration for now. Scott wants to write the Shilshole story and viewing guidance; that should not need a PR. Options: curator role UPDATE grant on haulouts + a tiny form on the page; or a sheet import like partners.csv. Decide when the first story is written.

Until then every page carries an 'unverified extraction' note. Also: reconcile the ~200 m NAD27→WGS84 offset if it turns out to matter for any site.
