title: The taxa refresh cannot record a replacement it does not already mirror
description:
Seven of the nine retired taxa in the mirror carry current_taxon_id = NULL even though
iNaturalist named a successor for each: 508823->508822, 520333->1651787, 531609->1661364,
1289590->1246814, 1368489->1672273, 1368490->1672272, 1368492->1664972. The refresh
reports each one every run ("replacement N is not mirrored; recorded as retired only").

WHY IT HAPPENS

inaturalist.taxa.current_taxon_id is a foreign key, and the mirror holds only taxa the
ingest closure has fetched. scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts therefore cannot record a
pointer to a taxon it does not hold, and it does not fetch one: pulling in a successor
drags in that successor's whole ancestor chain, which is the closure's job.

The ingest DOES follow current_taxon_id since salish-5ds, but only for a taxon entering
the mirror. These seven are already held, so nothing re-asks and nothing ever fetches
their successors.

WHY IT MATTERS LITTLE TODAY

Nothing references any of the seven (checked in prod 2026-08-29), and under decision 032 a
retirement with no replacement displays under its own name, which is the honest answer.
The cost shows up only if a record lands on one of them, and iNaturalist reassigns
observations to the successor when it retires a taxon, so that is unlikely.

OPTIONS IF IT IS EVER WORTH FIXING

- Let the refresh fetch a missing successor and insert it with its ancestor chain, which
  means giving the script a closure resolver (or importing resolveTaxonClosure).
- Have the refresh record the successor id in a nullable column with no FK, and resolve
  through it only when the target happens to be mirrored. Cheaper, but it splits "the
  replacement" across two columns.
- Leave it. The state is honest and reported on every run.

Related: decision 032, salish-5ds, migration 20260828000000.

title: Validate --plan-from JSON in scripts/backfill/maplify-taxa.ts
description:
PR #397 added parsePlan() to scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts so a plan file from `supabase db query --linked` is rejected unless every row has the expected types. The sibling script scripts/backfill/maplify-taxa.ts still does a bare JSON.parse and reads doc.current / doc.taxa unchecked.

Failure mode there is milder than the one #397 fixed: a taxon_id arriving as a JSON string makes `to !== row.taxon_id` true for a row that has not actually changed, so the emitted UPDATE carries rows that are no-ops (the statement's IS DISTINCT FROM guard saves it from writing anything wrong). A non-object root crashes at .map with an opaque message.

Apply the same treatment: validate the root shape and every field before resolving names or emitting SQL.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #406 (476be38).

title: Sentry init is PROD-gated on one entry point and not the other three
description:
`src/salish-sea.ts:31` guards `sentryClient.init()` with `import.meta.env.PROD`; `individual-page.ts:16`, `matriline-page.ts:15` and `ecotype-page.ts:15` call it unconditionally. So dev sessions on the profile pages already report to the production DSN, tagged `environment: development`.

Separately, `getCurrentScope().setClient(sentryClient)` in `src/sentry.ts` runs at import on every entry point, and the BrowserClient constructor builds its transport whenever a DSN is present. `init()` only installs integrations — so a direct `captureException` (as `receiveIdToken` now does, decision 030) transmits in dev regardless of the PROD guard.

Decide whether dev events are wanted at all, then make all four entry points agree. Either gate `setClient` on PROD, or drop the guard in salish-sea.ts and rely on the `environment` tag for filtering.

Found by adversarial review of PR #403.
notes: Merged in #422 (6e16a98) and deployed. Decision confirmed by the owner and recorded as docs/decisions/037-sentry-transmits-from-production-only.md (PR #423).
close_reason: Merged in #422. One initSentry() in sentry.ts that all four entry points call; gates the scope binding, not init(), since binding is what makes captureException transmit. sentryClient unexported. Chose not to send dev events (alternative was filtering on the environment tag) — stated as an assumption in the PR; reversing it is one line, and a decision record should follow if confirmed.

title: Symbology at historical density (029 open question, GH #31)
description:
Left open by decision 029. Everything measured for it covers 33-106 occurrences
in a day. The busiest day on record is 185, and the historical view (GH #31)
would exceed that by orders of magnitude.

Untested at that scale: whether layer-level declutter keeps up, whether the
labels degrade usefully (they drop rather than shrink), and whether 60+ segments
of travel line read as anything but a mesh.

The prototype's variant C ("Density" — no labels, radius by count, opacity by
age) exists on branch prototype/map-symbology and was built for exactly this
question. It is the obvious starting point rather than a fresh design.

title: What makes a track worth drawing? (029 open question)
description:
Left open by decision 029 and unchanged by its implementation.

A 2-point, sub-hour segment is a thin claim to render as a journey — the map
draws a line and an arrow, which asserts the animal travelled that way, from two
sightings that may be two people seeing the same whale from opposite shores. The
threshold probably wants 3+ points or a minimum distance.

Now more visible than when 029 was written, because the head label says
"Seen 2× in under an hour" out loud — the map is stating the weakness of its own
claim in words.

Relevant: imputeSegmentFrom already gates on 12h, 20km, and 3x the taxon's mean
travel speed (src/segments.ts). This is about what to DRAW, not what to chain.

title: Pooled matriline identifiers make the label too long for a phone
description:
Visible on production 2026-08-27, the first real day under decision 029:

  Biggs · T137A, T36, T36Bs, T137, T137Bs
  Seen 5× over 3h

The identity line pools identifiers across the whole segment (salish-ayb.6 /
#402), which is right — a matriline named in one sighting of an encounter and
not the next still names the track. But a 5-point Biggs encounter can name four
or five matrilines, and the line reaches ~45 characters. On a phone that is most
of the screen width, and it is the one label a reader most wants.

029 did not anticipate it: its worked example is "Gray whale · CRC53", one
identifier. The record's own worry was name length, and the register fixed that;
this is the same problem arriving from the other side.

Options, none decided:
  * Cap the list and count the rest — "T137A, T36 +3".
  * Drop to the matriline root — T137A/T137Bs/T137 are all T137s.
  * Let the second line carry them, since it already exists for multi-point
    tracks and is where "what happened" lives.

Do not simply un-pool them: the head would then name whichever matrilines the
LAST sighting happened to mention, which is worse and arbitrary.

title: maskLayer's zIndex works only because OpenLayers' sort sees NaN
description:
obs-map.ts gives maskLayer zIndex: 1 with a comment saying it belongs "above
the basemap, below the occurrences". Every other layer in the stack leaves
zIndex undefined.

OpenLayers sorts layer states with (a, b) => a.zIndex - b.zIndex
(ol/renderer/Composite.js). ol/layer/Base.js sets state.zIndex to the layer's
zIndex, which is `undefined` for a managed layer that was never given one. So
every comparison between the mask (1) and anything else is `1 - undefined` =
NaN, V8 treats a NaN comparator result as "equal", and the sort is a no-op.
Paint order is array order, which happens to be what the comment describes.

Taken literally, zIndex: 1 would put the mask ABOVE the occurrences and shade
the sightings it exists to distinguish from empty water — the opposite of GH
#16's intent.

Nothing is visibly wrong today. The hazard is that the next person to set an
explicit zIndex on any other layer turns the comparisons real and silently
reorders the map. Fix is to drop zIndex: 1 and rely on array order (the stack
is already ordered correctly), or give every layer an explicit zIndex.

Found while reordering the infrastructure layers for salish-fll.3.

title: Correct a false claim in migration 20260828110000: dwc DOES read public.occurrences
description:
The header of supabase/migrations/20260828110000_occurrences_register_names.sql says:

  "The DwC-A export emits no vernacularName and nothing in `dwc` reads this view, so the
   archive is unaffected."

The second clause is false. Four of the six dwc relations read public.occurrences:
_maplify_occurrences, _native_occurrences, datasets, occurrences.

The conclusion still holds — no dwc relation has a vernacular column, so the register
display-name change genuinely did not touch the archive — but the stated reason is wrong,
and it is the kind of claim someone will rely on. It nearly misled me an hour later while
sizing salish-a4y, where "does dwc read this view" is the difference between a display
tweak and a change to what we publish.

Found because I checked pg_get_viewdef on the dwc relations directly rather than trusting
a pg_depend query that had already missed two dependents earlier the same day.

Fix the comment in place; no behaviour change.

title: Restate DwC-A coverage once ingest scope is filtered
description:
The dwc schema reads public.occurrences (4 of its 6 relations), so filtering scope there
changes the published archive — roughly 17,620 Maplify records leave it.

That is defensible and arguably overdue: an archive under a Salish Sea remit should not be
publishing Californian humpbacks. But decision 027 and rights-policy §6.5 state coverage
deliberately, and verify-artifact's SC#4c gates the build on that prose, so the change has
to be reflected rather than discovered.

Check whether geographicCoverage in eml.xml states a bounding box, and whether it matches
the new scope. Re-run the GBIF validator afterwards.
notes:
Downgraded: no consumers of the export today, so this is follow-up rather than a gate on
the filter shipping.
close_reason: EML geographicDescription and rights-policy §6.5 restated in PR #419; bbox unchanged (orcas range-wide). GBIF validator NOT re-run — no consumers; rerun when someone consumes the export

title: Nothing re-asks iNaturalist about taxa we already hold
description:
Surfaced by salish-ayb.4, and broader than the deactivation problem it was filed under.

`resolveTaxonClosure` (supabase/functions/ingest/fetch-inaturalist.ts) diffs referenced
taxa against what we store and fetches only the MISSING ones. So a taxon row is written
once, at first sighting, and upstream is never asked about it again. `ON CONFLICT DO
NOTHING` in persist.ts is not the cause and changing it fixes nothing — the row is never
re-offered.

Consequences beyond deactivation:

  - vernacular_name never updates. iNaturalist renames common names; ours are frozen at
    whatever they were when the taxon first appeared. This matters directly for
    salish-ayb.5: the display name we are about to stop using comes from this column.
  - rank and parent_id likewise.
  - is_active and current_taxon_id (added 2026-08-28) can only be maintained by the
    v1-based refresh script, since the ingest's v2 endpoint omits inactive taxa entirely.

scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts refreshes deactivation status on demand. What is
missing is (a) something that runs it, and (b) extending it to the other mirror fields.

Options for (a): a scheduled GitHub Action like the animals crosswalk check, a pg_cron
job, or folding it into the nightly DwC-A build. A weekly cadence is plenty — nine
retirements accumulated over the mirror's whole lifetime.

Whatever runs it must not clobber is_active/current_taxon_id from a v2 response, which
cannot see them.
notes:
ALSO IN SCOPE (from the adversarial review of #396): the nightly ingest can revert a
repoint of inaturalist.observations.taxon_id. persist.ts upserts
'taxon_id = EXCLUDED.taxon_id WHERE EXCLUDED.updated_at > ...', so if upstream still
reports the retired id on a record whose updated_at advances (a comment, a fave, an edit),
the mirror flips back. The FK still passes, because the retired taxon remains mirrored.

Deeper point worth a decision rather than a quiet fix: that column is UPSTREAM's, unlike
maplify.sightings.taxon_id which we derive ourselves. Rewriting it is in tension with
decision 008's rule that source schemas are verbatim mirrors. The honest options are to
resolve retirements at read time in the occurrences view, to have the ingest itself follow
current_taxon_id when it writes, or to accept the mirror carrying a dead id and translate
downstream. Currently we do the third badly: a batch repair that upstream can undo.
close_reason:
Closed by #408 (read-time resolution, decision 032) and #409 (weekly refresh), both deployed 2026-08-29.

(a) Nothing re-asked about taxa we hold: .github/workflows/taxa-refresh.yml now runs scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts --apply Mondays 03:00 PT via the DwC-A nightly's session-pooler DSN (no new secret), files a taxa-refresh-failed issue, and puts the diff in the job summary. The script refreshes every mirrored field, not just status, and asks through the ingest's own taxaUrl/parseInatTaxa so the two cannot drift. First run (33267002050) fixed 13 stale prod rows: 8 vernacular names (41472 Inia geoffrensis read 'Boto', now 'Amazon River Dolphin') and 5 genera whose parent moved when iNaturalist inserted the seal tribes. DwC family/genus unchanged, 28345/28345 still populated.

(b) The taxon_id question, settled as decision 032: resolve on read, never rewrite. A stored id records what was claimed (upstream's, or a contributor's determination); public.occurrences and dwc.taxa_classification hop through current_taxon_id, hopping at every ancestor step in the classification because parent_id is the one link a repointing script refuses to touch. All repointing removed, so the revert risk in this issue's notes is gone by construction.

INCIDENT, worth knowing: teaching inaturalist.species_id() to resolve a retired parent turned a pure CASE into a function with a table read. A view checks referenced objects against its OWNER; a function BODY is checked against the CALLER, and anon lacks USAGE on the inaturalist schema, so every anonymous read of public.occurrences 42501'd. Smoke caught it, fixed in ~6 min with SECURITY DEFINER + empty search_path (migration 20260829040000). Testing via psql as postgres cannot see this; 'SET ROLE anon' reproduces it, and a test now does.

title: Travel lines: absent at default zoom, faint when present (GH #271)
description:
GH #271 reports travel lines as barely visible. Two separate causes found
during the symbology prototype:

1. ABSENT, not faint. `travelStyle` returns early when `resolution > 100`. At
   48N, zoom 10 is ~102 m/px and the app's default view is wider than that, so
   travel lines do not draw at all until the user zooms in past ~zoom 11. A
   user reporting "you can hardly see them" may be looking at a map where they
   are not rendered.
2. FAINT when they do draw. 2 px of #ffcc33 with no casing disappears into the
   Esri basemap's coastline. The prototype added a white casing stroke beneath
   the line, which is what actually makes it read.

Both belong in the symbology decision rather than being patched separately,
since how loud the line should be is inseparable from whether the segment is
the primary labelled object.

Public issue: https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/issues/271
close_reason: PR #401. Measured the default Salish Sea view at 489 m/px against the old resolution>100 gate — the lines were absent, not faint. Gate removed from the line, kept for the annotations (arrows, imputed present position). White casing under the 2px #ffcc33. Verified headless at res 489 and at zoom 13.

title: Occurrence markers and infrastructure markers read as the same visual class
description:
Hydrophones, viewing locations and salmon counting sites draw as circular
badges at roughly the same size as occurrence bubbles, so on the live map a
hydrophone reads as a sighting. Visible in any screenshot of the current map:
the circle-with-waves icons sit in the same visual register as the lettered
occurrence circles.

Whatever symbology lands, occurrences and infrastructure need to be
distinguishable classes — different shape, different weight, or different
saturation — not merely different glyphs inside the same circle.

Surfaced during the symbology prototype, 2026-08-27.
close_reason: PR #401. All three infrastructure icons move to a rounded-square plate and the viewing-location eye off #3399CC (the occurrence blue) onto the shared #1e2b76. Infrastructure layers moved below travel and occurrences. Shape was chosen over colour deliberately: it survives whatever palette 029's taxon colours land on. Filed salish-qfg for the maskLayer zIndex hazard found while reordering.

title: North Pacific Humpback never seeds a travel segment (missing travelSpeedKmH entry)
description:
`src/segments.ts` looks up `travelSpeedKmH[start.taxon.scientific_name]` by
exact match. `src/constants.ts` has six entries and
`Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira` is not one of them, so 319 occurrences of North
Pacific Humpback Whale can never START a segment, while plain
`Megaptera novaeangliae` (17,933 records) can.

Decision 027 records that the empty entries in that table are intent, not
oversight — pinnipeds and otters are excluded deliberately. This is different:
the subspecies of an included species is excluded by accident of exact-string
matching.

Check the same class of bug for other subspecies present in the corpus:
Orcinus orca ater and rectipinnus ARE listed; Phocoena phocoena vomerina and
Phoca vitulina richardii are not, though those taxa are excluded on purpose
anyway.

Fix is either a table entry or matching on species_id, which segments.ts
already uses for the candidate comparison one line later.
close_reason: PR #401. travelSpeedFor() falls back trinomial -> binomial; reaches Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira (342 prod records) and Balaenoptera acutorostrata scammoni (2), leaves 027's deliberate omissions omitted at every rank, and lets an explicit subspecies key still win. Prod confirmed species_id is shared across subspecies (41566 humpbacks, 41521 orcas), so only the seed lookup was failing.

title: Emit coordinateUncertaintyInMeters: what the accuracy audit means for the export
description:
Context for salish-6dy, from the symbology accuracy audit (2026-08-27).

`accuracy` on public.occurrences is NULL for maplify (34,791) and direct (438),
carries three discrete coordinate-precision values for happywhale (2/16/161 m),
and for iNaturalist ranges p50 31 m to a max of 7,313 km across 16,410 of
20,581 records.

Two consequences for the DwC-A:
  - SRC-01 excludes iNaturalist and HappyWhale, which are the only providers
    with any value at all. So the exported archive would emit
    coordinateUncertaintyInMeters on approximately zero records. Worth
    confirming before building the field.
  - Where a value does exist it describes reporter position, not animal
    position, which is not what coordinateUncertaintyInMeters means for an
    occurrence record. Emitting it unqualified would overstate precision to
    GBIF consumers.

Relates to salish-6dy. Filed separately so the audit is not lost in it.

title: Short-form map labels: our presentation layer over the register's names
description:
ADR-0011 is explicit that this is ours: `label` is "input to display, not
display", and the register "cannot know whether a consumer needs a dropdown
entry, a map pin, a sentence fragment, a chart axis, or twenty characters on a
phone". Truncation and capitalisation are named as consumer concerns.

So a map pin saying "Humpback" rather than "Humpback whale" is legitimate, and
is a DIFFERENT change from adopting "River otter" over "North American River
Otter" — the latter is fixing a wrong name (the register's job), the former is
composing a short form (ours).

It is not a general rule. "Humpback whale" -> "Humpback" works because the
modifier is a noun; "Gray whale" -> "Gray" does not. So it is a curated short
form per taxon, keyed by SSA identifier, living in this repo as presentation
config — not as another name row, and never by writing back into the register.

Longest names currently reaching the map, for sizing the work:
  Eastern Pacific Long-beaked Common Dolphin  42 chars
  North Pacific Humpback Whale                28
  Pacific White-sided Dolphin                 27
  North American River Otter                  26
  Resident Killer Whale                       21   (4,115 records)

Blocked on the materialization issue: there is no SSA identifier to key on
until occurrences resolve to register entities.
close_reason:
PR #402. Short forms keyed on the register's SSA identifier, carried onto taxon by migration 20260829000000; shipped with decision 029's implementation because the map had nowhere to render a short form until it existed.

Only FIVE entries were needed — Humpback, White-sided dolphin, Elephant seal, Bottlenose dolphin, Right whale dolphin. The issue sized this against iNaturalist's names (42, 28, 27, 26 chars); adopting the register in ayb.5 already fixed those, and most register names are the right length for a map pin.

The rule that came out of it: short forms are TRUNCATIONS, never substitutions, and never lifted from a 'hidden' register name. The register carries orca / humpback / elephant seal / bottlenose dolphin / right whale dolphin as hidden rows — evidence a string is in use, explicitly not one it offers for display. So an unattributed killer whale reads 'Killer whale', not 'Orca'. Recorded in 029's Implementation notes.

title: animals: add birder alpha codes OSPR, HOSP, UNBI
description:
Filed salish-sea/animals#25 on 2026-08-14. Verified against the IBP alpha code list by extracting the PDF, not from memory.

Add as hidden names under a new IBP source (authority, not use — unlike ORCASOUND, which only claims a name is in use):
- SSA:0000907 Aves -> UNBI ("Unidentified Bird", Aves (gen, sp) — rank matches exactly)
- SSA:0000910 Pandion haliaetus -> OSPR
- SSA:0000911 Passer domesticus -> HOSP

SSA:0000909 Cepphus columba already has PIGU; the list confirms it.

DO NOT add UNLG to SSA:0000908 Laridae. UNLG is "Unidentified Larus Gull" — Larus is a GENUS, Laridae is a FAMILY that also holds terns and kittiwakes. Attaching it narrows the entity through a name, passes validation, and is the ADR-0019 guarantee's failure mode arriving by a route the guarantee does not cover (a curator adding a name at the wrong rank, not a fold collision). Recorded in the issue so it is not "fixed" later.

Open: license status for the IBP source needs deciding rather than assuming cleared. Six-letter scientific codes (PANHAL, PASDOM, AVEGSP, CEPCOL) exist as a second system; not proposed, no evidence of use.

Low value until OrcaHello's tag corpus is actually read — its api/tags endpoint is [AllowAnonymous] but the host is unknown.
notes: UPDATE 2026-08-19: 'kier' was a typo for 'keir', fixed in orcahello#573 — the earlier IBP search only ruled out KI__ codes, not KE__. dthaler says KEIR and PIGU are both 4-letter birder codes (the system Dave Bain uses for birds). Before the register carries KEIR: verify it against the IBP alpha code list and identify the species — if it checks out, extend animals#25 to add it the same way as PIGU/OSPR/HOSP/UNBI. Tracked in salish-8vr.23.
close_reason: Already done and never closed: salish-sea/animals#26 ('Three birder alpha codes, and one that must never be added') merged 2026-08-28. Verified 2026-09-20 -- OSPR, HOSP and UNBI are all present as names in data/names.tsv on animals main.

title: orcasite: JSON:API include emits type: null for tags
description: Filed orcasound/orcasite#1011 2026-08-13. Tag and ItemTag lack the AshJsonApi.Resource extension and a json_api type block, so included tags serialize with type: null; feed, which has both, is correct. Blocks nothing on our side — we can key on the relationship name — but a typed include is what lets a generic JSON:API client walk the graph. Watch for a fix; no work here.
close_reason: Fixed upstream and deployed to staging 2026-08-14; orcasound/orcasite#1011 closed as completed.

title: Upload the branded social preview to GitHub repo settings
description: GitHub exposes no REST or GraphQL endpoint for a repository's social preview image, so docs/branding/github-social-preview.png (1280x640, built by scripts/branding/build-icons.sh) has to be uploaded by hand at Settings -> General -> Social preview. Until then the repo card is GitHub's auto-generated tile. Blocked on PR #390 landing the file. Repeat this after any brand change: the build regenerates the file, but GitHub keeps serving the last upload.

title: Backfill ORCIDs for existing iNaturalist contributors
description:
20260621010000_inat_orcid_capture.sql is forward-only by construction: it says so plainly — the 3,072 existing iNat contributor rows are not backfilled because inaturalist.observations does not retain the raw user JSON and the upsert's WHEN MATCHED branch does not re-mint (D-16). So re-ingest will never cover them; only contributors who post a NEW observation get an ORCID.

Needs a one-time pass over the iNat users API keyed on contributors.inat_login, writing through a path that respects the new canonical-URI CHECK.

Note this does not by itself put an ORCID in the archive: iNat records are excluded by SRC-01, and iNat contributor rows are separate from native ones. Its value is the register of identities, plus whatever cross-provider resolution later does with it.
acceptance_criteria: Existing iNat contributors with a linked ORCID have it stored; the pass is idempotent and re-runnable.

title: Validate the contributors_orcid_is_canonical_uri constraint
description:
The CHECK added in 20260813200000_dwc_recorded_by_id.sql is NOT VALID: it governs new writes but never audited the ~3,000 existing iNat-sourced rows. Deliberate — a constraint failure there would have failed the deploy carrying it, since the deploy job runs supabase db push before flipping the frontend.

Audit and finish it: SELECT count(*) FROM public.contributors WHERE orcid IS NOT NULL AND orcid !~ '^https://orcid\\.org/[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{3}[0-9X]$'; then either ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT (if clean) or normalise the offenders first. Run against prod, not just local — the iNat rows are a prod-only population.
acceptance_criteria: Constraint is VALIDATED in prod, or the non-conforming rows are documented and normalised.
notes:
Pre-audited 2026-08-13 before deployment: all 46 non-NULL prod orcid values were run through public.is_valid_orcid and passed both shape and ISO 7064 check digit, predicting a clean validation.

Closed legitimately the same day: ALTER TABLE public.contributors VALIDATE CONSTRAINT was actually run against prod after a43d8a5 deployed the constraint, and pg_constraint.convalidated is now true — the whole existing population scanned and passed, as predicted.

An earlier close reason on this issue wrongly implied deployment alone finished it. Deploying a NOT VALID constraint does not validate it; that is a separate statement.
close_reason: Pre-empted: the constraint and public.is_valid_orcid deployed to prod with a43d8a5, and the audit run beforehand showed all 46 prod ORCIDs pass shape and check digit. Reopen only if VALIDATE CONSTRAINT is later found not to have been run — see the note below.

title: Haul-out clustering for pinnipeds (GH #385)
description:
Spatial aggregation of repeated pinniped sightings at fixed haul-out sites — the pinniped-shaped analogue of a travel segment. Public issue: https://github.com/salish-sea/salishsea-io/issues/385

Context: travel segments are species-gated by design (decision 027) because pinnipeds are too numerous and not individually identifiable for a travel chain to mean anything. Haul-out clustering is the pattern that DOES apply: seals return to fixed sites, so repeated sightings are evidence about a place, not a journey. ~13,800 pinniped + ~1,600 otter occurrences currently aggregate into nothing.

Design questions are open — see the GitHub issue. A harbor-seal catalog with photo-ID would separately make the taxon eligible for real segments; that is not this work.
notes: Reframed by decision 040 (2026-09-11): sites are a held list seeded from the atlas; clustering's job is now to PROPOSE sites the list lacks and flag listed sites with no reports. Depends on the epic salish-4pr landing first.

title: guard.test.ts row-floor test is vacuous in CI and fails locally
description:
scripts/dwca/guard.test.ts:203 sets process.env.ROW_FLOOR='9999999999' inside the test body, but scripts/dwca/guard.ts:41 evaluates ROW_FLOOR at module import time (`const ROW_FLOOR = BigInt(process.env['ROW_FLOOR'] ?? 1000)`). The override therefore never takes effect and the guard runs against the default floor of 1000.

In CI the test still passes, but for the wrong reason: supabase/ci-seed.sql seeds only a handful of occurrences, so the real row count is already below the default floor. The assertion never exercises what it claims to. On a developer machine with a realistically populated local dwc schema (27,391 rows here) the guard does not trip and the test fails.

Found while verifying the pnpm migration (salish-w3y) — NOT caused by it; reproduces identically under npm.
design: Options: (a) inject the floors as parameters/an options object into main() rather than reading module-level env, which is the honest fix and makes the other floor tests non-vacuous too; (b) vi.resetModules() + dynamic re-import after setting env; (c) vi.stubEnv before import. (a) is preferred — the same import-time-const pattern applies to ZIP_FLOOR_BYTES and PARQUET_FLOOR_BYTES, whose tests only pass because they mock fs.stat rather than needing an env override.
acceptance_criteria: The row-floor test fails if the guard's row check is removed (mutation-tested), and passes against both a seeded CI database and a fully populated local one.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #375 (754c4e9), merged 2026-08-04. main() now takes injectable GuardFloors defaulting to floorsFromEnv(), evaluated per call rather than at import. Also rejects floors that would disable the guard (Number('')===0 from an unset workflow var would have silently passed an empty archive) and stops the nightly's failure issue misreporting a config rejection as 'failed before guard.ts could run'. 356 -> 378 tests; mutation-tested with no DSN set, where the old suite caught nothing. Reviewed by CodeRabbit (CLI x3 + PR-side) and an independent Fable pass; each layer found a distinct instance of the same underlying flaw (coverage that only looks real because ambient values line up).

title: Reconcile the two remaining prod/migration drifts and drop the pull-prod-db.sh workarounds
description:
Two schema drifts found in the salish-0ew sweep (2026-07-30) were recorded but never fixed or explicitly accepted. Both are still worked around in scripts/pull-prod-db.sh, so a prod mirror succeeds while the underlying drift persists.

1. **happywhale.encounter_sample exists only in prod.** One `id integer` column, 5,610 rows, referenced nowhere in the repo — an ad-hoc sampling leftover. Either drop it in prod or add a migration. pull-prod-db.sh excludes it (`-x happywhale.encounter_sample`, line 94).

2. **happywhale.individuals.primary_id and .nickname are varchar(100) in prod; migrations declare varchar(50).** Only nickname needs the width (2 rows over 50 chars, max 60); primary_id maxes at 28. pull-prod-db.sh widens nickname locally so the load succeeds (line 116).

Note for (2): public.occurrences depends on primary_id, so widening it in a migration means dropping and recreating the view — bare ALTER TABLE fails with 'cannot alter type of a column used by a view or rule'.
acceptance_criteria: Each drift is either reconciled by a migration or recorded as explicitly accepted with a reason. A fresh `supabase db reset` and prod agree on both points. The corresponding workarounds in scripts/pull-prod-db.sh (the -x exclusion and the nickname ALTER) are deleted, since their comments already say they should go when the drift is reconciled.
notes: This is acceptance criterion 4 of salish-0ew, which was closed with criteria 1 and 2 met. The grant-replay step in pull-prod-db.sh is deliberately NOT part of this — it is kept as a guard against future out-of-band grant drift.

title: Retire or replace the last in-DB HTTP functions (HappyWhale)
description:
Three in-database functions still make live HTTP calls from Postgres:

- `happywhale.fetch_species_config`
- `happywhale.ensure_species`
- `happywhale.ensure_inat_taxa`

They are the last of the pattern decision 011 set out to remove — Postgres keeps storage and pure relational views, ingest lives in a TypeScript imperative shell.

## Why they were left behind

Migration `20260731120000` retired the equivalent Maplify and iNaturalist functions (salish-89d.3). These were deliberately not included, because HappyWhale was **never part of that cutover**:

- `ingest.runs` has no `happywhale` rows at all — 7,053 iNaturalist runs and 7,091 Maplify runs, zero HappyWhale.
- No cron job has ever scheduled them.
- There is no TypeScript replacement to move the work to.

So dropping them would remove the only mechanism, dormant as it is, with nothing standing behind it. That is a different decision from retiring a path that has a proven replacement running in production, and it belongs in its own change.

Prod does hold HappyWhale data (~5,600 encounters, ~176 kB of individuals), so it was populated at some point — presumably by hand. Whether that data is still wanted, and whether it should be refreshed at all, is the actual question here.

## What to decide first

1. **Is HappyWhale still a source we want?** Check `docs/data-provenance.md` and the rights position before building anything. If the answer is no, this is a deletion, not a migration.
2. If yes, port the fetch into `supabase/functions/ingest` alongside `fetch-maplify.ts` and `fetch-inaturalist.ts`, give it an `ingest.runs` source, and only then drop the three functions.
3. Either way, `supabase/seed.sql` no longer calls `fetch_species_config` — nothing depends on these today.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision is recorded on whether HappyWhale remains a source.
- If retained: the fetch lives in supabase/functions/ingest, writes an ingest.runs row, and is scheduled the same way Maplify and iNaturalist are.
- The three happywhale.* HTTP functions are dropped in a migration.
- No function in any schema makes an outbound HTTP call from Postgres.

title: Integrate Flukebook (Wildbook) for computer-vision individual identification
description:
WHY: Photo-ID by eye doesn't scale. Flukebook — the Wildbook-based CV photo-ID platform for whales/dolphins — can match a sighting's photos to known individuals automatically, turning every photographed occurrence into a candidate identification. A differentiating, 'killer' feature.

WHAT: Submit occurrence photos to Flukebook's matching API; receive ranked candidate individual matches with confidence scores; record them as candidate Identifications against public.individuals. Flukebook individual IDs map to our catalog as an external-catalog link (alongside HappyWhale). CV match scores are a natural input to the validation model (salish-ek3): high-confidence matches may auto-validate, others stay candidate for human review.

SPIKE / OPEN QUESTIONS (resolve before build):
- Wildbook/Flukebook API capabilities: species coverage (SRKW, Bigg's/transients, humpback), submission + async match-result model, auth, rate/cost.
- Two-way? Whether we also contribute photos/encounters back to Flukebook.
- Cross-catalog dedup: HappyWhale is already mirrored; avoid representing the same animal as two unlinked catalog individuals.

DEPENDS ON the individuals catalog; produces candidate Identifications that feed the identification + validation model.
design:
Two viable architectures (research: docs/research/flukebook-wildbook-api.md):
(A) Contribute INTO hosted Flukebook — request a free account, push encounters/photos via web submit or spreadsheet Bulk Import, let Flukebook's pipeline match, read results back via the login-gated read-only /rest/ query API (what RWildbook wraps). No public 'POST photo → poll for match JSON' endpoint exists on flukebook.org; write access + results at that level need a data-sharing conversation with Wild Me / Conservation X Labs. Data model: 'all data rights remain with contributor' (no CC auto-licensing).
(B) Self-host Wildbook + WBIA (both AGPL) and call WBIA's async job engine directly (/api/engine/query/..., jobid + poll/callback). Full CV control; ops + infra cost.
Either way the match model is async (queue/poll), never request/response.
acceptance_criteria: Photographed occurrences receive ranked candidate individual matches from Flukebook, recorded as candidate identifications with source + confidence score, mapped to public.individuals via a Flukebook external-catalog link.
notes: PARKED 2026-07-03: research complete (docs/research/flukebook-wildbook-api.md), but actual integration is significant product work — not being pursued now. Dominant next action when picked up is a single Wild Me / CXL conversation (orca accuracy + v4 access/licensing + integration path); a draft outreach exists in session history. Deprioritized P2→P3 to match the rest of the individuals epic as unscheduled future work.

title: Define validation model for individual identifications
description: WHY: Identifications differ in trust — a sighter's tag, a regex-extracted candidate (T065S), and a HappyWhale-confirmed match are not equivalent. Per docs/rights-policy.md only validated identities may be emitted as organismID. WHAT: Design the validation/confidence model over identification links (states, who/what validates, provenance of the assertion). Orthogonal to the catalog and linking mechanics — plenty to discuss. Gates organismID emission (salish-1bb).
acceptance_criteria: A documented validation model distinguishing validated from candidate identifications, sufficient to gate organismID emission.

title: Identify individuals in upstream records
description: WHY: Most volume comes through upstream sources; we want their records associated with catalog individuals too. WHAT: Resolve the two upstream inputs against public.individuals — (a) public.extract_identifiers candidate codes parsed from Maplify/native comment text, and (b) happywhale.encounters.individual_id (already a confirmed upstream match). Produce identification links for upstream occurrences. Per decision 008, resolution translates upstream signals into our catalog; it does not adopt the mirror as authoritative. Validation status is handled separately.
acceptance_criteria: Upstream occurrences (maplify/inaturalist/happywhale) carry identification links to catalog individuals where a resolvable identifier or HappyWhale match exists.

title: Identify individuals in our own observations
description: WHY: Native sighters/editors should be able to say which catalog individual(s) an observation records — the primary way our own high-quality identifications enter the system. WHAT: An identification link between a native occurrence (public.observations) and one or more public.individuals, plus the editor UI to set it. Depends on the individuals catalog.
acceptance_criteria: A native observation can be linked to one or more catalog individuals via the editor; the link is queryable on the occurrence.

title: Decode un-identified Maplify acronym collection stubs
description:
public.collections has 11 stub rows seeded from raw Maplify [Tag] bracket codes with kind=NULL and organization_id=NULL (reference_tables migration, 'Acronym stubs (D-06)'). Each is an unidentified data source representing pending work: decode what real-world channel/org each acronym names, then set kind + organization_id (and correct the display name), or remove it. Note: these raw upstream bracket tags sitting half-resolved in an authoritative table are a mild violation of the anti-corruption boundary in decision 008 — resolving them also cleans that up.

Stubs to decode: psws, mcw, cww, wssji, hiws, sbw, wa, ssch, sa, psww, bremerton-fb.

Known so far:
- psws = Puget Sound Whale Sightings (Facebook group): https://www.facebook.com/groups/pugetsoundwhalesightings (kind=facebook_group)
- bremerton-fb = appears to be a Bremerton-area Facebook group (confirm).
acceptance_criteria: Each acronym stub is either resolved (name/kind/organization_id filled) or removed; no NULL-kind collection rows remain from raw Maplify bracket tags.

title: Ingest pinniped/mustelid occurrences from GBIF
description: Second source toward full PSEMP Marine Mammal Working Group taxonomic scope. GBIF carries in-region pinniped and mustelid occurrence records not covered by iNaturalist. Overlaps with the planned inbound-GBIF-ingest direction (mirror-image of SRC-01) — must not re-import SalishSea.io's own contributions back from GBIF. See PRODUCT.md Future directions.

close_reason: Premise was false. iNaturalist taxon 372843 (which I mis-identified as 'a second cetacean taxon') is Phocoidea = ALL pinnipeds; it's already in inaturalist.update_observations. Prod carries thousands of pinniped records (2,152 California sea lions, 1,827 harbor seals, 531 Steller sea lions, etc., 2026-07-03). No downstream cetacean-only filter. Pinnipeds are ingested + surfaced today — not a gap. Broader GBIF ingest remains captured by the existing 'inbound GBIF records' future direction.

description: Platform links out to existing external cetacean resources and databases.

title: Emit organismID and register archive with GBIF/OBIS
description: Occurrence records carry individual-animal identity (organismID); register the DwC-A with GBIF/OBIS. Note: unvalidated whale IDs (e.g. T065S) are never emitted as organismID per docs/rights-policy.md — only validated identities qualify.

title: Model an authoritative catalog of individual whales (public.individuals)
description:
WHY: We want our own domain concept of an individual animal — distinct from the happywhale.individuals upstream mirror and from the regex-extracted text identifiers (public.extract_identifiers). Per decision 008 those are INPUTS, not our catalog; their vocabulary must not become our domain.

WHAT: An authoritative public.individuals catalog: stable designation (e.g. T065A), aliases, species, matriline/pod (for SRKW), and links to external catalogs (HappyWhale individual id, etc.). This is the foundation the identification work and organismID emission build on.

Inputs to reconcile into the catalog: happywhale.individuals (~693 mirrored) and public.extract_identifiers output (unvalidated candidate codes like T065S). Validation of identifications is tracked separately (orthogonal).
acceptance_criteria: public.individuals table exists with our own authoritative identity model; HappyWhale mirror and extracted identifiers are reconcilable inputs, not the source of truth.
notes: Schema landed in PR #317 (catalog/biggs-schema-seed): public.individuals/social_groups/designations/nicknames/group_memberships/parties. Awaiting CodeRabbit + merge. Deferred: validation-trust model (ek3), CV (z5m), the observation bridge.

Fresh question per partner: do they forward observer names / stable IDs for recordedByID? Trigger: partner confirms API access, or product wants to retire Maplify.

title: Cross-provider contributor unification (contributor_links)
description:
jmaughn (iNat) ≈ James Maughn (native) is probable, not confirmed. Extension point is a contributor_links table — never a shared FK on name similarity (docs/decisions/006).

Why it now has a consumer (2026-08-13): the archive emits recordedByID from contributors.orcid (PR #389), and 'source the ORCID from iNaturalist where possible' is the stated preference. But the ORCIDs we hold sit on iNat contributor rows, the archive exports native rows, and nothing joins the two — so that sourcing is a curation habit rather than machinery until this lands. inat_login cannot serve: it is a dedup key for iNat rows only (D-15, native rows leave it NULL) and it is UNIQUE, so a native row cannot be tagged with a login an iNat row already holds. contributors.entity_id (uuid, currently unused) may be the intended hook.

An ORCID that both records carry is also the strongest available link evidence — better than name similarity, which decision 006 rules out.
design:
Findings from reading the live schema (2026-08-13, verified against prod). These are constraints any design must survive, not a proposal.

SCALE — the merge set is tiny. 6,452 contributors: 6,420 carry inat_login, and only 9 have any native observations. maplify.sightings.contributor_id and happywhale.encounters.contributor_id exist but link ZERO rows, so 'cross-provider' today means exactly native<->iNat. Matching ~9 people against 6,420 logins is curator work, not automated resolution.

TRAP 1 — observations.contributor_id is ON DELETE CASCADE. A 'repoint then delete the loser' merge silently DELETES any observation it failed to repoint. Those are the exported records (occurrenceID salishsea:<id>), so they vanish from an archive GBIF has already ingested. The failure mode is backwards: the iNat/Maplify/HappyWhale FKs are ON DELETE NO ACTION and would abort loudly; the one table holding our own occurrences fails quietly. contributor_email_addresses and user_contributor are also CASCADE.

TRAP 2 — a delete-based merge undoes itself. inaturalist.mint_contributor is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (inat_login) DO UPDATE. Delete the iNat row and the next observation from that user re-creates it under a NEW id; the duplicate returns and any link recorded against the old id dangles. This is the mechanical reason decision 006's contributor_links shape is right — it is the only form that survives ingest. Never delete a contributor row.

TRAP 3 — merging rewrites published attribution. dwc recordedBy is c.name read at view time, so the survivor's name propagates to every already-published record on the next nightly, with occurrenceID unchanged: same records, different observer. Choose the survivor for name quality, not row age — if Scott's iNat row won, 374 archive records would start reading 'scottveirs' instead of 'Scott Veirs'. This is also the mechanism that makes merging worth doing: it is how an iNat-sourced ORCID reaches native records without hand-curation (see salish-pj6, where 374 records needed a manual write for an ORCID the database already held on the sibling row).

EDGES — inat_login is UNIQUE, so moving it to the survivor requires nulling/deleting the loser first; ordering matters inside the transaction. public.contributors has only a SELECT policy, so a merge needs SECURITY DEFINER (precedent: mint_contributor, create_contributor_on_sign_in) — an app-level UPDATE cannot do it. No matviews reference contributors, so nothing needs refreshing.

OPEN — is 'one ORCID, one contributor' an invariant? There is no UNIQUE on contributors.orcid today. If we deliberately let both of a person's rows carry the same ORCID, that constraint can never be added later. Decide before backfilling (salish-rtz).

CORRECTION — this issue previously guessed contributors.entity_id was the intended hook. It is referenced NOWHERE: not in src/, not in any view, not in any migration after the one that defines it. It is an unused column with a gen_random_uuid() default, not a designed seam. Deciding what it means is prerequisite to building on it.

DIRECTION implied by the above: a contributor_links table asserting 'these rows are the same person', with an explicit preferred/display row; the export joins through the link rather than the row; ORCID is the evidence, never name similarity (decision 006).

title: URL → whole-occurrence importer (source_url Layer 2)
description: Given a source_url, fetch and map a whole occurrence (species/date/location/photos/observer), not just resolve its channel. One fetcher per provider domain; reuse the URL registry; dedupe on source_url; respect SRC-01. Trigger: appetite for a new inbound ingest path.

title: Populate contributor ORCIDs for 28 native contributors
description:
contributors.orcid column shipped in v1.3; the recordedByID emit did NOT — an earlier version of this issue and PRODUCT.md both claimed it had. It landed 2026-08-13 as occurrence column 26 (PR #389), verified end to end against the local stack.

What remains is the data: all 28 native contributors have a NULL orcid, so the archive emits recordedByID on 0 of 27,391 rows. Curation is the path — where a contributor has an ORCID linked on their iNaturalist profile, take that; otherwise ask or leave NULL. Never guess from a name.

Values must be the full https://orcid.org/XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX URI; the CHECK constraint added with the emit rejects anything else.
notes:
Started 2026-08-13: Peter Abrahamsen (id 6) and Scott Veirs (id 7) set in prod, from ORCIDs verified twice — against the ORCiD public API (names match) and against their iNaturalist profiles, which carry the identical canonical URIs.

Live in prod as of 2026-08-13: dwc.occurrences has 27 columns, and 374 native observations (all Scott's) resolve to a contributor with an ORCID, so the next nightly DwC-A build emits recordedByID on those records.

Prod holds 46 ORCIDs in total, but 44 sit on iNat contributor rows with no native observations, so they export nothing (SRC-01). Remaining work is the other native contributors, still NULL.

Note the two-rows-per-person shape: 'rainhead' (id 37) and 'scottveirs' (id 1990) are the same two humans' iNat rows — id 1990 already carries the ORCID, id 37 does not. That duplication is salish-8fm.

title: Generate the Bigg's catalogue rows from the register too, once nothing in them is ours alone
description: Decision 070: the Bigg's rows follow the Southern Residents' when ready. Ready means each fact only our checked-in copy holds has moved: parentage and superseded/alternate designations (T046A, CA/AO codes) upstream to the register; the matriarch read from register.matriarch (salish-o3gx); nicknames' status/namer/year kept as checked-in data keyed by register identifier. Then generate individuals, designations and social groups for Bigg's the way 070 does for J/K/L and retire data/catalogue's copies. Not scheduled.

title: Scripts' entrypoint check fails in a checkout path with a space or #
description: 17 scripts under scripts/ (backup, dwca, ingest, read-path) decide whether they were run directly with `import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}``. import.meta.url percent-encodes a space or # in the path and the interpolation doesn't, so in such a checkout the script exits without running main(). No real checkout hits it today (/app on Fly, ~/dev locally, CI's workspace). Fix all at once: a shared isMain(import.meta.url) helper comparing against pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href. Raised by CodeRabbit on scripts/read-path/profile-index.ts during salish-t3g.7.5.

title: Decide whether the taxa refresh still needs --plan-from/--emit-sql
description:
scripts/backfill/inat-taxa-status.ts keeps a second route to production: --plan-from reads
the mirror from a JSON plan so no database connection is needed, and --emit-sql prints the
statements for `supabase db query --linked`. Added in #397 because "production has no
direct connection from a laptop".

.github/workflows/taxa-refresh.yml removed that constraint. It has a connection, runs
weekly, and takes workflow_dispatch for an off-cycle run.

So the pair is now a manual fallback rather than the only route, and it costs: parsePlan
validates seven columns, --emit-sql renders the same UPDATE a second time in string form,
and both have to be extended whenever a mirrored column is added. That second rendering is
exactly the drift #397's repointSql() was careful to avoid elsewhere.

Kept for now rather than deleted a day after it merged, and because a laptop route is
genuinely useful when the workflow itself is what is broken.

Decide: keep (and accept maintaining both paths), or delete and rely on workflow_dispatch.
If deleting, check first whether anyone has used --emit-sql since 2026-08-28.
